His first major title came on November 6, 1983, when he won the Mexican National Lightweight Championship.

After moving up to the welterweight division, he captured the Mexican National Welterweight Championship in 1985. Later, he became a two-time NWA World Welterweight Champion, defeating Solar II in 1988 and holding the title for an impressive 808-day reign. During this time, he also worked part-time for the World Wrestling Association (WWA), winning their welterweight title twice.

One of his most notable rivalries was with Octagón, leading to several high-profile *Luchas de Apuesta* (bet matches) where their masks were on the line. In 1992, he became the first CMLL World Welterweight Champion, though he lost the title just 22 days later.

Fuerza Guerrera left EMLL in 1992 when Antonio Peña founded Asistencia Asesoría y Administración (AAA). He continued his feud with Octagón in AAA, where he and his son, Juventud Guerrera, formed a successful tag team known as *Los Guerreras*. Together, they won multiple championships, including the Mexican National Tag Team Championship and the WWA Tag Team Championship. Fuerza also briefly held the IWC World Middleweight Championship.

In the late 1990s, he had a brief stint with the WWF, teaming with Jerry Estrada and Heavy Metal in a match at the 1997 Royal Rumble. He later returned to CMLL, winning the CMLL World Trios Championship in 2002 with Blue Panther and Dr. Wagner Jr. before rejoining AAA.

In 2007, Fuerza Guerrera had a dramatic storyline where he faced his son, Juventud Guerrera, in a Street Fight at Triplemanía XV, which Juventud won. His final major match for AAA came in 2007, after which he transitioned to working with International Wrestling Revolution Group (IWRG). He won the IWRG Intercontinental Welterweight Championship twice, holding it for over 500 days in one reign.

Outside the ring, Fuerza Guerrera has faced personal challenges, including a strained relationship with his son, Juventud, since the 1990s. In 2018, he introduced two more children—Fuerza Guerrera Jr. and Fuerza Guerrera (his daughter)—as professional wrestlers. He is also the uncle of the late Furia Guerrera, who was tragically murdered in 2009.

Throughout his career, Fuerza Guerrera has held numerous titles across major Mexican promotions, including AAA, CMLL, and IWRG. He remains a respected figure in *lucha libre*, known for his longevity, skill, and contributions to the sport. Despite his advanced age, he continues to wrestle, and there has been speculation about a potential *Luchas de Apuesta* match with his longtime rival, Octagón, before their retirements.

title: Michael Folorunsho
text:
Michael Ijemuan Folorunsho is an Italian professional footballer born on 7 February 1998, who plays as a midfielder. He currently represents Serie A club Cagliari on loan from Napoli and has also played for the Italy national team. Folorunsho began his career in the youth system of Lazio, where he played for their Under-19 squad. In July 2017, he signed with Serie C club Virtus Francavilla, making his professional debut on 26 August 2017 in a match against Lecce. Over the next two seasons, he played 60 games in Serie C for Virtus Francavilla, establishing himself as a reliable player in the third tier of Italian football.

In July 2019, Folorunsho transferred to Serie A club Napoli on a permanent basis. However, he was immediately loaned out to Serie C club Bari for two years. His time at Bari was followed by a series of loan spells in Serie B, where he played for Reggina in the 2020–21 season, Pordenone and Reggina again in 2021–22, and Bari once more in 2022–23. These loan moves provided him with valuable experience in Italy’s second division, further developing his skills as a midfielder.

In August 2023, Folorunsho joined Serie A club Hellas Verona on loan for the 2023–24 season, marking his first stint in the top flight. The following January, he moved to Fiorentina on loan with an option to make the deal permanent. In July 2025, he was loaned to Cagliari, again with an option for a permanent transfer. Throughout his career, Folorunsho has demonstrated versatility and adaptability, playing for multiple clubs across different tiers of Italian football.

Internationally, Folorunsho made his debut for the Italy national team in June 2024. He was initially called up by head coach Luciano Spalletti in March 2024 but did not feature in friendly matches against Venezuela and Ecuador. Later that year, he was included in Italy’s squad for UEFA Euro 2024. His first appearance for Italy came on 9 June in a friendly against Bosnia and Herzegovina, where he entered the game as a substitute in the 76th minute, replacing Davide Frattesi. Italy won the match 1–0, with Folorunsho contributing to the team’s success.

Folorunsho is of Nigerian descent, adding to the diversity of his background. His career has been marked by consistent progression, with highlights including winning Serie A Goal of the Month for February 2024. This recognition underscores his ability to make an impact on the field and his growing reputation as a talented midfielder. As of the latest updates in the article, he continues to develop his career, balancing loan moves with opportunities to prove himself at the highest level.

title: Mukesh (actor)
text:
Mukesh Madhavan, better known by his stage name Mukesh, is a prominent Indian actor, producer, television presenter, and politician, primarily known for his work in Malayalam cinema. Born on 5 March 1957 in Kollam, Kerala, to actors O. Madhavan and Vijayakumari, Mukesh grew up in a family deeply rooted in the performing arts. His sisters, Sandhya Rajendran and Jayasree, are also involved in stage and film acting. Mukesh attended Infant Jesus Anglo-Indian School in Kollam, followed by a Bachelor of Science degree from Sree Narayana College and a law degree from Kerala Law Academy. Before entering films, he was active in stage dramas.

Mukesh made his film debut in 1982 with *Balloon* and soon landed his first leading role in *Ithu Njangalude Katha*, a remake of a Tamil film. Though the movie was an average grosser, its songs became popular. In the mid-1980s, he appeared in several comedy films directed by Priyadarshan, often in supporting roles. His first solo lead role came in *Mutharamkunnu P.O.* (1985), which, despite average box office performance, later gained cult status. His breakthrough came with *Boeing Boeing* (1985), a commercial hit where he played a supporting role to Mohanlal. This began a long collaboration, with films like *Ninnishtam Ennishtam* (1986) and *Hello My Dear Wrong Number* (1986). He also appeared in supporting roles alongside Mammootty in successful films like *Snehamulla Simham* (1986), *Shyama* (1986), and *Thaniyavarthanam* (1987). His role as Chacko in *Oru CBI Diary Kurippu* (1988) became iconic, and he reprised the character in multiple sequels. His biggest success of the 1980s came with *Ramji Rao Speaking* (1989), a blockbuster comedy that ran for 200 days in theaters and remains a cult classic.

In the 1990s, Mukesh solidified his stardom with films like *In Harihar Nagar* (1990) and *Godfather* (1991), the latter being the longest-running Malayalam film at the time. He also teamed up with Jayaram in successful films like *Thoovalsparsham* (1990) and *Aayushkalam* (1992). Other notable hits included *Mookilla Rajyathu* (1991), a slapstick comedy, and *Hitler* (1996), a comedy-drama co-starring Mammootty. His film *Kaanakkinaavu* (1996) won the Nargis Dutt Award at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI). The late 1990s saw more hits, including *Friends* (1999), the year’s highest-grossing film, and *Aakasha Ganga* (1999).

In the 2000s and 2010s, Mukesh shifted to supporting roles in films like *Udayananu Tharam* (2005) and *Katha Parayumbol* (2007), which he co-produced and won several awards, including the Kerala State Film Award for Best Film with Popular Appeal and Aesthetic Value. He also produced *Thattathin Marayathu* (2012), considered a defining film of the Malayalam New Wave. He hosted television shows, including a Malayalam version of *Deal or No Deal* and the talk show *Badai Bungalow*.

Mukesh’s personal life has included two marriages—Saritha, a South Indian actress, in 1988 (divorced in 2011), and dance scholar Methil Devika in 2013 (divorce filed in 2021). He has authored two books: *Mukesh Kathakal – Jeevithathiley Nerum Narmavum* (2007) and *Mukesh Babu and Party in Dubai* (2009). In 2021, he faced controversy after a leaked phone call where he allegedly mistreated a student, and in 2024, he was arrested and later released on bail in a sexual harassment case following the Hema Committee report.

Politically, Mukesh is a member of the Communist Party of India (Marxist). He has been the MLA for Kollam since 2016, winning re-election in 2021 but with a reduced margin. In 2024, he contested the Lok Sabha from Kollam but lost to the UDF candidate. Beyond acting, he served as the chairman of the Kerala Sangeetha Nataka Academy and has been involved in theater productions, including *Chayamukhi* (2008) and *Naaga* (2015).

Mukesh’s filmography spans over 275 Malayalam films, with sporadic appearances in Tamil cinema. His contributions to Malayalam cinema, both as an actor and producer, have earned him lasting recognition, though his career has also seen its share of controversies and setbacks.

title: Phife Dawg
text:
Malik Izaak Taylor, known professionally as Phife Dawg, was a Trinidadian-American rapper and a key member of the influential hip-hop group A Tribe Called Quest. Born on November 20, 1970, in Queens, New York City, he was the son of Trinidadian immigrant parents, poet Cheryl Boyce-Taylor and Walt Taylor. Raised in the St. Albans neighborhood of Queens, Phife was born prematurely, and his twin brother, Mikal, died shortly after birth. He grew up alongside future A Tribe Called Quest member Q-Tip, whom he first met at the age of two. After hearing "Rapper's Delight" by the Sugarhill Gang at nine years old, Phife suggested he and Q-Tip should rap together. He attended Pine Forge Academy, a Seventh-day Adventist boarding school near Philadelphia, for his freshman year of high school before transferring to Springfield Gardens High School in Queens.

In 1985, Phife co-founded A Tribe Called Quest (originally called Quest) with Q-Tip and DJ Ali Shaheed Muhammad, later joined by Jarobi White. The group became part of the Native Tongues collective, which included hip-hop acts like De La Soul and Jungle Brothers. A Tribe Called Quest signed with Jive Records in 1989 and released their debut album, *People's Instinctive Travels and the Paths of Rhythm*, in 1990. Phife’s role in the group expanded with their second album, *The Low End Theory* (1991), where he adopted the nickname "the Five-Foot Assassin" (a playful reference to his 5-foot-3-inch height) and rapped about social and political issues. The album is now considered one of the greatest hip-hop records ever made. The group released three more albums—*Midnight Marauders* (1993), *Beats, Rhymes and Life* (1996), and *The Love Movement* (1998)—before disbanding due to internal conflicts and label disputes. These tensions, particularly between Phife and Q-Tip, were documented in the 2011 film *Beats, Rhymes & Life: The Travels of A Tribe Called Quest*.

Outside of A Tribe Called Quest, Phife collaborated with other artists, appearing on tracks like the Fu-Schnickens' "La Schmoove," Diamond D's "Painz & Strife," and Chi-Ali's "Let the Horns Blow." In 2000, he released his solo debut, *Ventilation: Da LP*, and was working on a second album, *MUTTYmorPHosis*, at the time of his death. A single from the unreleased album, "Sole Men," was posted the day after his passing, followed by "Nutshell" in April 2016. In 2015, A Tribe Called Quest reunited for a performance on *The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon*, leading to the recording of a final album, *We Got It from Here... Thank You 4 Your Service*, released posthumously in 2016. Phife’s second solo album, *Forever*, was released in 2022, six years after his death.

Phife was married to Deisha Head-Taylor and had two children. A fan of the New York Knicks, he appeared as a playable character in the video games *NBA 2K7* and *NBA 2K9*. Diagnosed with diabetes in 1990, he struggled with the condition throughout his life, calling himself a "funky diabetic" in A Tribe Called Quest’s 1993 hit "Oh My God." Despite a kidney transplant from his wife in 2008, his health declined, and he died at age 45 on March 22, 2016, due to complications from diabetes.

Phife Dawg’s legacy includes his unique "self-deprecating swagger" and his role in redefining hip-hop’s sound during the 1990s. His work influenced artists like Kanye West, Jill Scott, and The Roots, while *The Low End Theory* remains a landmark in the genre. In 2016, a section of Linden Boulevard in Queens was renamed "Malik 'Phife Dawg' Taylor Way," and in 2024, he was posthumously inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of A Tribe Called Quest. His filmography includes minor acting roles in *Who's the Man?* (1993) and *The Rugrats Movie* (1998), as well as appearances in documentaries and video games. Phife Dawg’s contributions to music and culture continue to be celebrated long after his passing.

title: Naz Mitrou-Long
text:
Nazareth Jersey Mitrou-Long, born on August 3, 1993, in Mississauga, Ontario, Canada, is a professional basketball player currently playing for AEK Athens in the Greek Basketball League and the Basketball Champions League. He is of Canadian–Greek descent, with his father being of Trinidadian heritage and his mother, Georgia, being a Greek Canadian who immigrated to Canada as a child. Naz has three siblings and six half-siblings, including his brother Elijah, who also played college basketball. In 2015, Naz decided to honor his mother by adding her surname, "Mitrou," to his jersey.

Mitrou-Long began his basketball career at Father Michael Goetz in Mississauga before moving to Findlay Prep in Las Vegas, where he helped the team to a 28–4 record and an ESPN Rise National High School Invitational appearance. He was ranked as the 7th-best player in Canada and participated in the 2011 All-Canada Classic. After high school, he committed to Iowa State University, where he played college basketball from 2012 to 2017.

At Iowa State, Mitrou-Long quickly established himself as a clutch three-point shooter. As a freshman, he averaged 1.4 points and 1.0 assists, playing in 18 games. His sophomore season was a breakout year, as he played in all 36 games, starting seven, and averaged 7.1 points per game with a 40% three-point shooting percentage. He made key shots in several games, including a buzzer-beater to send the Cyclones to overtime against Oklahoma State. His junior season saw him improve further, averaging 10.1 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 2.0 assists, while making 77 three-pointers, the eighth-most in a single season for Iowa State. However, he suffered labral tears in both hips, requiring offseason surgeries. He missed part of his senior season due to lingering hip pain but was granted a medical redshirt, allowing him to return for a redshirt senior year. In his final season, he was named to the All-Big 12 Second Team after averaging 12.0 points and shooting 44.9% from the field, despite 77.5% of his shots coming from three-point range.

After going undrafted in the 2017 NBA draft, Mitrou-Long played for the Sacramento Kings in the NBA Summer League and later signed with the Utah Jazz. He split time between the Jazz and their G League affiliate, the Salt Lake City Stars, appearing in 20 NBA games. He also had a brief stint with the Indiana Pacers in 2019 before playing in the G League with the Fort Wayne Mad Ants. In 2021, he moved to Italy, signing with Basket Brescia Leonessa, where he averaged 17.5 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 5 assists per game. The following year, he joined Olimpia Milano, an Italian powerhouse, but was waived in 2023 after a short stint with Žalgiris Kaunas in Lithuania.

In November 2023, Mitrou-Long signed with Olympiacos Piraeus in Greece, securing a three-year contract after obtaining Greek citizenship. He officially became a domestic player for Olympiacos in December 2023. Additionally, he was called up to the Greek national team in 2024, making his debut against Great Britain in November 2024, where he scored 12 points.

Throughout his career, Mitrou-Long has been known for his three-point shooting and clutch performances. His journey from Canada to the NBA, Europe, and now the Greek national team highlights his versatility and resilience, particularly after overcoming hip injuries to extend his career.

title: Lina Marulanda
text:
Lina María Marulanda Cuartas, better known as Lina Marulanda, was a Colombian television personality and model born on 15 May 1980 in Medellín, Colombia. Her modeling career began at the age of 12, and she quickly became involved in fashion shows and photo shoots, though she later expressed regret for her rushed upbringing in the industry. She attended Santa María del Rosario de Medellín High School but transferred to Parra Paris High School after conflicts with the school’s administration. After graduating, she pursued higher education at Jorge Tadeo Lozano University in Bogotá, where she studied advertising.

Marulanda’s television career began in 2002 when she debuted as a presenter at CM& News. She later joined Caracol News, where she worked for six years, presenting the 0700 edition and the international news segment. From 2003 onward, she co-hosted the entertainment section of the evening news, first with actress Margarita Ortega and later with model Adriana Arboleda. In December 2005, she took over the entertainment portion of the 12:30 news slot alongside journalist Iván Lalinde. In 2007, she expanded her roles by hosting the reality show *Challenge 20-07* on Canal Caracol and returning to CM& News for special reports on Colombiamoda 2007. She also contributed to W Radio, covering Colombiamoda 2007 and later joining *La hora del Regreso* as a presenter, replacing Marcela Sarmiento.

Beyond her broadcasting work, Marulanda was a prominent spokesmodel for major clothing brands and appeared in several magazines, including *SoHo*, *Don Juan*, *Cromos*, and *G*. Her career spanned both television and print media, establishing her as a recognizable figure in Colombian entertainment.

Tragically, Marulanda’s life ended on 22 April 2010 when she fell from the balcony of her sixth-floor apartment in Bogotá. Her death was ruled a suicide. At the time, she was with her parents, her ex-husband, and a doctor, and she was in the midst of divorce proceedings from her second husband, Carlos Oñate, a marriage that had lasted only three months. Her untimely death at the age of 29 marked the end of a career that had seen her rise to prominence in Colombian media.

title: Julie Bishop
text:
Julie Isabel Bishop, born on 17 July 1956 in Lobethal, South Australia, is a former Australian politician who played a significant role in national and international affairs. She served as the Minister for Foreign Affairs from 2013 to 2018 and as the deputy leader of the Liberal Party from 2007 to 2018. Bishop represented the Division of Curtin in Western Australia as a Member of Parliament from 1998 to 2019. Since January 2020, she has been the chancellor of the Australian National University, the first woman to hold that position, and in April 2024, she was appointed as the United Nations special envoy for Myanmar.

Bishop grew up on an apple and cherry orchard in Basket Range, South Australia, after her family's property was rebuilt following the Black Sunday bushfires. She attended St Peter's Collegiate Girls' School and later studied law at the University of Adelaide, graduating in 1978. Before entering politics, she worked as a commercial lawyer in Perth, becoming a partner at Mangan, Ey & Bishop in 1982 and later at Robinson Cox, which merged into Clayton Utz in 1992. She served as the managing partner of Clayton Utz's Perth office from 1994 to 1998. During her legal career, she was involved in several high-profile cases, including a controversial asbestos-related lawsuit for CSR Limited, which she defended on legal grounds despite later criticism.

Bishop entered politics in 1992, joining the Liberal Party after the WA Inc scandal. She was elected to parliament in 1998, representing Curtin. In the Howard government, she held various ministerial roles, including Minister for Ageing (2003–2006), Minister for Education and Science (2006–2007), and Minister for Women (2006–2007). Her tenure as education minister was marked by proposals for national education standards and performance-based pay for teachers, which faced opposition from state governments and educators.

After the Coalition lost the 2007 election, Bishop was elected deputy leader of the Liberal Party, the first woman to hold the position. She served under three different leaders—Brendan Nelson, Malcolm Turnbull, and Tony Abbott—before becoming Australia's first female foreign minister in 2013. During her time as foreign minister, she oversaw significant changes to Australia's foreign aid program, including the abolition of AusAID and its integration into the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFAT). This move, along with subsequent budget cuts, reduced Australia's aid spending from around $5.0 billion in 2014/15 to $4.2 billion in 2015/16, with further reductions in the following years.

Bishop also introduced the New Colombo Plan, which provided funding for undergraduate students to study in the Indo-Pacific region. Her tenure was marked by international crises, including the rise of ISIS, the shooting down of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17, and the execution of Australian citizens by Indonesia. She compared the psychological motivations of ISIS to those of Nazism in a 2015 speech.

In 2018, Bishop ran for the Liberal Party leadership during a leadership spill but was eliminated in the first round, with Scott Morrison ultimately becoming prime minister. She stepped down as deputy leader and moved to the backbench, announcing her retirement from politics in February 2019. Since then, she has taken on high-profile roles, including her current position as chancellor of the Australian National University and her appointment as the United Nations special envoy for Myanmar in 2024. Bishop's career has been marked by her trailblazing roles in Australian politics and her contributions to foreign policy and international relations.

title: Dominique Blake
text:
Dominique Blake is a Jamaican track and field athlete born on 15 February 1987 in the Bronx, New York. She began her competitive career in 2002 as an indoor track and field athlete before transitioning to outdoor events the following year. Blake attended Penn State University, where she competed for the university’s track and field team from 2004 to 2008 and earned a communications degree.

During her NCAA career, Blake participated in several relay events. In 2006, she finished 12th in the 4x400 meter relay at the NCAA Division I Indoor Track and Field Championships. The following year, she and her relay team placed 4th in the same event, while also finishing 13th in the distance medley relay. At the 2008 NCAA Indoor Championships, Blake’s 4x400 meter relay team secured 5th place, but she did not advance past the heats in the individual 400 meters, placing 17th overall.

Blake’s professional career began with controversy when she was disqualified from the 2006 USA Outdoor Track and Field Championships after testing positive for ephedrine, resulting in a nine-month ban. She later competed at the 2008 U.S. Olympic Trials, where she finished 23rd in the 400 meters, failing to advance beyond the preliminaries.

Representing Jamaica, Blake won a gold medal in the 4x400 meter relay at the 2010 Central American and Caribbean Games. That same year, she competed at the Commonwealth Games, finishing 12th in the 4x400 meter relay and 18th in the individual 400 meters, reaching the semi-finals. She also participated in the 2012 IAAF World Indoor Championships but did not medal.

At the 2012 London Olympics, Blake was named to Jamaica’s 4x400 meter relay team but did not run in the event. Despite not competing, the Jamaica Olympic Association mistakenly awarded her a bronze medal, which she initially kept. In 2013, Blake was suspended for six years after testing positive for methylhexanamine. She successfully appealed the decision, reducing her ban to 4.5 years, and returned to competition in January 2017. Later that year, she returned the Olympic bronze medal in compliance with anti-doping regulations.

In 2018, Blake was part of Jamaica’s 4x400 meter relay team at the IAAF World Indoor Championships, helping them qualify for the final. However, the team was disqualified in the final. At the 2018 National Relay Championships, she placed 6th in the 400 meters and did not finish the 800 meters. The following year, she finished 4th in the 400 meters at the 2019 National Relay Championships. Blake’s career has been marked by both success and controversy, including doping violations and the unusual circumstance of receiving an Olympic medal without competing in the event.

title: Diafra Sakho
text:
Diafra Sakho, born on 24 December 1989 in Guédiawaye, Senegal, was a professional footballer who played as a striker. His career began in Senegal with Génération Foot, a football academy affiliated with FC Metz, before he moved to France in 2007 to join Metz. After impressing in the reserve team with 17 goals in 22 games during the 2009–10 season, he earned a first-team debut in January 2010. Initially used mostly as a substitute, Sakho was loaned to Boulogne in 2012. His breakthrough came the following season when he scored 19 goals in 33 league appearances, helping Metz secure promotion from Championnat National to Ligue 2. In the 2013–14 season, he netted 20 goals in 36 appearances, leading Metz to the Ligue 2 title and earning him the Ligue 2 Player of the Year award.

In August 2014, Sakho signed for West Ham United, joining the Premier League club with a four-year contract. He quickly made an impact, scoring in his first four Premier League starts, a feat that broke a 26-year-old club record. His strong form continued, and he was named Premier League Player of the Month for October 2014. Despite injuries interrupting his 2014–15 season, he finished as West Ham’s top scorer with 12 goals. The following season, he contributed to West Ham’s Europa League campaign but was sent off in a qualifying match. His performances in the Premier League included goals against Liverpool and Manchester City, though injuries and a failed transfer request complicated his tenure. By 2017, persistent injuries limited his appearances, and he left West Ham in January 2018 after scoring 24 goals in 71 games.

Sakho then joined Rennes, where he scored on his debut. Later in 2018, he was loaned to Turkish club Bursaspor. In 2020, he moved to Swiss side Neuchâtel Xamax but left after failing to score in eight appearances. In 2022, he signed for French Championnat National club Nancy, where he retired in July 2023.

On the international stage, Sakho made his Senegal debut in 2014 and scored his first goal four days later. He was part of the squad for the 2018 FIFA World Cup, which marked Senegal’s return to the tournament after 16 years. His club honors include the Ligue 2 title with Metz and individual accolades such as Ligue 2 Player of the Year and Premier League Player of the Month.

Sakho’s career was also marked by off-field issues in 2015, when he was arrested twice on allegations of assault and witness intimidation. However, he was later cleared of all charges. His final club was Djibouti Premier League side Arta/Solar7, where he won league and cup titles in 2021–22. Sakho retired from professional football in 2023.

title: Fahadh Faasil
text:
Fahadh Faasil, born Abdul Hameed Mohammed Fahad Fazil on 8 August 1982 in Alappuzha, Kerala, is one of the most celebrated actors in Malayalam cinema. Born into a film family—his father is director Fazil—Fahadh made his debut at 20 in his father’s 2002 film *Kaiyethum Doorath*, which failed critically and commercially. Initially credited as Shaanu, he received mixed reviews for his performance. The film’s poor reception led him to take a seven-year hiatus, during which he pursued a Master’s in Philosophy at the University of Miami.

Fahadh returned to acting in 2009 with *Kerala Cafe*, an anthology film that marked his first positive industry response. His breakthrough came in 2011 with *Chaappa Kurishu* and *Akam*, both thrillers where he earned the Kerala State Film Award for Second Best Actor. The following year, 2012, proved pivotal, with *22 Female Kottayam* and *Diamond Necklace* establishing him as a leading star. *22 Female Kottayam* won him his first Filmfare Award for Best Actor – Malayalam, while *Diamond Necklace* showcased his range as an oncologist in Dubai, earning praise for his nuanced performance.

2013 was a prolific year, with Fahadh starring in twelve films, including *Annayum Rasoolum* (a romantic drama), *Amen* (a black comedy), and *North 24 Kaatham* (an adventure drama). *Artist* and *North 24 Kaatham* earned him the Kerala State Film Award for Best Actor, while *North 24 Kaatham* also won him another Filmfare Award. His performance in *Bangalore Days* (2014), a coming-of-age drama, solidified his stardom, with the film becoming one of Malayalam cinema’s highest-grossing hits.

Despite some box office failures, Fahadh continued to impress critics with roles in *Maheshinte Prathikaaram* (2016), *Take Off* (2017), and *Thondimuthalum Driksakshiyum* (2017). The latter won him the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor and his third Filmfare Best Actor – Malayalam award. His portrayal of a thief in the film was particularly lauded for its subtlety and depth.

In 2018, he experimented with genres, starring in *Carbon* (a coming-of-age drama), *Varathan* (an action thriller), and *Njan Prakashan* (a satirical comedy). *Kumbalangi Nights* (2019), where he played a male chauvinist, became a cult classic and won him the Kerala State Film Award for Best Character Actor. His 2021 film *Joji*, where he played an engineering dropout, earned him widespread acclaim, further cementing his reputation as a versatile actor.

Fahadh is also a producer, co-owning Fahadh Faasil and Friends with his wife, actress Nazriya Nazim, and Bhavana Studios with directors Dileesh Pothan and Syam Pushkaran. Beyond films, he is a philanthropist and celebrity endorser. His career is marked by a willingness to take risks, whether in indie films or mainstream blockbusters, making him one of Malayalam cinema’s most respected and bankable stars.

title: Haruto Takahashi
text:
Haruto Takahashi, born on November 7, 1995, is a Japanese professional baseball pitcher who currently plays for the Hanshin Tigers in Nippon Professional Baseball (NPB). His early interest in baseball was influenced by his older brother, and he initially played softball before transitioning to little league baseball with the Nishina Shonen Baseball Club in Shizuoka. He later attended Tokoha University Tachibana Integrated High, where he played as both a pitcher and right fielder, contributing to his school’s victory in the national junior high softball tournament. In his second year of high school, he pitched in the 2012 Summer Koshien as a reliever, but his team was eliminated in the first round. Despite declaring his intent to turn professional after graduation, he went undrafted and instead enrolled at Asia University in Tokyo. There, he became a regular starter in the Tohto University Baseball League and helped his team reach the 2016 Japan National Collegiate Baseball Championship Tournament, where he was named to the Best 8. His collegiate career ended with a 5-7 record and a 3.57 ERA over 31 appearances.

Takahashi was selected by the Hanshin Tigers in the second round of the 2017 NPB draft, signing a 70 million yen contract with an annual salary of 12 million yen. Assigned jersey number 29, he made his professional debut on April 11, 2018, pitching seven shutout innings against the Carps to earn his first career win. This made him the first Hanshin rookie pitcher in 60 years to win his debut at Koshien Stadium. Despite his early success, his weak arm required extended rest intervals, and he was sidelined in June to prevent further strain. He finished his rookie season with a 2-3 record and a 3.63 ERA, earning a 1 million yen salary raise. In 2019, he struggled early in the season, spending time in the farm system before returning in May. He secured his first win in over a year on May 30 and showed strong performances in July, though a lack of run support prevented further victories. His arm issues resurfaced later in the season, and he finished with a 3-9 record, 1 hold, and a 3.78 ERA. His post-season performances helped Hanshin reach the Climax Series final, and his improved play earned him a 9 million yen raise, bringing his salary to 22 million yen.

The 2020 season, shortened due to COVID-19, saw Takahashi thrive early, posting a 0.82 ERA in August and a career-high 14 strikeouts on October 5, earning his first complete win. His strong performances against the Giants, including a 2.03 ERA in six starts, highlighted his effectiveness. He finished the season with a 5-4 record and a career-best 2.49 ERA, second among Hanshin starters. His success was partly attributed to his battery work with catcher Seishiro Sakamoto, who helped optimize his pitching strategy. His salary increased by 7 million yen to 29 million yen.

Takahashi is a 5'11" left-handed pitcher with a three-quarter delivery. His repertoire includes a four-seam fastball (averaging 150 km/h), a cutter, a two-seamer, and occasional curveballs and sliders. Despite his arm’s physical limitations, he has reached a top speed of 152 km/h. His pitching style emphasizes precision, often targeting the edges of the strike zone. Throughout his career, he has demonstrated resilience and adaptability, overcoming early setbacks to become a reliable starter for the Hanshin Tigers.

title: Dr. Dre
text:
Dr. Dre, born Andre Romell Young on February 18, 1965, in Compton, California, is a pioneering figure in hip-hop as a rapper, producer, and entrepreneur. He began his career in 1984 as a member of the electro-hop group World Class Wreckin' Cru, where he adopted the moniker Dr. Dre. His early work, while not yet distinctive, laid the groundwork for his later success. In 1987, he co-founded N.W.A with Eazy-E, Ice Cube, and Arabian Prince, a group that popularized gangsta rap and brought raw, unfiltered depictions of inner-city life to mainstream music. Their 1989 album *Straight Outta Compton* became a landmark in West Coast hip-hop, though its explicit content, particularly the track "Fuck tha Police," drew criticism from the FBI. After Ice Cube's departure in 1989, Dre became the primary producer for N.W.A's follow-up album, *Efil4zaggin*, before leaving the group in 1991 due to financial disputes with Eazy-E.

Dre then joined Death Row Records, where he released his debut solo album, *The Chronic* (1992), which established the G-funk sound—characterized by smooth synths, heavy bass, and slow rhythms. The album was a massive success, spawning hits like "Nuthin' but a 'G' Thang" (featuring Snoop Dogg) and "Let Me Ride," the latter winning a Grammy. *The Chronic* also introduced or elevated artists like Snoop Dogg, Kurupt, and Nate Dogg. Dre further solidified his influence by producing Snoop Dogg's *Doggystyle* (1993) and Warren G's *Regulate... G Funk Era* (1994). However, he left Death Row in 1996 amid conflicts with label head Suge Knight, founding Aftermath Entertainment under Interscope Records.

Aftermath's early struggles were reversed in 1998 when Dre signed Eminem, whose debut *The Slim Shady LP* (1999) revitalized the label. Dre's second album, *2001* (1999), marked a return to gangsta rap, featuring collaborations with Eminem, Snoop Dogg, and others. The album was a commercial and critical triumph, certified six times platinum. Beyond music, Dre has produced hit singles like "No Diggity" (1996) with Blackstreet and contributed to film soundtracks, including *Friday*.

As a producer, Dre has shaped the careers of artists like 50 Cent, Kendrick Lamar, and The Game. He has won seven Grammy Awards, including Producer of the Year, and was ranked among *Rolling Stone*'s 100 Greatest Artists of All Time. Outside music, he co-founded Beats Electronics, which Apple acquired in 2014 for $3 billion. His career has been marred by controversies, including a 1991 assault charge involving TV host Dee Barnes and later allegations of domestic violence, which he publicly apologized for in 2015. Despite these challenges, Dr. Dre remains one of hip-hop's most influential figures.

title: Quincy Jones
text:
Quincy Delight Jones Jr. (1933–2024) was a legendary American record producer, composer, arranger, conductor, trumpeter, and bandleader with a seven-decade career marked by extraordinary achievements. He received 28 Grammy Awards, a Primetime Emmy, a Tony Award, and numerous other honors, including multiple Academy Award and Golden Globe nominations. His work spanned jazz, pop, and film, making him one of the most influential figures in music history.

Born in Chicago on March 14, 1933, Jones was the son of a semi-professional baseball player and a bank officer. His family moved to Seattle during the Great Migration, where he developed his musical talents as a trumpeter and arranger. His mother and a neighbor, Lucy Jackson, introduced him to music at an early age. After his mother's mental health crisis, his father remarried, and the family relocated to Bremerton, Washington. Jones later attended Garfield High School, where he honed his skills alongside future jazz musicians. He earned scholarships to Seattle University and Berklee College of Music, where he studied with influential jazz artists.

Jones began his professional career in the 1950s, touring Europe with jazz bands and later working as an arranger and conductor. He played a key role in Elvis Presley’s first television appearances in 1956 and later collaborated with Frank Sinatra and Count Basie. His breakthrough as a producer came in the 1960s when he produced hits for Lesley Gore, including "It's My Party" and "You Don't Own Me." He also composed film scores, beginning with *The Pawnbroker* (1964) and continuing with classics like *In the Heat of the Night* (1967) and *The Italian Job* (1969). His work in television included iconic themes for *Sanford and Son* and *Ironside*.

In 1978, Jones produced the soundtrack for *The Wiz*, which introduced him to Michael Jackson. Their collaboration on *Off the Wall* (1979) was a massive success, followed by *Thriller* (1982), the best-selling album of all time, and *Bad* (1987). He also produced *We Are the World* (1985), a charity single for famine relief in Ethiopia. His film scoring continued with *The Color Purple* (1985), for which he received an Oscar nomination. That same year, he won an Emmy for his work on the miniseries *Roots*.

Throughout his career, Jones received numerous accolades, including the Grammy Legend Award, the Kennedy Center Honors, and the National Medal of the Arts. He was also honored with the Academy Honorary Award in 2024. His influence extended beyond music, as he co-founded Qwest Productions and later Qwest Entertainment, a multimedia company that produced films, television, and music.

Jones’s legacy is defined by his versatility and innovation. From jazz to pop, film scores to charity work, he left an indelible mark on the entertainment industry. His ability to collaborate with diverse artists and adapt to changing musical trends solidified his status as one of the most respected figures in music history.

title: W. Clark Still
text:
William Clark Still, born in 1946, is an American organic chemist and distinguished professor at Columbia University. His work has significantly advanced the fields of natural product synthesis, reaction development, conformational analysis, macrocyclic stereocontrol, and computational chemistry. One of his most enduring contributions is the development of flash column chromatography, a widely adopted purification technique for organic compounds.

Still’s research in total synthesis includes groundbreaking work on complex natural products. In 1979, he achieved the first total synthesis of periplanone B, a potent sex pheromone of the American cockroach. The synthesis confirmed the compound’s relative stereochemistry and featured a key anionic oxy-Cope rearrangement to form a 10-membered macrocyclic ring. This transformation involved treating a tertiary alcohol with potassium hydride and 18-crown-6, followed by trapping the resulting enolate with chlorotrimethylsilane. Subsequent steps included Rubottom oxidation, TBS protection, and selenoxide rearrangement to form an enone substrate. Epoxide formation was highly diastereoselective, guided by macrocyclic stereocontrol, and the synthesis was completed with the removal of protecting groups and oxidation.

In 1980, Still and his team synthesized monensin, a complex polyether ionophore. A critical step was the late-stage union of two fragments via an intermolecular aldol reaction, yielding a beta-hydroxyketone with 75% diastereoselectivity. The synthesis was completed by hydrogenolysis, TES deprotection, spiroketal formation, and ester hydrolysis. This work demonstrated advanced acyclic stereocontrol consistent with the Cram-Felkin-Anh model.

Beyond total synthesis, Still developed several influential reaction methods. The Wittig-Still rearrangement (1978) expanded the scope of the 2,3-Wittig rearrangement by using organotin-substituted ethers, enabling chemoselective transmetalation with n-butyllithium. This method was applied in the formal synthesis of Cecropia juvenile hormone, producing a stereoselective (Z,Z)-isomer. In 1983, Still and Gennari introduced the Still-Gennari alkenation, a modification of the Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons reaction. By using trifluoroethoxy-substituted phosphonates and a potassium counterion, this method achieved high Z-selectivity in alkene formation.

Flash column chromatography, published in 1978, revolutionized organic compound purification. Still’s innovation involved applying pressure to speed up solvent elution, reducing separation time and improving resolution. The technique became essential for small-scale purifications, and the original paper remains one of the most cited in the *Journal of Organic Chemistry*.

Still also pioneered computational chemistry, particularly conformational analysis. His Monte Carlo multiple-minimum search method (1989) efficiently identified the lowest-energy conformations of organic molecules. To make molecular modeling accessible, he developed *MacroModel* in 1986, an integrated software program featuring an implicit solvation model (GB/SA). Later acquired by Schrodinger, Inc., *MacroModel* provided organic chemists with a user-friendly tool for molecular mechanics calculations. Still’s contributions have left a lasting impact on synthetic chemistry, computational methods, and laboratory techniques.

title: Patrick Merrill
text:
Patrick Merrill, born on February 22, 1979, is a Canadian former professional lacrosse player who has since transitioned into a coaching and management role in the sport. He currently serves as the head coach and general manager of the San Diego Seals in the National Lacrosse League (NLL). Throughout his playing career, Merrill was a standout defender, known for his physicality and leadership on the floor. He played for two teams in the NLL: the Toronto Rock and the Titans (now known as the Toronto Rock again, following a brief period as the Titans after the 2008 NLL expansion draft). Additionally, he played for the Toronto Nationals in Major League Lacrosse (MLL).

Merrill entered the NLL as a first-round draft pick of the Toronto Rock in 2002, where he spent four seasons before being selected first overall by the Boston Blazers in the 2008 NLL expansion draft. However, due to the cancellation and subsequent reinstatement of the 2008 NLL season, the Blazers, along with the Arizona Sting, opted not to participate in that season. As a result, a dispersal draft was held, and Merrill was chosen second overall by the Titans. This move marked the beginning of a new phase in his career, though the team would later revert to the Toronto Rock name.

During his playing days, Merrill was recognized for his defensive skills and ability to control loose balls, which are crucial aspects of the game. His statistics in the NLL and MLL reflect his contributions, though the article does not provide specific figures. His brother, Brodie Merrill, also has a notable lacrosse career, currently playing for the San Diego Seals, where Patrick now serves as head coach and general manager. The familial connection in the sport adds an interesting dynamic to Patrick’s role with the team.

Beyond his playing career, Merrill has transitioned into coaching and management. His current position with the San Diego Seals involves overseeing both the on-floor strategy and the team’s administrative operations. While the article does not detail specific coaching achievements or statistics, his background as a former player and his leadership role suggest a deep understanding of the game at both the tactical and organizational levels.

In summary, Patrick Merrill’s career in lacrosse has spanned from being a highly regarded player to a key figure in team management. His journey from the Toronto Rock to the San Diego Seals highlights his adaptability and longevity in the sport. His work with the Seals, particularly in a dual head coach and general manager role, demonstrates his commitment to the game beyond his playing years. The article also notes the presence of his brother, Brodie, in the league, further emphasizing the Merrill family’s influence in professional lacrosse.

title: Radja Nainggolan
text:
Radja Nainggolan, born on 4 May 1988 in Antwerp, Belgium, is a professional footballer who has played primarily as a central midfielder for clubs in Italy, Belgium, Indonesia, and, most recently, the Challenger Pro League. Nicknamed "Il Ninja," Nainggolan spent the majority of his career in Italy, representing clubs like Piacenza, Cagliari, Roma, and Inter Milan, where he made 367 Serie A appearances and scored 48 goals. His performances earned him a place in Serie A's Team of the Year for four consecutive seasons.

Nainggolan's early life was marked by challenges. Born to a Belgian mother and an Indonesian father of Toba Batak descent, he was raised in the working-class neighborhood of Kiel. His father left the family when he was young, and his mother passed away in 2010, prompting him to tattoo her dates of birth and death on his back. He speaks Dutch, English, French, and Italian fluently and was raised Roman Catholic.

His professional career began with Tubantia Borgerhout and Germinal Beerschot before moving to Piacenza in Italy's Serie B in 2005. He quickly became a key player, helping them avoid relegation in the 2008–09 season. In 2010, he joined Cagliari, where he became a fan favorite and a key player for three seasons before transferring to Roma in 2014. At Roma, he played a crucial role in qualifying the team for the Champions League and extended his contract multiple times. His time at Roma was highlighted by his leadership and consistent performances.

In 2018, Nainggolan signed with Inter Milan for €38 million, including player exchanges. However, his time there was less successful, and he spent loan spells back at Cagliari. After leaving Inter in 2021, he briefly returned to Belgium with Antwerp before joining SPAL in Italy's second tier and later Bhayangkara in Indonesia. He currently plays for Lokeren-Temse in Belgium's third division.

Internationally, Nainggolan represented Belgium from 2009 to 2018, making 30 appearances and scoring six goals. He played at Euro 2016, where he scored crucial goals against Sweden and Wales. However, he retired from international football after being left out of Belgium's 2018 World Cup squad.

Nainggolan is known for his versatility, physicality, and technical ability, playing in various midfield roles, including as a playmaker, box-to-box midfielder, or even a winger. His aggressive tackling, vision, and long-range shooting have made him a standout player. However, he has also been criticized for his off-pitch behavior, including controversy over smoking and alcohol use.

Off the field, Nainggolan is married to Claudia Lai, with whom he has two daughters. His twin sister, Riana, is also a footballer. In 2019, his wife was diagnosed with cancer, and he has been vocal about supporting her. In 2023, he was appointed as an ambassador for the FIFA U-17 World Cup but faced legal trouble in 2025 when he was arrested in a cocaine-smuggling investigation.

Throughout his career, Nainggolan has won multiple honors, including Serie A titles with Inter Milan and Antwerp's Belgian Pro League. His contributions to Italian football earned him four Serie A Team of the Year selections, and he was named Serie A Player of the Month in November 2019. Despite his controversies, his talent and impact on the pitch remain undeniable.

title: Camille Paulus
text:
Camille Paulus, born on 24 April 1943, is a Belgian lawyer and politician with a long career in liberal politics. He earned his doctorate in law from the Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) in 1966, which provided the foundation for his professional and academic pursuits. Throughout his career, Paulus has held significant roles in both academia and public service.

One of his earliest notable positions was as a law professor at the VUB, where he likely contributed to legal education and research. In 1989, he succeeded Frans Van den Eynde as the mayor of Aartselaar, a position he held for several years. His leadership in local government demonstrated his ability to manage municipal affairs and engage with the community. Additionally, from 1982 to 1993, he served as the President of the Liberaal Vlaams Verbond, a liberal political organization in Flanders, reflecting his prominent role within the liberal movement.

Paulus’s most high-profile role came in 1993 when he was appointed governor of the Belgian province of Antwerp, a position he held until 2008. As governor, he oversaw the administration of the province, playing a key role in regional governance, policy implementation, and coordination with local and national authorities. His tenure spanned nearly 15 years, indicating a period of stability and continuity in provincial leadership.

The article cites sources such as the Liberal Archive and a historical publication on the province of Antwerp, which likely provide further context on his political and administrative contributions. While the summary is brief, it highlights his academic background, political leadership, and long-term influence in Belgian governance, particularly in the Antwerp region. His career exemplifies a blend of legal expertise, political engagement, and public administration, making him a notable figure in Belgian liberal politics.

title: Caitlin Lowe
text:
Caitlin Faith Lowe-Nagy, born on February 6, 1985, is a former collegiate softball standout and current head coach of the Arizona Wildcats softball team. She is widely recognized for her exceptional career as a player, having earned four consecutive first-team All-American honors while playing for the University of Arizona. Lowe led the Wildcats to back-to-back Women’s College World Series championships in 2006 and 2007, cementing her legacy as one of the program’s greatest players. Her contributions were instrumental in both titles, including a standout performance in the 2006 finale, where she scored a then-series record eight runs. Lowe’s senior year was particularly notable, as she set a career-high 49 stolen bases in a season, leading the Pac-10 and ranking second in NCAA history at the time. She concluded her college career as Arizona’s all-time leader in stolen bases and second in batting average, while also ranking in the top 10 in hits, triples, and runs. Her excellence off the field was equally impressive, earning her the inaugural Lowe’s Senior CLASS Award, which recognizes outstanding academic, athletic, and community contributions.

Before her college success, Lowe was a dominant high school player at Foothill High School in North Tustin, California, where she was a four-time All-American and helped lead her team to state and national championships in 2000. She was named Orange County Player of the Year in 2003, among other accolades.

Lowe’s career extended beyond college, as she became a key member of the U.S. Women’s National Team in 2005, earning a silver medal at the 2008 Summer Olympics. She played a pivotal role in the team’s silver-medal performance, including a game-winning hit in the semifinals against Japan. Her international career also included gold and silver medals in various World Cups and the 2007 Pan American Games, where she showcased her speed with a perfect 9-for-9 stolen base record.

In professional play, Lowe spent six seasons with National Pro Fastpitch’s USSSA Pride, winning three championships (2010, 2013, 2014) and earning Player of the Year honors in 2012. She retired in 2015 and was inducted into the USSSA Hall of Fame, with her jersey number 26 retired by the Pride.

Lowe transitioned to coaching, joining Arizona’s staff in 2013 as director of operations and later as a volunteer assistant. She was promoted to associate head coach in 2018 before being named head coach in June 2021, following Mike Candrea’s retirement. She is also one of only three players named to the Greatest College Softball Team All-Time by both fan vote and experts.

In her personal life, Lowe graduated from the University of Arizona with a degree in psychology and a minor in communications. She is married to Paul Nagy, an assistant soccer coach at Arizona, and they have two children. Her sisters Paige and McKenna also played softball for Oregon State University, highlighting her family’s athletic background.

Lowe’s career statistics and accolades place her among the elite in NCAA Division I softball history, including being one of the few players to achieve over 300 hits, 200 runs, and 100 stolen bases while maintaining a .400 career batting average. Her impact on the game, both as a player and now as a coach, continues to influence the sport.

title: Salt Bae
text:
Nusret Gökçe, widely recognized as Salt Bae, is a Turkish butcher, chef, and restaurateur who gained international fame in 2017 for his distinctive meat-preparation style, which became a viral internet sensation. Born in 1983 in Paşalı, a village in Erzurum Province, Gökçe comes from a Kurdish family and left school at the age of 11 or 12 to work as a butcher’s apprentice in Istanbul due to financial constraints. His father, Faik, was a mineworker, and the family’s limited resources forced Gökçe to enter the workforce early.

Before rising to fame, Gökçe traveled to countries like Argentina and the United States between 2007 and 2010, working in local restaurants without pay to gain experience. Upon returning to Turkey, he opened his first restaurant in Istanbul in 2010 and later expanded to Dubai in 2014. His global brand, Nusr-Et, is a luxury steakhouse chain with locations in Turkey, Greece, the United States, the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia. The name "Nusr-Et" combines his first name, Nusret, with "et," the Turkish word for "meat."

Gökçe’s viral fame began in January 2017 when a video of him preparing meat, dubbed "Ottoman Steak," spread across social media. The clip, which showed him sprinkling salt in a flamboyant manner—dropping it from his fingertips to his forearm before letting it fall onto the dish—earned him the nickname "Salt Bae." The video was viewed millions of times, catapulting him to global recognition. This exposure led to him serving numerous celebrities and politicians, further boosting his profile.

Despite his popularity, Gökçe’s restaurants have received mixed reviews. In 2018, critics panned his New York City location, describing the food as overpriced and underwhelming. The New York Post called it a "Public Rip-off No. 1," while GQ’s Joshua David Stein criticized the steak as mundane and the burgers as overcooked. Other reviewers noted that the meat was tough and lacked flavor, and that dining there felt like a "personal victory" due to the high prices. His Manhattan burger bar, once labeled New York’s worst restaurant, closed in 2023. However, some critics appreciated the theatricality of his tableside performances, viewing the experience as "dinner theater" rather than a traditional fine-dining establishment.

Gökçe’s career has been marred by several controversies. In 2017, he faced backlash for a 2016 photo in which he posed mimicking Fidel Castro, the former Cuban president. In 2018, a fire at his Istanbul restaurant injured Czech internet personality Týnuš Třešničková, who suffered severe burns. Later that year, he was criticized for serving Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro amid food shortages in Venezuela, leading to protests at his Miami restaurant. In 2019, four former employees accused him of withholding their tips, prompting a lawsuit that was later settled for $230,000. He also faced scrutiny in 2020 when his Boston restaurant was temporarily closed for violating COVID-19 safety protocols. In 2021, a £37,000 bill at one of his UK restaurants drew media attention. After the 2022 FIFA World Cup final, he was criticized for joining Argentine players on the field, handling the trophy, and biting their medals, leading to a FIFA investigation. In 2024, his London restaurant faced accusations of turning off the heat while profits rose, as well as allegations of tip theft and discrimination from former staff.

Despite these controversies, Gökçe has engaged in philanthropic efforts, including building a school, library, guesthouse, mosque, English education center, and computer laboratory in his hometown of Erzurum. These contributions highlight his dedication to giving back to his community, even as his business ventures remain a subject of both admiration and criticism.

title: Douglas Wood (engineer)
text:
Douglas Wood, an Australian construction engineer, was born on 30 June 1941 in Whyalla, South Australia. He attended Geelong College and the Gordon Institute of TAFE, graduating as a mechanical engineer. In 1973, he moved to the United States, settling in Alamo, California, where he worked for the Bechtel Corporation for 25 years. His career focused on project management, particularly in the construction of nuclear plants, including the Palo Verde Nuclear Generating Station in Arizona. After leaving Bechtel, he started his own company and later relocated to Iraq for business opportunities.

On 2 May 2005, while in Baghdad organizing a business deal, Wood was kidnapped along with two Iraqi associates by the Shura Council of the Mujahideen of Iraq. The armed group forced him into captivity and released video footage of him pleading for his life on the Arabic network al-Jazeera, demanding the withdrawal of Australian and American troops from Iraq. His captors repeatedly threatened and injured him, with later videos showing him with a machine gun held to his head, reading a statement demanding troop withdrawal within 72 hours. The Australian government, led by Prime Minister John Howard and Foreign Minister Alexander Downer, refused to pay a ransom or withdraw troops, fearing such actions would encourage further kidnappings. Wood’s family launched a public relations campaign in Australia and Iraq, portraying him as a peaceful family man sympathetic to the kidnappers' cause. Despite the deadline passing without action, Wood was not killed.

After six weeks in captivity, Wood was rescued on 14 June 2005 when Iraqi army troops, assisted by U.S. forces, raided a house in Ghazaliya during a routine weapons cache search. A brief firefight occurred, but no casualties were reported. Wood’s Iraqi associates had been killed a month earlier. News of his rescue reached Australian officials the following day, and footage of his recovery was broadcast in Australia. Prime Minister Howard praised the Muslim community and cleric Sheikh Taj al-Din Alhilali for their efforts, though Wood later denied ever speaking to Alhilali. In 2009, Wood claimed that seven of the ten Iraqi soldiers who rescued him had been murdered in retaliation for testifying against his kidnappers. As a result, two Iraqi servicemen were granted refugee visas by Australia.

Wood had previously worked on the failed Jervis Bay Nuclear Power Plant feasibility study and supported the development of nuclear energy in Australia. He stated he would live near a nuclear plant and assist in its construction but expressed concerns about the qualifications of Australia’s engineers and industrial suppliers for such a project. He passed away on 31 December 2019.

title: Charley Boorman
text:
Charley Boorman, born on 23 August 1966 in Wimbledon, London, is a British television presenter, travel writer, and actor with a strong passion for motorbikes. He is the son of film director Sir John Boorman and German costume designer Christel Kruse, and his godfather was the actor Lee Marvin, a close friend of his father. Boorman spent much of his childhood in County Wicklow, Ireland.

Boorman’s acting career began at a young age, often appearing in films directed by his father. His first role was in *Deliverance* (1972). In 1981, he played young Mordred in *Excalibur*, alongside his sister Katrine, who portrayed Ygraine. He later starred in *The Emerald Forest* (1985) and had a non-speaking role as a German pilot in *Hope and Glory* (1987), in which his sister also appeared. His other film credits include *The Serpent’s Kiss* (1997), where he met Ewan McGregor, and *The Bunker* (2001).

In 2007, Boorman took to the stage in Newcastle upon Tyne at the Tyne Theatre, performing a solo show that later toured the UK and Ireland. Around this time, he was diagnosed with testicular cancer, which was caught early, and he had a testicle removed. He became an advocate for men’s health, particularly through Movember, openly discussing his experience to raise awareness. His stage show continued in 2011, and he also promoted African Adventures, a commercial motorcycle expedition across Africa, which he documented using GPS tracking.

Boorman has been involved in charity work, supporting UNICEF since 2004, visiting projects featured in his TV series *Long Way Round*, *Long Way Down*, and *By Any Means*. In 2009, he became president of Dyslexia Action, a charity supporting dyslexic individuals, and has participated in campaigns to promote literacy and awareness of dyslexia. He also visited British troops in Afghanistan’s Helmand Province in 2009 and presented Duke of Edinburgh awards in 2014 and 2016.

A serious motorbike accident in Portugal in 2016 left Boorman with broken legs and a hip injury after colliding with a wall while avoiding a car. His recovery was complicated when he later broke his hip on a Vespa, leaving him temporarily reliant on a wheelchair. Though he returned to riding, he now walks with a limp due to a left leg that is 1 cm shorter than his right.

Boorman’s presenting career began with *Long Way Round* (2004), a motorcycle journey from London to New York with Ewan McGregor, which became a popular TV series and book. In 2006, he competed in the Dakar Rally but had to withdraw after an injury. *Long Way Down* (2007) documented another adventure with McGregor, from Scotland to South Africa. Other series include *By Any Means* (2008), where he traveled from Ireland to Australia using local transport, and *Right to the Edge* (2009), from Sydney to Tokyo. *Extreme Frontiers* (2011) explored Canada, while later series covered the US and South America, including *Long Way Up* (2020), where he and McGregor rode electric Harley-Davidsons from Argentina to Los Angeles. In 2022, he began presenting *Motorbike TV* for Motorsport.TV.

Boorman has authored several books, including *Long Way Round* (2004), *Long Way Down* (2007), and his autobiography *Long Way Back* (2017). His upcoming project, *Long Way Home* (2025), continues his adventures with McGregor. His work has been documented in both TV and print, showcasing his love for travel and motorcycling.

title: Zubaira Tukhugov
text:
Zubaira Alikhanovich Tukhugov, born on January 15, 1991, is a Russian mixed martial artist who primarily competed in the lightweight division of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC). He began his professional MMA career in 2010, making his debut by winning the Pankration Atrium Cup 2 tournament, a single-night, eight-man event. After compiling a record of 10-3 in regional promotions, he signed with the Russian organization Fight Nights, where he won all three of his fights, defeating opponents like Romano De Los Reyes, Harun Kina, and Vaso Bakocevic. During this period, he also fought for Cage Warriors, securing a victory over Denys Pidnebesnyi at CWFC 58.

In December 2013, Tukhugov was signed by the UFC and was initially scheduled to make his promotional debut against Thiago Tavares. However, Tavares had to withdraw due to injury and was replaced by Douglas Silva de Andrade, whom Tukhugov dominated to earn a unanimous decision win. His next fight came in October 2014 against Ernest Chavez, which he won via first-round technical knockout. A planned rematch with Tavares in 2015 was canceled after Tukhugov suffered a rib injury.

Tukhugov’s UFC career saw a mix of successes and setbacks. He defeated Phillipe Nover via split decision in December 2015 but lost a controversial bout against Renato Moicano in May 2016, despite twice being struck in the groin, with the referee allowing the fight to continue. Later that year, he was suspended for two years by USADA after testing positive for ostarine, a banned substance, in an out-of-competition drug test. During his suspension, he was also involved in the UFC 229 post-fight melee, where he jumped the cage and punched Conor McGregor, leading to a one-year suspension and a $25,000 fine from the Nevada State Athletic Commission (NSAC), later reduced to eight months.

Upon his return in September 2019, Tukhugov drew with Lerone Murphy in a competitive fight. He followed this with a first-round TKO victory over Kevin Aguilar in 2020 but lost a split decision to Hakeem Dawodu after missing weight and fighting at catchweight. In 2021, he defeated Ricardo Ramos via unanimous decision, marking his first win in nearly a year. However, his career was marred by frequent withdrawals, including fights against Nate Landwehr, Lucas Almeida, and Joel Álvarez, often due to weight-cutting issues, visa problems, or opponent withdrawals.

In his final UFC bout in February 2023, Tukhugov again missed weight, weighing in at 157.5 pounds for a lightweight fight, and lost a split decision to Elves Brenner. Shortly after, he was released from the UFC. Throughout his career, Tukhugov demonstrated durability and resilience but was also plagued by controversies, suspensions, and inconsistent performance, ultimately leading to his departure from the organization.

title: Michael Douglas
text:
Michael Kirk Douglas, born on September 25, 1944, is an acclaimed American actor and film producer known for his extensive career in Hollywood. He has received numerous prestigious awards, including two Academy Awards, five Golden Globe Awards, a Primetime Emmy, and the AFI Life Achievement Award. The son of legendary actor Kirk Douglas and Diana Dill, Douglas earned a Bachelor of Arts in drama from the University of California, Santa Barbara. His career began in the late 1960s, with early roles in films like *Hail, Hero!* (1969), which earned him a Golden Globe nomination for Most Promising Male Newcomer.

Douglas gained prominence in the 1970s, particularly through his role as a homicide inspector in the TV series *The Streets of San Francisco* (1972–1976), which earned him three consecutive Emmy nominations. His producing career took off when he secured the rights to *One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest* (1975) from his father, leading to an Academy Award for Best Picture. His breakout film role came in *The China Syndrome* (1979), a thriller about a nuclear power plant accident, which was released just days before the real-life Three Mile Island incident.

The 1980s and 1990s marked the peak of Douglas’s acting career. He starred in and produced *Romancing the Stone* (1984) and its sequel *The Jewel of the Nile* (1985), solidifying his status as a leading man. His most iconic role came in *Wall Street* (1987), where he portrayed corporate raider Gordon Gekko, winning an Academy Award for Best Actor. He reprised the role in the 2010 sequel, *Wall Street: Money Never Sleeps*. Other notable films from this period include *Fatal Attraction* (1987), *Basic Instinct* (1992), and *The American President* (1995). He also founded the short-lived record label Third Stone Records in 1992.

In the early 2000s, Douglas continued to take on diverse roles, including *Traffic* (2000), for which he won a Screen Actors Guild Award, and *Wonder Boys* (2000), earning Golden Globe and BAFTA nominations. He starred in *It Runs in the Family* (2003) alongside his parents and son, though the film was not well-received. In 2004, he received the Cecil B. DeMille Award, joining his father as one of only two father-son recipients. He also guest-starred in *Will & Grace*, earning an Emmy nomination.

Douglas’s later career included a resurgence in the 2010s, particularly with his Emmy-winning performance as Liberace in *Behind the Candelabra* (2013). He also starred in Marvel’s *Ant-Man* series as Hank Pym, appearing in multiple films and the animated series *What If...?* (2021–2023). On television, he played Sandy Kominsky in *The Kominsky Method* (2018–2021), winning a Golden Globe. In 2024, he portrayed Benjamin Franklin in the Apple TV+ miniseries *Franklin*.

Beyond acting, Douglas is known for his humanitarian and political activism. He serves on the board of the Nuclear Threat Initiative, is an honorary member of the Ploughshares Fund, and was appointed a United Nations Messenger of Peace in 1998. He has been married to actress Catherine Zeta-Jones since 2000. In 2025, Douglas announced his semi-retirement from acting, citing his age and a desire to spend more time with his family. His career spanned over six decades, leaving a lasting impact on film and television.

title: Riccardo Tisci
text:
Riccardo Tisci is an influential Italian fashion designer born in 1974. He began his education at the Design Istituto d’Arte Applicata in Cantù, Italy, before moving to London, where he graduated from Central Saint Martins College of Art and Design in 1999. Early in his career, Tisci worked with brands like Puma, Antonio Berardi, and Coccapani before joining Ruffo Research, a company known for launching fashion careers, including that of Sophia Kokosalaki. After his contract with Ruffo Research ended in 2004, he spent time in India developing his own collection, which he debuted in September 2004 during Milan Fashion Week.

In 2005, Tisci was appointed creative director of Givenchy’s haute couture, ready-to-wear, and accessories lines, a role that expanded in 2008 to include menswear and accessories. His tenure at Givenchy was marked by a significant increase in the brand’s turnover, growing six-fold over twelve years. He also designed costumes for Madonna’s Sticky & Sweet Tour in 2008 and later for the tour’s encore in 2009. Tisci’s work at Givenchy was characterized by a modern, romantic, and melancholic aesthetic, often featuring highly stylized runway presentations. In 2010, he included Lea T, a transgender model, in his Fall–Winter collection, reflecting his inclusive approach.

Tisci left Givenchy in 2017 to pursue personal interests. In 2018, he became Burberry’s chief creative officer, succeeding Christopher Bailey. During his time at Burberry, he collaborated with Vivienne Westwood on the Winter 2018 collection and aimed to blend tradition with a darkly gothic modern sensibility. His tenure ended in 2022 when he was replaced by Daniel Lee.

Throughout his career, Tisci has been known for his diverse collaborations. He curated issues of *A Magazine* and *Visionaire*, worked with perfumer François Demachy on *Le Dahlia Noir*, and designed album covers for Jay-Z and Kanye West, including *Watch the Throne* (2011) and singles like "H•A•M" and "Otis." He also dressed Rihanna for her Diamonds World Tour and collaborated with Nike on multiple projects, including the *NikeLab x RT: Training Redefined* collection for the 2016 Olympics. Additionally, he designed costumes for the ballet *Boléro* at the Opéra Garnier in Paris and worked with virtual pop idol Hatsune Miku for a *Vogue* article in 2016.

Tisci is openly gay, and in 2025, he was sued for alleged sexual assault in New York. His close association with Italian model Mariacarla Boscono, who frequently appeared in his runway shows, highlights his connections within the fashion industry. Tisci’s work has left a lasting impact on high fashion, blending romanticism with contemporary edge.

title: Billy Snedden
text:
Sir Billy Mackie Snedden (1926–1987) was a prominent Australian politician who played significant roles in the Liberal Party, serving as its leader from 1972 to 1975, a cabinet minister from 1964 to 1972, and Speaker of the House of Representatives from 1976 to 1983. Born in Perth, Western Australia, on 31 December 1926, he was the youngest of six children in a working-class family of Scottish immigrants. His father, a stonemason, left the family when Snedden was young, forcing his mother to work as a laundress while his siblings supported the household. Snedden left school at 15 and worked as a law clerk before enlisting in the Royal Australian Air Force in 1945. After the war, he studied law at the University of Western Australia, graduating in 1950.

Snedden’s political career began in the early 1950s, when he became the inaugural federal chairman of the Young Liberal Movement. He worked for the Department of Immigration overseas before returning to Australia in 1954 and settling in Melbourne. In 1955, he was elected to the House of Representatives for the seat of Bruce, where he served for nearly three decades. His narrow victory in 1961 was crucial in preventing Labor from winning the election, which would have ended 12 years of Coalition rule.

As a cabinet minister, Snedden held several key portfolios under five prime ministers: Attorney-General (1964–1966), Minister for Immigration (1966–1969), Minister for Labour and National Service (1969–1971), and Treasurer (1971–1972). As Attorney-General, he played a pivotal role in the 1967 referendum that removed discriminatory references to Indigenous Australians from the Constitution. His tenure as Minister for Labour and National Service was marked by controversy due to the unpopular conscription policy for the Vietnam War. In 1971, he became Liberal Party deputy leader and Treasurer under William McMahon.

After the Liberal Party’s defeat in the 1972 election, Snedden succeeded McMahon as party leader, becoming Leader of the Opposition. He led the party to the 1974 election, which Labor won with a reduced majority. His leadership was challenged by Malcolm Fraser, who succeeded him in 1975. Snedden then retired to the backbench before being elected Speaker of the House in 1976, a position he held for nearly seven years. Known for his impartiality, he sought to strengthen the Speaker’s role and restore its dignity by wearing traditional wig and gown. His tenure was marked by efforts to enhance parliamentary independence, including securing separate funding for Parliament. One notable incident occurred in 1982 when he refused to suspend Bob Hawke for calling Prime Minister Malcolm Fraser a "liar," defying Fraser’s demands for punishment.

Snedden resigned from Parliament in 1983, adhering to Westminster conventions that Speakers should not remain in politics. In retirement, he served as chairman of the Melbourne Football Club and on the board of the Victorian Football League. His death in 1987 under unusual circumstances—linked to the ex-girlfriend of his son—drew significant public attention. Snedden’s career spanned military service, law, and politics, leaving a lasting impact on Australian governance.

title: Esteban Espíndola
text:
Esteban Ezequiel Espíndola López is an Argentine professional footballer born on 22 March 1992, who plays as a centre-back. He began his career with River Plate, one of Argentina's most prominent clubs, in the Primera División. Although he was included in the squad on two occasions during league matches, he did not make his debut until the 2012–13 Copa Argentina, where he played against Estudiantes. His early career was marked by limited opportunities, as he appeared only three times for Atlético de Rafaela during the 2013–14 season after joining the club on loan. This lack of playing time continued after he moved to Nueva Chicago in the Primera B Nacional in 2014, where he failed to make any appearances before leaving the club less than a year later. In February 2015, he joined another Primera División team, Belgrano, where he gradually established himself, making twenty appearances across all competitions over his first three seasons.

In August 2017, Espíndola was loaned to San Martín in the Primera B Nacional, where he played a key role in the team's promotion to the top division. His tenure at San Martín was followed by a short stint with Olimpia in Honduras, where he appeared in fourteen matches before terminating his contract in December 2018. The following January, he signed for Racing de Córdoba in Argentina's Torneo Federal A, but the club suffered relegation during his time there. He then returned to Honduras, this time joining Marathón, and scored his first senior career goal in a 1–1 draw against his former club, Olimpia. Further goals against Honduras Progreso and Real Sociedad preceded his move to Costa Rica, where he signed a one-year contract with Saprissa in July 2020. At Saprissa, he was assigned the number five shirt.

On the international stage, Espíndola represented Argentina at youth levels, including the U15 and U17 teams. He made three appearances for the U17 squad at the 2009 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Nigeria, scoring a penalty in a group stage match against Germany. His club career includes winning the U-20 Copa Libertadores with River Plate in 2012 and the Liga FPD with Saprissa in the Clausura 2021. As of February 2021, his career statistics reflect a journey marked by both challenges and achievements, with his most notable performances coming later in his professional journey, particularly in Honduras and Costa Rica. His ability to adapt and contribute at different levels of competition underscores his resilience as a footballer.

title: Jamie Dornan
text:
Jamie Dornan is a Northern Irish actor, model, and musician born on May 1, 1982, in Holywood, County Down.
