He grew up in the suburbs of Belfast and faced personal tragedies early in life, including the death of his mother from pancreatic cancer when he was 16 and his father from COVID-19 complications in 2021. His father, an obstetrician, had supported his career, and Dornan has spoken fondly of his encouragement. Dornan has two older sisters—Liesa, who works for Disney, and Jessica, a fashion designer—and is a distant cousin of actress Greer Garson. Raised in a Methodist family, he attended Methodist College Belfast, where he participated in drama and rugby, even playing for the Ulster Rugby under-21 team before a foot-and-mouth disease outbreak ended his potential professional sports career. He briefly attended Teesside University before moving to London in 2002 to pursue acting without formal drama school training.

Dornan began his career as a model in 2001 after appearing on the reality show *Model Behaviour* and signing with Select Model Management. Though initially reluctant, his sisters persuaded him to pursue modeling. He quickly became a sought-after model, working with brands like Hugo Boss, Dior Homme, Calvin Klein, and Dolce & Gabbana. *The New York Times* dubbed him "the Golden Torso," and *Vogue* later ranked him among the "25 Biggest Male Models of All Time." Despite his success, Dornan never walked traditional runways due to his unconventional walk. In parallel, he was a musician, performing in the folk band Sons of Jim until 2008.

His acting career began in 2006 with a role in Sofia Coppola’s *Marie Antoinette*. He struggled initially, facing stigma as a model-turned-actor and enduring numerous audition rejections. His breakthrough came in 2013 with *The Fall*, where he played serial killer Paul Spector opposite Gillian Anderson. His performance earned critical acclaim, an Irish Film and Television Award, and a BAFTA nomination. The role transformed his career, leading to mainstream success.

Dornan gained global recognition as Christian Grey in the *Fifty Shades* film trilogy (2015–2018), which grossed over $1.3 billion but received poor critical reviews. Despite the criticism, he acknowledged the franchise’s impact on his career, opening doors to other projects. In 2016, he starred in the war films *The Siege of Jadotville* and *Anthropoid*, earning further acclaim. He also appeared in *A Private War* (2018), portraying a journalist, and *Belfast* (2021), for which he received a Golden Globe nomination for his role as a working-class father.

Dornan has since expanded into comedy, appearing in *Barb and Star Go to Vista Del Mar* (2021), and leading the BBC thriller *The Tourist* (2022–2024), which became the UK’s most-watched drama of the year. In 2023, he starred in *Heart of Stone* and *A Haunting in Venice*, the latter directed by Kenneth Branagh. Throughout his career, Dornan has balanced commercial and independent projects, earning recognition for his versatility. In 2020, *The Irish Times* ranked him among Ireland’s 50 greatest film actors.

title: Franck Ribéry
text:
Franck Ribéry, born on 7 April 1983 in Boulogne-sur-Mer, France, is a former professional footballer widely regarded as one of the greatest wingers of his generation. Known for his pace, skill, and precise passing, Ribéry's career spanned over two decades, with stints in France, Turkey, Germany, and Italy. His distinctive facial scars, a result of a childhood car accident, became a recognizable part of his image.

Ribéry began his football journey at FC Conti Boulogne at age six, later moving to Lille's youth academy. However, academic and behavioral issues led to his release, and he briefly worked as a construction worker. He rejoined US Boulogne in 1999, where his performances earned him a move to Metz in 2004. After impressing in Ligue 1, he joined Galatasaray in 2005, winning the Turkish Cup in his only season there. His move to Marseille in 2005 was controversial, as he left Galatasaray citing unpaid wages and threats, leading to a legal battle resolved in his favor by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

At Marseille, Ribéry became a star, helping the club reach consecutive Coupe de France finals and earning the UNFP Young Player of the Year award. In 2007, he joined Bayern Munich for a then-club-record €25 million, forming a legendary partnership with Arjen Robben, dubbed "Robbery." During his 12 seasons at Bayern, he won nine Bundesliga titles, six DFB-Pokals, one Champions League, and one FIFA Club World Cup, including a treble in 2013. His performances earned him the 2013 UEFA Best Player in Europe Award and a Ballon d'Or nomination alongside Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo.

Ribéry's international career with France included 81 caps, two World Cups (2006, 2010), and two European Championships (2008, 2012). He received three French Player of the Year awards and was the first player to win both French and German Footballer of the Year honors. After leaving Bayern in 2019, he played for Fiorentina and Salernitana before retiring in 2022. He later became a technical collaborator for Salernitana.

Throughout his career, Ribéry's speed, dribbling, and creativity made him a standout winger, leaving a lasting legacy in European football.

title: Gretl Braun
text:
Gretl Braun, born Margarete Berta "Gretl" Berlinghoff (née Braun), was the youngest of three daughters of schoolteacher Friedrich "Fritz" Braun and seamstress Franziska "Fanny" Kronberger. She was born on 31 August 1915 and grew up in Munich. After dropping out of secondary school at 16, she worked as a clerk for Heinrich Hoffmann’s photography company, where her sister Eva also worked. Hitler provided the sisters with a three-bedroom apartment in Munich in 1935 and a villa in Bogenhausen the following year. Their father disapproved of this arrangement and wrote to Hitler to protest. Gretl was an enthusiastic photographer and attended the Bavarian State School of Photography in 1943.

Gretl frequently joined Eva at Hitler’s Berghof retreat in the Obersalzberg, where she contrasted with the formal atmosphere by smoking, flirting with staff, and engaging in lively behavior. Hitler’s secretary, Traudl Junge, recalled that Hitler disapproved of smoking but could not persuade Gretl to quit. Gretl briefly had a romantic interest in Hitler’s SS adjutant, Fritz Darges, but he was dismissed and sent to the Eastern Front after making an insubordinate remark in 1944.

On 3 June 1944, Gretl married SS-Gruppenführer Hermann Fegelein, Himmler’s liaison officer on Hitler’s staff. The wedding took place at the Mirabell Palace in Salzburg, with Hitler, Himmler, and Martin Bormann as witnesses. Eva organized the ceremony, and a three-day celebration followed at the Berghof and the Eagle’s Nest. The marriage helped legitimize Eva’s presence at public events, though Fegelein was known for his extramarital affairs. Shortly after the wedding, the Normandy Landings occurred, effectively ending the social life at the Berghof. By January 1945, Gretl and Eva had moved to Berlin, but Gretl later returned to Berchtesgaden, while Eva stayed in the capital. In April 1945, Gretl was pregnant and at the Berghof when her husband was arrested for desertion. Hitler, furious over Himmler’s attempted surrender negotiations, ordered Fegelein executed. Two days later, Hitler married Eva, and the couple died by suicide on 30 April 1945. Gretl gave birth to a daughter, Eva Barbara (named in memory of her sister), on 5 May 1945.

After the war, Gretl changed her name and married Kurt Berlinghoff in 1954. Her daughter took the name Evi Fegelein-Berlinghoff. Gretl lived quietly until her death on 10 October 1987 in Steingaden, Bavaria, at the age of 72. She was buried under the name Gretl Berlinghoff, alongside her daughter, her second husband (who died in 1999), and her sister Ilse Braun. Despite her close ties to the Nazi regime, Gretl avoided significant post-war repercussions and lived out her life in relative obscurity.

title: Ushoshi Sengupta
text:
Ushoshi Sengupta is an Indian actress, model, and beauty pageant titleholder who gained recognition after winning the first edition of *I Am She – Miss Universe India*. Born in Kolkata, she comes from a family with a background in the Indian Air Force, as her father served as an official in the force. Sengupta attended Kendriya Vidyalaya, Ballygunje, in Kolkata, where she demonstrated a strong aptitude for mathematics and was even offered a scholarship to study engineering. However, she chose to pursue liberal arts instead and later completed her bachelor's degree in Humanities from St. Xavier's College, Kolkata, affiliated with the University of Calcutta. Before entering the pageant world, she worked as a professional model.

Her breakthrough moment came when she won the title of *I Am She – Miss Universe India*, a national beauty pageant organized by Tantra Entertainment Private Limited in collaboration with former Miss Universe Sushmita Sen. This victory earned her the opportunity to represent India at the *Miss Universe 2010* competition, held at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas, Nevada, on 23 August 2010. Among 83 international delegates, Sengupta competed for the prestigious crown, which ultimately went to Ximena Navarrete of Mexico.

In addition to her pageant success, Sengupta ventured into acting, making her debut in the Bengali film industry with *Egoler Chokh*, released in August 2016. The film was directed by Arindam Sil, marking the beginning of her career in cinema. Beyond her professional achievements, Sengupta’s journey highlights her transition from academia and modeling to pageantry and acting, showcasing her versatility and ambition. Her participation in *Miss Universe 2010* remains a notable highlight of her career, further solidifying her presence in the entertainment and pageant industries.

title: Patricia Cladis
text:
Patricia Elisabeth Cladis was a Canadian-American physicist born on July 13, 1937, in Shanghai. She attended Little Flower Academy in Vancouver, graduating in 1955. Cladis earned her B.A. in combined Honours Mathematics and Physics from the University of British Columbia in 1959, followed by an M.A. in physics from the University of Toronto in 1960. She completed her PhD in physics, specializing in superconductivity, at the University of Rochester in 1968.

After her master’s degree, Cladis worked briefly as a meteorologist for Transport Canada before becoming a programmer-analyst at KCS Ltd. in 1962. She then joined Western Connecticut State University as an assistant professor of physics in 1963. From 1964 to 1968, she worked as a research assistant at the University of Rochester while completing her doctoral studies. Following her PhD, she moved to Paris, where she conducted research at the University of Paris (Orsay) with the Orsay Liquid Crystal Group, collaborating with Professor Pierre-Gilles de Gennes, who later won the Nobel Prize in 1991 for his work on liquid crystals.

In 1972, Cladis joined Bell Labs in Murray Hill, New Jersey, as a research physicist, where she continued her work on liquid crystals for 25 years. Her research focused on the material properties and processing of liquid crystals, particularly their defects, the discovery of the reentrant nematic phase, and phase transitions and pattern formation. In 1997, she founded Advanced Liquid Crystal Technologies in Summit, New Jersey, a company specializing in physical and biological research.

Cladis held visiting academic appointments at several institutions, including Northwestern University, where she received the Edith Kreeger Wolf Distinguished Professor award from the Gender and Sexuality Studies department in recognition of her contributions to her field. She also held positions at the University of Paris (Orsay), Ecole Pratique des Hautes Etudes, École Normale Supérieure, Weizmann Institute of Science, University of Duisburg-Essen, and University of Bayreuth.

Throughout her career, Cladis received numerous honors, including being named a fellow of the American Physical Society in 1983 and receiving a Guggenheim Fellowship in 1993. She was also awarded the Humboldt Prize, which recognizes lifetime achievements and fosters international scientific collaboration. Additionally, she served on the Editorial Board of *Liquid Crystals* from 1986 to 1993 and was a board member of the International Liquid Crystal Society.

Cladis was a prolific researcher, authoring or co-authoring over 130 publications and editing several books. Her most notable work was *Spatio-temporal patterns in nonequilibrium complex systems*, published in 1995, which explored patterns in complex fluids, including polymers. Liquid crystals, a key focus of her research, have applications in technologies like LCD displays.

Cladis passed away on July 3, 2017, in Summit, New Jersey. Her contributions to liquid crystal physics and her pioneering work in the field left a lasting impact on the scientific community.

title: Idris Elba
text:
Idris Elba, born Idrissa Akuna Elba on 6 September 1972 in the London Borough of Hackney, is an accomplished English actor and musician. Raised in Hackney and East Ham, he shortened his name to "Idris" during his school years in Canning Town, where he first became involved in acting. His parents, Winston Elba (a Sierra Leonean worker at Ford Dagenham) and Eve (a Ghanaian woman), moved to London after marrying in Sierra Leone. Elba began his career in acting after securing a role through an advertisement in *The Stage*, which led to his first agent. In 1986, he started DJing with an uncle’s wedding business and soon launched his own DJ company under the moniker "Big Driis." After studying at Barking and Dagenham College, he won a grant from the Prince’s Trust to join the National Youth Music Theatre. To support himself early in his career, he worked various odd jobs, including tire-fitting and night shifts at Ford Dagenham, while continuing to audition for roles.

Elba’s acting career began with minor roles, including crime reconstructions for *Crimewatch* and a BBC children’s drama, *The Boot Street Band* (1994). His breakthrough came with *Bramwell* (1995), where he played a petty thief named Charlie Carter. He appeared in several British television series, including *The Bill*, *Absolutely Fabulous*, and *Silent Witness*, before moving to New York City. There, he played Achilles in a stage production of *Troilus and Cressida* (2001). His career took off with the role of Stringer Bell in *The Wire* (2002–2004), which gained him significant recognition in the U.S. He also starred in the 2003 Jamaican film *One Love*.

From 2005 onward, Elba’s career expanded with roles in *Sometimes in April* (2005), *The Office* (2009), and *The No. 1 Ladies’ Detective Agency* (2008). His most iconic role, however, came with *Luther* (2010–2019), where he portrayed DCI John Luther. His performance earned him a Golden Globe Award and multiple Emmy nominations. On film, he appeared in *American Gangster* (2007), *Obsessed* (2009), *Prometheus* (2012), and *Pacific Rim* (2013). He also played Nelson Mandela in *Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom* (2013), earning a Golden Globe nomination. In 2015, he starred in *Beasts of No Nation*, winning a SAG Award and receiving BAFTA and Golden Globe nominations.

Elba joined the Marvel Cinematic Universe as Heimdall in *Thor* (2011) and its sequels, as well as the DC Extended Universe in *The Suicide Squad* (2021) as Bloodsport. He also lent his voice to animated films like *Zootopia*, *The Jungle Book*, and *Finding Dory* (2016), and later portrayed Knuckles the Echidna in the *Sonic the Hedgehog* sequels (2022–2024). His directorial debut was *Yardie* (2018). Beyond acting, Elba is a musician, performing as a DJ and releasing music under the name "DJ Big Driis." He has collaborated with artists like Jay-Z, Pharoahe Monch, and Macklemore & Ryan Lewis.

In 2016, Elba was named one of *Time*’s 100 Most Influential People in the World. His films have grossed over $9.8 billion globally, making him one of the top 20 highest-grossing actors. He co-owns the Formula E team Kiro Race Co. and runs the production company Green Door Pictures, which has developed projects like *Dantai* for Crunchyroll. In 2024, he launched 22Summers, a new production company, and received approval to establish a film studio in Zanzibar. Additionally, he has ventured into gaming, voicing a character in *Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty* (2023).

Elba’s career spans acting, music, and production, solidifying his status as a versatile and influential figure in entertainment.

title: Daniel Ek
text:
Daniel Georg Ek is a Swedish entrepreneur and technologist best known as the co-founder and CEO of the music streaming service Spotify. Born on 21 February 1983 in Stockholm, Ek grew up in the Rågsved district. He graduated from IT-Gymnasiet in Sundbyberg in 2002 and briefly attended the KTH Royal Institute of Technology before dropping out to pursue a career in technology. Ek began developing websites and open-source technologies at the age of fourteen and later worked at Jajja, a search engine optimization firm. He held a senior role at the Nordic auction company Tradera, which was acquired by eBay in 2006, and served as the CTO of Stardoll, a browser-based game and fashion community. Ek also founded Advertigo, an online advertising company, which he sold to TradeDoubler in 2006. After briefly serving as CEO of μTorrent, he retired briefly before founding Spotify in 2006 with Martin Lorentzon, his former colleague at TradeDoubler.

The idea for Spotify originated in 2002 after the shutdown of Napster and the rise of Kazaa, illegal peer-to-peer music services. Ek believed that the only way to combat piracy was to create a legal service that was superior to illegal alternatives while compensating the music industry. Spotify launched in 2008 as a peer-to-peer distribution model, later switching to a server-client model in 2014. By 2019, the platform had 217 million active users and had raised over $2.5 billion in venture funding. In 2017, Ek was named the most powerful person in the music industry by *Billboard*. In 2022, he invested an additional $50 million in Spotify, citing the company’s strong growth trajectory.

Beyond Spotify, Ek co-founded Neko Health in 2018, a medical technology company specializing in non-invasive full-body scanning using AI. The company received €30 million in initial funding from Ek and later secured additional investment. He also established Prima Materia, an investment firm focusing on European "moonshots," alongside Spotify investor Shakil Khan. Prima Materia has backed companies like Helsing, a defense technology firm where Ek serves as chairman. In 2025, Prima Materia led a €600 million investment in Helsing.

Ek has been outspoken on political and industry-related issues. In 2016, he and Lorentzon wrote an open letter to the Swedish government, warning that high taxes and restrictive housing policies could force Spotify to relocate. He has also commented on the music industry, arguing in 2020 that artists must engage continuously with fans rather than relying on occasional album releases. His remarks sparked backlash, with musicians like Dee Snider and Mike Mills criticizing Spotify’s low artist payouts. In 2024, a tweet about the "cost of creating content being close to zero" drew further criticism, leading Ek to clarify that he did not intend to devalue creative work.

In his personal life, Ek married Sofia Levander in 2016, with Bruno Mars performing and Chris Rock officiating. The couple has two daughters. A lifelong Arsenal fan, Ek expressed interest in purchasing the football club in 2021, making an offer of approximately £1.8 billion, which was rejected. He was portrayed by Edvin Endre in the 2022 Netflix miniseries *The Playlist*.

Ek’s influence in the music industry has been significant, but his comments on artist compensation and the future of music have drawn criticism, particularly from musicians who argue that streaming platforms like Spotify undervalue their work. Despite the controversy, Spotify remains a dominant force in digital music distribution.

title: Joseph Michael Linsner
text:
Joseph Michael Linsner is an American comic book writer and artist, best known for creating the mature-audiences supernatural character Dawn, a lingerie-wearing occult figure. Born on December 13, 1968, in Queens, New York, Linsner grew up as one of three brothers and lost his father at the age of 14. His early artistic influences included Batman, the X-Men, Conan the Barbarian, and the pinup artist Alberto Vargas, while later inspirations came from creators like Alan Moore, Pat Mills, and David Cronenberg.

Linsner introduced his signature character, Dawn, in *Cry for Dawn*, a nine-issue series self-published by Cry for Dawn Productions in 1989. The company dissolved in 1993, after which Linsner moved Dawn to Sirius Entertainment, where the character appeared in various limited series and one-shots from 1995 to 2000. His work on Dawn established his reputation for illustrations of female characters, often characterized by a strong, sensual aesthetic.

Linsner's career expanded into mainstream comics when he drew the cover of *Justice League Quarterly* #13 in 1993. He later contributed to Marvel Comics, including the one-shot *Killraven* #1 (2001), covers for the *Mystique* series, and interior artwork for the *Wolverine-Black Cat* series *Claws* (2006) and its sequel *Wolverine & Black Cat: Claws 2* (2011). His cover art also appeared for Topps Comics, Dark Horse Comics, and others. Notably, he began working with Dynamite Entertainment in 2007, becoming one of their most prolific cover artists, particularly for titles featuring licensed characters like Red Sonja, Vampirella, and Bettie Page.

Linsner has also been involved in charitable projects, such as *I Love New York* (2002), a self-published comic benefiting the American Red Cross after the September 11 attacks. His art was featured in *The Art of Joseph Michael Linsner* (2003) and *Our Gods Wear Spandex* (2007). He has supported The Hero Initiative, a nonprofit organization aiding comic book creators in need.

In 2013, Linsner faced controversy when he accused his former assistant, Eva Hopkins, of selling his original artwork without permission. Hopkins denied the claims, leading to a public dispute. Despite this, Linsner continued his prolific career, working on titles like *Dawn/Vampirella* (2014–2015) and contributing to *Harley Quinn* (2015–2017) at DC Comics.

Linsner has received recognition for his work, including a 1997 Eisner Award nomination for Best Painter/Digital Artist, an Inkpot Award at the 2007 San Diego Comic-Con, and appearances as a guest of honor at the 2008 Toronto Comic Con. He is married to Kristina Deak-Linsner.

His bibliography spans numerous titles, including *Dawn* series, *Dark Ivory* (co-created with Hopkins), and collaborations with major publishers. Linsner's contributions to the comic industry, both as a creator and a cover artist, have solidified his reputation in the field.

title: Julian Jarrold
text:
Julian Edward Peter Jarrold, born in 1961 in Norwich, is a BAFTA-nominated British film and television director with a distinguished career in both mediums. He comes from a notable background, being the only son of Peter Jarrold and Juliet Pollard, and a descendant of the Huguenot family that founded the well-known Jarrolds of Norwich in 1823. He attended Gresham's School in Holt before studying at Trinity & All Saints College in Leeds. In 2005, he married Jo Higgins, and the couple resides in Primrose Hill, London.

Jarrold's directing career began with the 1999 adaptation of *Great Expectations*, starring Ioan Gruffudd. The film was praised for its restrained, unromanticized portrayal of the characters, with critics noting that Jarrold avoided maudlin or overly sentimental performances. In 2006, he directed *Kinky Boots*, a film that became widely popular in its television showings. While the *Chicago Tribune* found it relatively lightweight, it was also described as effortlessly well-made and occasionally moving. The following year, *Becoming Jane*, his adaptation of Jane Austen’s life, was released. Critics lauded the film’s wit and technical achievements, particularly its long tracking shots and clever use of focus.

In 2008, Jarrold directed the first film adaptation of Evelyn Waugh’s *Brideshead Revisited*, a novel previously considered unfilmable. The production starred Hayley Atwell, Matthew Goode, Emma Thompson, and Michael Gambon. Jarrold acknowledged the daunting task of adapting such a revered work, noting that while some fans questioned the necessity, he aimed to introduce the story to a new generation. The *Daily Telegraph* praised the film’s grand period details, such as Rolls-Royces and sculpted fireplaces, while also noting Jarrold’s ability to prevent the film from becoming overly glossy.

In 2013, Jarrold received his first Emmy nomination for *The Girl*, an HBO film. He also directed *Exit 147*, a serial killer film produced by Mandalay Vision, with Taylor Kitsch starring as a sadistic sheriff. Later, in 2015, he directed *A Royal Night Out* for Ecosse Films, a film released in May of that year. Another Emmy nomination followed for *Red Riding 1974*, part of a critically acclaimed crime trilogy starring Andrew Garfield, Sean Bean, and Rebecca Hall. The film’s gritty Super 16 cinematography and dense atmosphere were praised, with critics noting its immersive, noir-style portrayal of crime and terror in 1970s Yorkshire.

In 2023, Jarrold’s series *The Good Mothers* won the best series award at the Berlin International Festival. Beyond his directing work, he has been involved in the Norwich Film Festival, serving as a judge in 2016 and later becoming its patron in 2017. His filmography includes both directing and producing credits, with early work such as the 1988 TV mini-series *The Other Side of Midnight*, presented by Tony Wilson. Jarrold’s contributions to British cinema and television have been marked by a blend of period drama, crime thrillers, and adaptations of classic literature, earning him recognition and critical acclaim throughout his career.

title: Kari Matchett
text:
Kari Matchett is a Canadian actress with a diverse career spanning film, television, and theater. Born in Spalding, Saskatchewan, she attended high school in Lethbridge, Alberta, before pursuing acting at the National Theatre School in Montreal and the Moscow Theatre School. Early in her career, she honed her craft at the Stratford Shakespeare Festival in Ontario, performing there for three years.

Matchett’s first major television role in Canada was on *The Rez*, but she gained wider recognition as Colleen Blessed in the series *Power Play* (1998–2000). Her work on *A Nero Wolfe Mystery* (2001–2002) alongside Timothy Hutton earned her a recurring role as Lily Rowan. She also appeared in *Wonderfalls* as Beth, the bisexual love interest of the main character’s sister. In film, she took on roles in dramas like *Angel Eyes* (2001) and science fiction thrillers such as *Cube 2: Hypercube* (2002). Her performance in *Blue Murder* (2004) as Detective Elaine Bender earned her a Gemini Award for her earlier guest appearance in 2001.

Throughout the mid-2000s, Matchett appeared in a variety of television projects, including the Syfy miniseries *Five Days to Midnight* (2003) with Timothy Hutton, the alien invasion series *Invasion* (2005), and the drama *Intimate Stranger* (2006). She also starred in *Civic Duty* (2006) alongside Peter Krause. In 2007, she joined the cast of *24* as Lisa Miller and later played Skye Wexler, the chief of emergency medicine, in *ER* (2007–2008). She also appeared in *Starz*’s *Crash* (2008–2009) as Jules, the daughter of Dennis Hopper’s character. From 2010 to 2014, she had a leading role as Joan Campbell in the USA Network series *Covert Affairs*.

In addition to her television work, Matchett has appeared in notable films, including *The Tree of Life* (2011), directed by Terrence Malick, which won the Palme d’Or at the Cannes Film Festival. In 2016, she starred in *Maudie* with Ethan Hawke. Most recently, in 2023, she took on a recurring role as U.S. President Michelle Travers in the Netflix series *The Night Agent*.

Matchett’s career reflects her versatility, as she has worked in both high-profile Hollywood productions and independent films, while maintaining a strong presence in television. Her ability to take on diverse roles—from political leaders to complex dramatic characters—has solidified her reputation as a respected actress in the entertainment industry.

title: Johann Christian von Engel
text:
Johann Christian von Engel (1770–1814) was an Austrian historian who made significant contributions to the study of Ukrainian, Romanian, Hungarian, Croatian, and German history. Born in Leutschau (now Levoča, Slovakia), which was then part of the Kingdom of Hungary under Habsburg rule, Engel received his education at the University of Göttingen, where he studied under prominent scholars such as Heyne and Schlözer. His works were highly regarded in his time, serving as valuable sources of historical knowledge and scholarship. Engel is credited with being the first to establish a solid scholarly foundation for the histories of Hungary, Ukraine, and the Danubian principalities. In recognition of his contributions, he was ennobled in 1812.

Among his most important works is *Die Geschichte der Ukraine und der ukrainische Kosaken, wie auch der Königreiche Halitsch-Wladimir* (1796), which provided a comprehensive history of Ukraine, the Ukrainian Cossacks, and the Kingdom of Halych-Volodymyr. This was followed by his *Geschichte des ungarischen Reiches und seine Nebenländer* (1797–1804), a five-volume history of imperial Hungary and its neighboring lands. Another notable work is *Geschichte der Moldau und Walachey* (1804), which focused on the history of Moldavia and Wallachia. His final major work, *Geschichte des Königreichs Ungarn*, was published posthumously in 1814, also spanning five volumes. These works were foundational in their fields, offering detailed and systematic accounts of the regions they covered.

Engel’s scholarship was characterized by meticulous research and a commitment to presenting historical events in a structured, evidence-based manner. His writings were particularly influential in the early 19th century, providing scholars and readers with authoritative accounts of Eastern and Central European history. The article notes that his works were considered "treasure houses of knowledge and scholarship" during his lifetime, demonstrating their enduring value.

The article also mentions that the text incorporates information from a 1920 edition of the *Encyclopedia Americana*, which further attests to von Engel’s lasting impact on historical studies. His career as a historian was marked by a dedication to uncovering and presenting the histories of regions that were often overlooked or poorly documented at the time. His works remain significant as early contributions to the historiography of Eastern Europe, particularly in the study of Ukraine, Hungary, and the Danubian principalities. Von Engel’s legacy endures in the field of historical research, where his writings continue to be referenced as foundational sources.

title: Carol Dweck
text:
Carol Susan Dweck, born on October 17, 1946, is an American psychologist and professor at Stanford University, where she holds the Lewis and Virginia Eaton Professorship in Psychology. She is best known for her research on motivation and the concept of "mindset," which explores how people’s beliefs about intelligence and ability influence their behavior and success. Dweck has had an extensive academic career, previously teaching at the University of Illinois, Harvard, and Columbia before joining Stanford in 2004. She has received numerous accolades, including election to the National Academy of Sciences in 2012 and the Yidan Prize for Education Research in 2017, which included a $3.9 million award.

Dweck’s interest in mindset was partly shaped by her early experiences in school. As a child, she attended a Brooklyn elementary school where students were ranked by IQ, and high-achieving students received special privileges. This environment made her reluctant to take risks, fearing she might lose her reputation as one of the smartest students. She later graduated from Barnard College in 1967 and earned her Ph.D. in psychology from Yale in 1972.

Her research focuses on how people’s beliefs about intelligence and ability—whether they see them as fixed or developable—affect their motivation and performance. Dweck introduced the concept of "implicit theories of intelligence" in a 1988 paper, later popularized in her 2006 book *Mindset: The New Psychology of Success*. She argues that people can be divided into two broad categories: those with a "fixed mindset," who believe intelligence and talent are innate and unchangeable, and those with a "growth mindset," who believe abilities can be developed through effort, learning, and perseverance. Dweck emphasizes that a growth mindset fosters resilience, as individuals see failure as an opportunity to learn rather than a reflection of their fixed abilities. However, she clarifies that a growth mindset is not just about effort alone but also about recognizing current limitations and working to improve them.

Dweck’s work has faced criticism, particularly regarding the replicability of her findings. Some researchers, like Timothy Bates of Edinburgh University, have struggled to replicate her results, leading to debates about the robustness of her theories. Additionally, critics argue that the mindset concept has been oversimplified in educational settings, sometimes leading to grading students on their attitudes rather than their academic progress. A 2019 large-scale study in England found no significant impact of growth mindset training on literacy or numeracy scores, raising questions about its practical application.

Despite these criticisms, Dweck’s work has been widely influential. She has published numerous academic papers and books, including *Self-Theories: Their Role in Motivation, Personality, and Development* (2000) and *Mindset: How You Can Fulfill Your Potential* (2012). Her research has been cited in journals like *Psychological Science* and *Nature*, and she continues to refine her theories, including her 2017 paper on a unified theory of motivation, personality, and development.

Dweck is married to David Goldman, a national theater director and critic. She has been recognized with multiple awards, including the American Psychological Association’s Distinguished Scientific Contribution Award in 2011 and the Association for Psychological Science’s William James Fellow designation in 2020. Her contributions to psychology and education have made her a prominent figure in the study of motivation and learning.

title: Ted Thompson
text:
Ted Thompson was a significant figure in the NFL as both a player and an executive, leaving a lasting impact on the Green Bay Packers. Born on January 17, 1953, and passing away on January 20, 2021, Thompson played a crucial role in the league for over four decades. He began his career as a linebacker and special teams player for the Houston Oilers from 1975 to 1984, where he played 146 of 147 games, showcasing his durability. His college career at Southern Methodist University was notable for his three-year stint as a starter, seven interceptions, and his dual role as a team captain and placekicker in his senior year. In a 1980 game, he even converted four extra-point attempts as an emergency kicker.

Thompson's front office career began in 1992 when he was hired by the Green Bay Packers as a scout. Over the next seven years, he rose through the ranks, eventually becoming the director of player personnel. During his tenure, the Packers advanced to the playoffs six times, winning Super Bowl XXXI in 1997. In 1999, he joined the Seattle Seahawks as vice president of football operations, a role he held until 2004. Under his direction, the Seahawks made two playoff appearances, and many of the players he acquired, such as Shaun Alexander and Darrell Jackson, contributed to the team's 2005 Super Bowl run.

In 2005, Thompson returned to the Packers as general manager, a position he held until 2017. His first major decision was to release several key players to address the team's salary cap issues, a move that initially led to a 4–12 record in 2005. However, his most notable draft pick that year was quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who would later become a franchise cornerstone. Despite early struggles, Thompson's 2006 offseason moves, including signing Charles Woodson and drafting A. J. Hawk, set the foundation for a strong 2007 season where the Packers finished 13–3 and reached the NFC Championship. His strategic drafting and free-agent signings earned him the Sporting News NFL Executive of the Year award in 2008.

Thompson's tenure was not without controversy, particularly in 2008 when he faced backlash for his handling of Brett Favre's unretirement. Favre was eventually traded to the New York Jets, a move that sparked debate but ultimately allowed Rodgers to take over as the starter. Thompson's focus on rebuilding through the draft paid off in 2009 with the selection of B. J. Raji and Clay Matthews, two Pro Bowl players. The Packers' 2010 season culminated in a Super Bowl XLV victory, making Thompson one of the few executives to win a Super Bowl as both a player and an executive.

In later years, Thompson continued to prioritize the draft, selecting key players like Randall Cobb in 2011 and dedicating the 2012 offseason to improving the defense. Despite some criticisms, his philosophy of building through the draft and maintaining a strong salary cap structure remained consistent. He was re-signed to a contract extension in 2011, recognizing his contributions to the team's success. Thompson's health declined in his later years, and he passed away in early 2021 after revealing he had an autonomic disorder in 2019. His legacy in the NFL, particularly with the Packers, is marked by two Super Bowl titles and a commitment to long-term team success.

title: Leo Kokubo
text:
Leo Brian Kokubo (小久保 玲央 ブライアン, Kokubo Reo Buraian) is a Japanese professional footballer born on 23 January 2001. He is currently a goalkeeper for the Belgian team Sint-Truiden. Kokubo has a diverse background, being born in Japan to a Nigerian father and a Japanese mother. His international career began with the Japan youth national teams, where he represented the U16, U18, and U23 squads.

One of the highlights of Kokubo’s career came on 4 April 2024, when he was called up to the Japan U23 squad for the 2024 AFC U-23 Asian Cup. In the tournament’s final, he played a crucial role in Japan’s victory over Uzbekistan, saving a penalty from Umarali Rakhmonaliev in stoppage time. This save secured Japan’s 1–0 win, marking their second AFC U-23 Asian Cup title in history. For his outstanding performance, Kokubo was named "Man of the Match" in the final.

Before his time in Belgium, Kokubo played for Benfica, where he contributed to the team’s success in the 2023 Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira. This domestic trophy win was one of his notable achievements during his time with the Portuguese club.

Kokubo’s career statistics, as of 15 February 2025, reflect his progress as a professional goalkeeper. His contributions to both club and country highlight his talent and potential in the sport. With his mixed heritage and international experience, he represents a unique and promising figure in modern football. His heroics in the 2024 AFC U-23 Asian Cup final, in particular, cemented his reputation as a reliable and clutch performer under pressure.

title: Grant Bowler
text:
Grant Bowler, born on 18 July 1968 in Auckland, New Zealand, is a New Zealand-Australian actor and television presenter with a career spanning film, television, theatre, and reality TV. He moved to Australia as a child and was raised in Brisbane. After graduating from the National Institute of Dramatic Art, Bowler began his acting career in theatre, working extensively with the Bell Shakespeare Company, which was originally founded by John Bell.

Bowler's television career took off in 1993 when he landed the role of Constable Wayne Patterson in the Australian police drama *Blue Heelers*, a part he played until 1996. Following that, he appeared in several Australian TV series, including *Pacific Drive* (1996), *Medivac* (1996–1998), *Always Greener*, and *Stingers*, as well as the miniseries *On the Beach* and the ABC series *Something in the Air*. In 2004, he starred in the miniseries *Through My Eyes*, based on the disappearance of Azaria Chamberlain, and had a recurring role in *All Saints* (2004–2005).

In addition to acting, Bowler became a well-known television presenter, hosting the Australian version of *The Mole* from 2000 to 2003. He later transitioned to narration, becoming the voiceover narrator for *Border Security: Australia* on the Seven Network since 2004, a role that expanded to include the Canadian and American versions of the show when they aired in Australia and New Zealand as *Border Security: International*. He also hosted *The Amazing Race Australia* for three seasons, from 2010 to 2013, before being replaced by Beau Ryan in the 2019 revival.

Bowler gained international recognition for his roles in American television series, including *Lost*, where he played Captain Gault in the season four episode "Ji Yeon," and *Ugly Betty*, where he had a recurring role as Connor Owens, a corrupt executive and love interest to the show's villain. In 2009, he appeared in *True Blood* as Cooter, a werewolf. His film credits include *Atlas Shrugged: Part I* (2011), where he portrayed Hank Rearden, as well as *The City of Gardens*, *Killer Elite*, and the biographical TV movie *Liz & Dick* (2012), in which he played Richard Burton opposite Lindsay Lohan’s Elizabeth Taylor. He also starred in *Gallipoli* (2015), a war drama, and appeared in action and sci-fi films such as *Swelter* (2015), *400 Days* (2015), and *Lucky Dog* (2017).

In 2012, Bowler was cast as the lead in the Syfy series *Defiance*, playing Joshua Nolan, a role that further boosted his international profile. He continued to take on diverse roles, including a recurring part in *The Baker and the Beauty* (2020), where he played the Australian father of the lead character.

In his personal life, Bowler was married to Australian actress Roxane Wilson, with whom he had two children, but they separated in 2011 after nine years of marriage. Throughout his career, Bowler has maintained a presence in both Australian and international entertainment, balancing acting with his work as a television host and narrator. His versatility as an actor and his distinctive voice have made him a recognizable figure in the industry.

title: Robert Jennings (rugby league)
text:
Robert Jennings, born on 2 January 1996 in Blacktown, New South Wales, Australia, is a Tongan international rugby league footballer who played as a winger and centre in the National Rugby League (NRL). His parents were born in Tonga, and he also has Fijian and English ancestry. Jennings comes from a rugby-league family, being the younger brother of Sydney Roosters player Michael Jennings and Melbourne Storm player George Jennings, as well as the nephew of former All Black Arthur Jennings. He began his junior football career with the Western City Tigers and Minchinbury Jets before being signed by the Penrith Panthers.

Jennings' early career included playing for the Penrith Panthers' NYC (Under-20s) team in 2014, where he impressed enough to be selected for the Australian Schoolboys team later that year. In 2015, he progressed to the Panthers' New South Wales Cup team. His NRL debut came in Round 7 of the 2015 season against the Gold Coast Titans. He also represented the Junior Kangaroos and the New South Wales Under-20s team in 2015. Despite being contracted with Penrith until the end of 2016, he did not receive any game time in the 2016 NRL season and was released, signing with the South Sydney Rabbitohs for the 2017 season.

At South Sydney, Jennings quickly made an impact, scoring a try and setting up another in his debut against the Manly Warringah Sea Eagles in Round 2 of the 2017 season. In 2018, he had a standout year, scoring a hat-trick against Manly in Round 3 and then four tries in a single game against the Parramatta Eels in Round 14. He finished the 2018 season with 19 tries, establishing himself as a key player for the Rabbitohs.

In 2019, Jennings signed a two-year deal with the Wests Tigers after being released by South Sydney. He made 18 appearances for the Tigers in the 2019 season, but the club finished ninth and missed the finals. In 2020, he was among eight players released by the Tigers.

Jennings returned to the Penrith Panthers in 2021 on a one-year deal, making three appearances during the NRL season, mainly as cover during the State of Origin period. In 2022, he played only four NRL games, spending most of the season with Penrith's NSW Cup team. He contributed to Penrith’s victory in the 2022 NSW Cup Grand Final and also played in their NRL State Championship final win. Later in 2022, he signed a two-year contract with the Dolphins, making his club debut in Round 7 of the 2023 season. He scored two tries in a narrow 28–26 victory over the Gold Coast Titans in Round 8.

At the end of the 2023 NRL season, Jennings' contract with the Dolphins expired, marking the end of his professional rugby league career. In 2025, he signed with the Stanley River Wolves, a local club in Woodford, Queensland, competing in the Sunshine Coast Gympie Rugby League competition. Playing in the second row, he had scored six tries by Round 11 of the 2025 season, continuing to contribute at the community level of the sport.

title: Belisarius
text:
Belisarius (c. 500 – 565) was a legendary military commander of the Byzantine Empire under Emperor Justinian I, renowned for his role in reconquering territories of the former Western Roman Empire. Born around 500, possibly in Germania (modern-day Sapareva Banya, Bulgaria), his early life is shrouded in mystery, but by 526, he had become a senior guardsman in Justinian’s service. He formed a elite bucellarii regiment, a 7,000-strong personal household unit equipped with lances, composite bows, and swords, which became the core of his armies.

Belisarius’ early career was marked by mixed results. In the Iberian War against the Sassanid Persians, he suffered defeats but also demonstrated tactical brilliance, such as at the Battle of Dara in 530, where he dug trenches to lure the Persians into a trap. His defeat at Callinicum later that year, despite numerical superiority, was a setback, but he was later exonerated of blame. His strategic maneuvering and use of deception, such as feigning retreats or negotiating under false pretenses, became hallmarks of his leadership.

A pivotal moment came during the Nika riots of 532, when Justinian’s reforms sparked widespread unrest in Constantinople. Belisarius, alongside Mundus and Narses, crushed the revolt in a bloody massacre, saving Justinian’s rule. This display of loyalty reinforced his standing with the emperor.

In 533, Justinian tasked Belisarius with reconquering the Vandal Kingdom in North Africa. The Vandals, led by King Gelimer, had persecuted Nicene Christians and weakening ties with the Byzantines. Belisarius commanded a force of around 17,000 soldiers, including elite cavalry, infantry, and mercenaries like Huns and Heruls. Despite logistical challenges—such as spoiled water and disease during the voyage—his disciplined leadership ensured morale remained high. Upon reaching Sicily, he learned the Vandals were unprepared for invasion, allowing him to sail directly to Carthage.

The Vandalic War unfolded rapidly. At the Battle of Ad Decimum in September 533, Belisarius defeated the Vandals, forcing Gelimer to flee. He captured Carthage and held it against a siege, though his troops were outnumbered. The decisive Battle of Tricamarum in December 533 saw another Byzantine victory, compelling Gelimer to surrender. The campaign lasted only nine months, a stunning success achieved with limited resources.

Belisarius later turned his attention to Italy, where the Gothic War (535–554) against the Ostrogoths tested his abilities further. Despite being outnumbered, he recaptured Rome in 536 and held it during a prolonged siege, showcasing his defensive tactics. He also repelled Persian invasions, such as at Melantias, and employed deception to lift the siege of Ariminum.

Belisarius’ career was marked by extraordinary achievements despite fluctuating support from Justinian. His ability to adapt to adversity, innovate in battle, and maintain discipline among his troops earned him a reputation as one of history’s greatest commanders. Though his later years were marred by political intrigue and false accusations, his legacy as a master tactician and defender of the empire endures. He died in 565, leaving behind a legacy of reconquest that reshaped the Mediterranean world.

title: Rigoberto Torres
text:
Rigoberto Torres is a sculptor born in Aguadilla, Puerto Rico, in 1960. He moved to New York City as a child, first settling in upper Manhattan before moving to the Bronx. Early in his career, Torres worked in a factory that produced religious statues, where he gained experience in casting and sculpting. This background influenced his later work, which often blends religious iconography with contemporary themes. Torres also identifies as a community-based artist, emphasizing the importance of engaging with and representing local communities in his art.

A significant part of Torres’ career was his collaboration with fellow artist John Ahearn. The two met in 1980, and between 1981 and 1985, they created four notable murals featuring life-sized sculptures of Torres’ neighbors in the Bronx. These murals—*We Are Family*, *Life on Dawson Street*, *Double Dutch*, and *Back to School*—depicted ordinary people in their everyday environments, offering a counterpoint to traditional public monuments that often glorify famous or heroic figures. Their work was displayed in public spaces, attached to buildings or presented as standalone installations, sometimes as part of performance art. Torres and Ahearn often moved their studio to the sidewalk, inviting neighborhood children to participate as subjects or spectators, fostering a sense of community involvement in the artistic process.

The sculptures from this collaboration are known for their humanistic naturalism, emphasizing realism and the individuality of their subjects. *Double Dutch*, created in 1981 and later reproduced in 2010, is one of the most recognized works from this period and is now part of the collection at the Pérez Art Museum Miami. The murals remain installed in various locations throughout the Bronx, including *Life on Dawson Street* at Longwood Avenue and Dawson Street, *We Are Family* on Southern Boulevard, and additional works outside The POINT Community Development Corporation on Garrison Avenue.

In 1990, Torres returned to Puerto Rico for a year-long residency, during which he produced twenty-two works, including *Ruth Fernandez* in 1991. This period marked a shift in his artistic focus, potentially influenced by his reconnection with his roots. Over the years, Torres’ work has been recognized for its ability to transform public spaces into reflections of the people who inhabit them, blending art with social commentary and community engagement. His pieces continue to be celebrated for their accessibility and the way they challenge conventional notions of public monuments.

title: Amr Diab
text:
Amr Abdel Basset Abdel Azeez Diab, born on October 11, 1961, in Port Said, Egypt, is a globally renowned Egyptian singer, composer, and actor. Coming from a middle-class Muslim family from Sharqia Governorate, Diab graduated with a bachelor’s degree in music from the Cairo Academy of Arts in 1986. He has since become one of the most celebrated artists in the Middle East and beyond, holding the title of the best-selling Middle Eastern artist and a Guinness World Record for the most World Music Awards won by a Middle Eastern artist.

Diab’s musical career began in 1983 with his debut album, *Ya Tareeq*. He quickly gained popularity with subsequent albums like *Ghanny Men Albak* (1984), *Hala Hala* (1986), and *Mayyal* (1988), all released under Delta Sound. His international breakthrough came in 1996 with *Nour El Ain*, his first album with Alam El Phan, which won him his first World Music Award. This album also introduced his signature "Mediterranean music" style, blending Western and Middle Eastern rhythms. He later collaborated with artists like Khaled and Angela Dimitriou, further expanding his global reach.

After leaving Alam El Phan in 2004, Diab signed with Rotana Records, releasing successful albums like *Leily Nahary* (2004) and *Kammel Kalamak* (2005). His 2009 album *Wayah* faced controversy when it was leaked online, leading fans to boycott illegal download sites. In 2011, he released the patriotic song *Masr Allet* in response to the Egyptian Revolution, followed by his album *Banadeek Taala*. His 2014 album *Shoft El Ayam* topped the Billboard World Albums chart, making him the first Middle Eastern artist to achieve this. He continued releasing albums, including *Maadi el Nas* (2017) and *Sahran* (2020), while also releasing numerous singles that dominated digital platforms.

Beyond music, Diab ventured into acting, starring in films like *El Afareet* (1989) and *Ice Cream in Gleam* (1992), which was praised by the University of California, Los Angeles. However, he found greater success in music, composing over 97 of his own songs. His music has been featured in international films, including *O Clone* (2001) and *Coco* (2009).

Diab’s personal life includes three marriages. He has a daughter from his first marriage to actress Shereen Reda and three children from his second marriage to Saudi businesswoman Zeina Ashour. He later married actress Dina El Sherbiny in 2018, but they separated in 2020.

Diab has received numerous accolades, including seven World Music Awards, six African Music Awards, and two All Africa Music Awards. His influence extends beyond music, as he has participated in humanitarian efforts, such as his charity campaign *Masry Begad* during the Egyptian Revolution. In 2016, he was recognized by Guinness World Records for his seven World Music Awards.

Throughout his career, Amr Diab has remained a cultural icon, shaping modern Middle Eastern music while achieving unprecedented global success. His innovative style, prolific discography, and dedication to his craft have cemented his legacy as one of the most influential artists of his generation.

title: Mark Murphy (singer)
text:
Mark Murphy (1932–2015) was an influential American jazz singer known for his innovative vocal improvisations and a prolific career spanning over five decades. Born in Syracuse, New York, he grew up in a musical family, with his father directing a church choir and his grandmother and aunt playing the organ. He began piano lessons at seven and was influenced by jazz vocalists like Peggy Lee, Nat "King" Cole, and Ella Fitzgerald, as well as pianist Art Tatum. Murphy graduated from Syracuse University in 1953 with a degree in Music and Drama, where he caught the attention of Sammy Davis Jr., who helped him secure early performance opportunities.

Murphy's professional career began in the mid-1950s, debuting with *Meet Mark Murphy* (1956) on Decca Records, followed by *Let Yourself Go* (1957). Despite modest initial success, he relocated to Los Angeles in 1958, recording for Capitol Records and releasing a minor hit, "This Could Be the Start of Something." Returning to New York in the early 1960s, he recorded for Riverside, including *Rah* (1961), featuring jazz luminaries like Bill Evans and Clark Terry, and *That's How I Love the Blues* (1962). His rendition of "Fly Me to the Moon" in 1963 became a national hit, earning him Down Beat’s New Star of the Year award. Around this time, he was deeply influenced by Miles Davis, striving to emulate Davis’s trumpet phrasing in his vocal style.

In 1963, Murphy moved to London, where he found success performing at Ronnie Scott’s Club and appearing on BBC Radio. He recorded several albums, including *Midnight Mood* (1968), one of his finest works. During this period, he also worked in European television and film, including the 1967 British comedy *Just Like a Woman*. In London, he met his longtime partner, Eddie O’Sullivan.

Returning to the U.S. in 1972, Murphy signed with Muse Records, releasing an album nearly every year for 14 years. Notable works from this era include *Satisfaction Guaranteed* (1979), *Bop for Kerouac* (1981), and *Stolen Moments* (1978), the latter featuring his original lyrics to Oliver Nelson’s composition. He was a longtime admirer of Jack Kerouac, which led to albums blending jazz with readings from *On the Road* and *The Subterraneans*. In 1984, he explored Brazilian music with *Brazil Song (Cancões Do Brasil)*, collaborating with musicians like Antonio Carlos Jobim.

In the 1980s and 1990s, Murphy expanded his musical horizons, recording Ivan Lins’s compositions on *Night Mood* (1987) and *September Ballads* (1988), both Grammy-nominated. His music gained renewed popularity during the acid jazz movement, with DJs like Gilles Peterson introducing his work to younger audiences. He also collaborated with rock and hip-hop artists, including UFO, where he contributed lyrics and rap, bridging jazz with contemporary genres. His 1997 album *Song for the Geese* earned his fifth Grammy nomination.

Later in his career, Murphy recorded for Verve, releasing *Once to Every Heart* (2005) and *Love Is What Stays* (2006), both critically acclaimed. He continued performing internationally into his 80s, appearing at festivals and collaborating with artists like the Tenth & Parker electronica group and the Finnish Five Corners Quintet. His final album, *A Beautiful Friendship: Remembering Shirley Horn* (2013), was a tribute to the late jazz singer. Murphy passed away on October 22, 2015, at the Lillian Booth Actors Home in Englewood, New Jersey, leaving behind a legacy as one of vocal jazz’s most inventive and enduring artists. Throughout his career, he recorded 51 albums as a leader and received four Down Beat awards for Best Male Vocalist, solidifying his status as a major figure in jazz.

title: Walter Model
text:
Otto Moritz Walter Model (1891–1945) was a prominent German military leader during World War II, rising to the rank of *Generalfeldmarschall*. Born in Genthin, Saxony, to a middle-class family, he joined the German Army in 1909, serving in the 52nd Infantry Regiment. His early military career was marked by ambition and a blunt demeanor, traits that defined his leadership style. During World War I, Model fought on the Western Front, earning the Iron Cross, First Class, and later undergoing staff training. He served in various roles, including as a supply officer and adjutant, and participated in key battles such as the First Battle of the Marne and the Battle of Verdun.

In the interwar years, Model remained in the military, adhering to the constraints of the Treaty of Versailles. He married Herta Huyssen in 1921 and had three children. His career advanced steadily, with postings in both staff and command roles. He was influenced by General Fritz von Loßberg’s defensive tactics and later contributed to the development of new military technology, including armor and artillery. By 1938, he had risen to the rank of *Generalmajor* and briefly served in the Oberkommando des Heeres (OKH) before being reassigned to the IV Corps.

When World War II began, Model served as chief of staff for the IV Corps during the invasion of Poland in 1939. Later, as chief of staff for the Sixteenth Army, he played a key role in Germany’s victory in the Battle of France (1940). His next major assignment came in 1941 when he took command of the 3rd Panzer Division for the invasion of the Soviet Union. Model’s aggressive leadership and innovative use of combined arms tactics earned him recognition, though he lacked formal panzer experience. His division was part of Heinz Guderian’s 2nd Panzer Group, contributing to early German advances, including a rapid push toward the Dnieper River.

Model’s defensive warfare expertise became crucial as the war progressed. In 1942, his successes with the Ninth Army brought him to Adolf Hitler’s attention. Hitler, impressed by Model’s tenacity and loyalty, frequently entrusted him with critical defensive operations on the Eastern Front, including as commander of Army Group North, Army Group North Ukraine, and Army Group Centre. His ability to stabilize precarious military situations earned him Hitler’s trust, though their relationship deteriorated later.

In 1944, Model was transferred to the Western Front as commander of OB West and Army Group B. His leadership during the Battle of the Bulge (December 1944–January 1945) was his final major command. Following Germany’s defeat in the Ruhr Pocket, Model’s Army Group B was encircled. Rather than surrender, he committed suicide on 21 April 1945. Known for his relentless defensive tactics and unwavering loyalty to the Nazi regime, Model remains a controversial figure in military history. His career reflects the evolution of German command from early offensive operations to the desperate defensive battles of the war’s final months.

title: Joel Edgerton
text:
Joel Edgerton, born on 23 June 1974 in Blacktown, New South Wales, Australia, is an acclaimed actor and filmmaker known for his work in both Australian and international projects. His parents are Michael Edgerton, a solicitor and property developer, and Marianne van Dort, a Dutch immigrant from The Hague. Edgerton graduated from The Hills Grammar School in 1991 and later attended the Nepean Drama School at the University of Western Sydney before pursuing stage productions, including work with the Sydney Theatre Company.

Edgerton rose to prominence in Australia with his role as Will McGill in the drama series *The Secret Life of Us* (2001–02), for which he won an AACTA Award for Best Lead Actor. He gained international recognition for his portrayal of Owen Lars in *Star Wars: Episode II – Attack of the Clones* (2002) and *Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith* (2005), a role he reprised in the 2022 Disney+ series *Obi-Wan Kenobi*. He also provided the voice of Metal Beak in the animated film *Legend of the Guardians: The Owls of Ga'Hoole* (2010).

His filmography includes a mix of Australian and Hollywood productions. Notable Australian films include *The Square* (2008), *Animal Kingdom* (2010), for which he earned an AACTA Award for Best Supporting Actor, *Wish You Were Here* (2012), and *Felony* (2013). Internationally, he has appeared in *King Arthur* (2004), *Warrior* (2011), *Zero Dark Thirty* (2012), *The Great Gatsby* (2013), *Black Mass* (2015), *Bright* (2017), *The Green Knight* (2021), and *The Boys in the Boat* (2023). He has also starred in television series such as *The Underground Railroad* (2021) and *Dark Matter* (2024).

Edgerton made his directorial debut with *The Gift* (2015), a thriller he also wrote, produced, and starred in, earning critical acclaim and a DGA Award nomination. He continued directing with *Boy Erased* (2018), a film about conversion therapy, and *The King* (2019), an adaptation of Shakespeare’s *Henry V* set in medieval England. In 2021, he starred in *The Stranger*, a crime drama set in Australia, and in 2024, he voiced a character in the animated series *Bluey*.

Beyond acting and filmmaking, Edgerton is involved in philanthropy, serving as an ambassador for The Fred Hollows Foundation, an organization dedicated to restoring sight in developing countries and improving Aboriginal health. He has personally witnessed the foundation’s work in Nepal and advocates for social activism as a counterbalance to the materialism often associated with the entertainment industry.

In his personal life, Edgerton has a brother, Nash, who is a stuntman and filmmaker, and together they are part of the Australian film collective Blue-Tongue Films. He was previously in a relationship with Olympic gold medalist Cathy Freeman from 2003 to 2005. Since 2018, he has been in a relationship with Christine Centenera, editor-in-chief of *Vogue Australia*, and the couple welcomed twins in May 2021.

title: Stan Marple
text:
Stanislaus Henry Marple was a Canadian former professional ice hockey player and coach, known primarily for his contributions to British ice hockey. He played twelve seasons in various British leagues, with his most notable tenure being with the Guildford Flames. His playing career was impacted by the EPL 4 import rule, which limited the number of foreign players teams could field, meaning Marple could only play when other imports were injured. Despite this limitation, he remained a key figure in British hockey, transitioning into coaching and management.

Before his time in the UK, Marple served as the general manager for the University of Alberta’s men’s hockey team, the Alberta Golden Bears, until 1994. Following this, he dedicated the next 13 years to coaching in the United Kingdom, where he made a significant impact. His most prominent role was with the Guildford Flames, where he later became head coach and general manager. Under his leadership, the team achieved considerable success, winning ten titles. His number 3 was retired by the Guildford Flames, a rare honor that underscores his importance to the franchise.

Marple’s coaching record at Guildford was impressive, with 396 wins, 174 losses, and 42 ties and overtime losses. As general manager, he compiled a record of 213 wins and 55 losses. These statistics highlight his effectiveness in both roles, contributing to the team’s sustained success over the years. His ability to lead and manage the team’s operations was instrumental in the Guildford Flames’ dominance during his tenure.

Beyond his coaching and management achievements, Marple’s influence extended to the broader British hockey community. His long-term commitment to the sport in the UK, spanning over a decade, solidified his reputation as a respected figure in the game. His career trajectory—from player to coach to general manager—demonstrates his deep involvement and dedication to hockey at multiple levels.

In summary, Stan Marple’s career was marked by his significant contributions to the Guildford Flames and British ice hockey as a whole. His playing career, though limited by league rules, was followed by a highly successful coaching and managerial career, during which he led the Flames to multiple titles and left a lasting legacy. The retirement of his number 3 by the Guildford Flames serves as a testament to his impact on the team and the sport.

title: Robbie Horgan
text:
Robbie Horgan was born on 7 June 1968 in Dublin, Ireland, and had a long career as a professional footballer, specializing as a goalkeeper. He began his career with Shamrock Rovers, making his League of Ireland debut on 14 April 1987. Notably, he was the last goalkeeper to play for Shamrock Rovers at their historic Glenmalure Park (Milltown) ground, which occurred during a match that determined the League of Ireland B Division title in 1987.

In 1988, Horgan moved to Drogheda United, where he made his debut on 4 September in a 2–1 home victory over Bray Wanderers. During his time at Drogheda, he performed exceptionally well, recording 12 clean sheets in 26 league games as the team won the League of Ireland First Division title in 1989. His strong performances continued into the 1990/1991 season, where he kept 15 clean sheets, helping Drogheda secure another First Division title. After four and a half years at the club, Horgan left in November 1992 to join Shelbourne.

In July 1994, Horgan returned to Shamrock Rovers, where he remained for another eight years. During this period, he played in two European matches for the club in the 2002–03 UEFA Cup, facing Djurgårdens IF. His final League of Ireland appearance came in the last game of the 2007 season.

After retiring as a player, Horgan transitioned into coaching. He served as the goalkeeping coach for Sporting Fingal until the club disbanded. In August 2009, he made history by becoming the only player to have played at both Milltown (Shamrock Rovers' former ground) and Tallaght Stadium (the club's new home).

In February 2011, Horgan joined Drogheda United as an assistant coach under Mick Cooke. Under their leadership, Drogheda won the League of Ireland Cup in 2012. When Cooke left the club in November 2013, Horgan was appointed as his successor, taking over as manager.

Horgan’s career spanned multiple clubs and roles, from playing at the highest level in Irish football to coaching and managing. His contributions to Drogheda United, both as a player and later as a coach, were particularly significant, helping the club achieve success in both league and cup competitions. His legacy also includes being a key figure in the transition of Shamrock Rovers from Milltown to Tallaght Stadium, marking a unique connection between two eras of the club’s history.

title: Tanel Ingi
text:
Tanel Ingi is an Estonian actor born on November 26, 1976, in Tallinn. He began his formal artistic education in 1995 at the Kopli-Tallinn Art School, later attending the Viljandi Culture Academy, where he graduated in 1999. Even as a student, he started performing in stage roles, marking the beginning of his acting career. In 1998, he joined the Ugala theatre in Viljandi, where he has remained a prominent figure in the theatre's productions to this day. His stage work includes performances in a wide range of classical and contemporary plays, showcasing his versatility. He has acted in works by renowned playwrights and authors such as William Shakespeare, Anton Chekhov, Leo Tolstoy, Victor Hugo, and local Estonian writers like August Gailit and Oskar Luts. His roles span various genres, demonstrating his ability to adapt to different styles and characters.

In addition to his stage career, Tanel Ingi has had a notable presence in film and television. His film debut came in 1999 with the drama *Lurjus* (released internationally as *An Affair of Honour*), directed by Valentin Kuik, in which he shared the screen with actor Taavi Eelmaa. One of his most recognized performances was in the 2005 television film *August 1991*, directed by Ilmar Raag, where he played the role of Tõnu. This film dramatized the events surrounding the failed Soviet coup attempt during Estonia's fight for independence, known as the Singing Revolution. His television roles include appearances in the children's series *Nöbinina* on ETV, the TV3 series *Kättemaksukontor*, the crime series *Kelgukoerad* on Kanal 2, and the political satire *Riigimehed* on ETV. In 2015, he joined the cast of the Kanal 2 drama series *Pilvene all*, portraying the character Andres Kroon. Two years later, he took on the role of Aivar in the ETV drama series *Pank*, which chronicles the rise and fall of a new bank in Estonia during the 1990s. In 2020, he expanded his career by co-directing the comedy film *Asjad, millest me ei räägi* with Andrejs Ekis, further showcasing his creative versatility.

Tanel Ingi lives in Viljandi with his wife, Kätlin. The couple also owns a summer home in Koeru Parish, near the village of Preedi in Järva County. His career reflects a deep commitment to both stage and screen, with a body of work that highlights his contributions to Estonian theatre and film. His ability to balance classical and contemporary roles, as well as his forays into directing, underscore his multifaceted talent in the arts.

title: Vicky Kaushal
text:
Vicky Kaushal, born on 16 May 1988 in Mumbai, is an accomplished Indian actor known for his work in Hindi films. He is the recipient of prestigious awards, including a National Film Award and three Filmfare Awards, and has been featured in Forbes India's Celebrity 100 list. Kaushal comes from a Punjabi Hindu family with roots in Hoshiarpur, Punjab. His father, Sham Kaushal, is an action director in Indian films, and his younger brother, Sunny Kaushal, is also an actor. Despite his family's background in the film industry, Kaushal initially pursued a degree in electrical engineering from Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Technology, graduating in 2009. However, during an industrial visit to an IT company, he realized his passion for acting and decided to pursue a career in films.

Kaushal's early career began as an assistant director to Anurag Kashyap in the crime drama *Gangs of Wasseypur* (2012), whom he considers his mentor. He also played minor roles in Kashyap’s films *Luv Shuv Tey Chicken Khurana* (2012) and *Bombay Velvet* (2015), as well as the short film *Geek Out* (2013). His first leading role came in the independent drama *Masaan* (2015), directed by Neeraj Ghaywan. The film, which premiered at the Cannes Film Festival, earned critical acclaim for its realism, and Kaushal’s performance as a young man from a low socio-economic background was widely praised. He won several awards for his debut, including the IIFA and Screen Award for Best Male Debut. His next notable role was in *Raman Raghav 2.0* (2016), where he played a troubled police officer, showcasing his versatility by taking on a character vastly different from his own personality.

Kaushal gained widespread recognition in 2018 with supporting roles in the high-grossing films *Raazi* and *Sanju*. His portrayal of a fictionalized best friend in *Sanju* earned him the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor. The same year, he appeared in Netflix’s *Love per Square Foot* and *Lust Stories*, further expanding his range. His breakthrough as a leading actor came in 2019 with *Uri: The Surgical Strike*, where he played an army officer. The film was a commercial success, and his performance won him the National Film Award for Best Actor. Despite his growing fame, Kaushal has continued to take on diverse roles, including a biopic of freedom fighter Udham Singh in *Sardar Udham* (2021), which earned him the Filmfare Critics Award for Best Actor.

In recent years, Kaushal has balanced commercial and critically acclaimed projects. His romantic comedy *Zara Hatke Zara Bachke* (2023) was a surprise box-office success, while *Sam Bahadur* (2023), a biopic of India’s first field marshal, showcased his dedication to historical accuracy. In *Dunki* (2023), he received another Filmfare nomination and award for Best Supporting Actor. His 2024 comedy *Bad Newz* demonstrated his comic timing, and in 2025, he starred in *Chhaava*, his highest-grossing film to date, where he portrayed the Maratha ruler Sambhaji. The film’s success solidified his position as one of Bollywood’s leading actors.

Off-screen, Kaushal has been involved in brand endorsements and has hosted major award ceremonies. He has also been vocal about his personal life, which includes his marriage to actress Katrina Kaif in December 2021. Known for his dedication to his craft, Kaushal continues to challenge himself with diverse roles, from intense biopics to light-hearted comedies, making him one of the most respected actors in Indian cinema.

title: Klaudia Kaczorowska
text:
Klaudia Kaczorowska, born on 20 December 1988, is a Polish volleyball player who has represented both the Polish women's national volleyball team and the club PGE Atom Trefl Sopot. She is best known for her achievements in both domestic and international competitions, including a bronze medal at the 2009 European Championship. Over the course of her career, she has won multiple Polish Championship titles, becoming a champion in 2008, 2009, 2011, 2013, and 2014. Additionally, she has secured several Polish Cup victories, further solidifying her reputation as a top-tier player in Polish volleyball.

Kaczorowska began her professional career with PTPS Farmutil Piła, where she quickly established herself as a key player. In the 2007/2008 season, she contributed to the club's success in both the Polish Cup and the Polish Championship. The following season, 2008/2009, she helped the team win the Polish SuperCup and another Polish Championship title. Her consistent performances earned her recognition as the Best Server in the 2008 Polish Cup.

In 2010, she joined Bank BPS Muszynianka Fakro Muszyna, where she continued to excel. During the 2010/2011 season, she won the Polish Cup and the Polish Championship with the team, demonstrating her ability to adapt and thrive in different club environments. Her next significant move came in 2012 when she transferred to PGE Atom Trefl Sopot. This transfer proved to be highly successful, as she played a crucial role in the team's victories in the 2012/2013 and 2013/2014 Polish Championships. In the 2014/2015 season, she secured another Polish Cup title with the club, reinforcing her status as a dominant force in Polish volleyball.

Beyond domestic success, Kaczorowska has also made significant contributions to the Polish national team. She participated in the 2009 Universiade and the 2009 European Championship, where Poland won the bronze medal. Her international experience extended to the 2014 European League, where she continued to represent her country at a high level. Her versatility and skill have been recognized with individual accolades, including being named the Best Server in the 2015 Polish Cup and the Most Valuable Player in the same competition. These honors highlight her impact on the game and her ability to influence matches in critical moments.

Throughout her career, Kaczorowska has demonstrated exceptional consistency, leadership, and adaptability. Her ability to perform at the highest level in both club and national team settings has made her one of the most respected players in Polish volleyball. With multiple titles and individual awards to her name, she has left a lasting legacy in the sport, inspiring future generations of volleyball players in Poland.

title: John Counter
text:
John Counter, born on April 18, 1799, was a prominent Canadian businessman and political figure in Kingston, Ontario. He emigrated to Canada from Devonshire, England, with his parents in 1820, joining his older brother George and younger sister Susannah. His parents were John and Susannah Counter. Initially, he worked in the family business as a baker and confectioner, operating a bakery at the corner of Barrie and Clergy Streets. Over time, he expanded his ventures, securing major local contracts to supply bread and later diversifying into real estate, transportation, and industrial enterprises. His goal was to establish Kingston as a key transportation hub, and he invested heavily in the city’s commercial development.

Counter married Hannah Rhode at the age of 17, and they had four children. However, his personal life was marked by tragedy, as he lost his brother, two grandsons, his two sons, and his wife within a decade. He himself died in obscurity and poverty on October 29, 1862, at the home of his son-in-law. Despite his financial struggles later in life, he was once a wealthy and influential figure in Kingston.
