After earning his black belt, he transitioned to hapkido under Henry Perez, whose gym later became an MMA facility. Whittaker quickly became passionate about MMA, choosing it over rugby league, for which he had been scouted by the Cronulla Sharks. Known for his professionalism, he avoids trash-talking outside the octagon, emphasizing his role as an athlete who respects the sport.

Whittaker turned professional in 2009, debuting with Xtreme Fighting Championships and later competing in Cage Fighting Championships, where he compiled a 6-0 record. His first loss came in 2011 at Legend Fighting Championships against Hoon Kim. In 2012, he joined *The Ultimate Fighter: The Smashes*, an Australian vs. British competition, and won the welterweight tournament with two first-round knockouts, earning the Knockout of the Season bonus. He made his UFC debut at the show’s finale, defeating Brad Scott by unanimous decision.

Whittaker’s early UFC career was marked by a mix of wins and losses. He defeated Colton Smith by TKO and lost a split decision to Court McGee, followed by a first-round TKO loss to Stephen Thompson. However, he rebounded with a unanimous decision over Mike Rhodes in 2014. Moving up to middleweight in 2014, he earned his first *Fight of the Night* bonus for a TKO win over Clint Hester. His momentum continued with a first-round knockout of Brad Tavares, securing his first *Performance of the Night* award.

In 2017, Whittaker became interim middleweight champion by defeating Yoel Romero at UFC 213. After Georges St-Pierre vacated the title due to health issues, Whittaker was crowned undisputed champion. His first title defense was scheduled against Luke Rockhold, but Whittaker withdrew due to a severe staph infection and subsequent abdominal surgery. A rematch with Romero in 2018 ended in a controversial split decision, with Whittaker winning despite Romero missing weight. He later coached *The Ultimate Fighter* before suffering another setback—dual emergency surgeries that forced him to withdraw from a title fight against Kelvin Gastelum.

Whittaker lost his title to Israel Adesanya in 2019 via second-round knockout. After overcoming burnout in 2020, he returned with wins over Darren Till, Jared Cannonier, and Kelvin Gastelum, the latter earning him another *Fight of the Night* bonus. He faced Adesanya again in 2022 but lost a unanimous decision. Subsequent fights included a loss to Dricus du Plessis, a decision win over Paulo Costa, and a first-round KO of Ikram Aliskerov, earning his fourth *Performance of the Night* award. In 2024, he lost to Khamzat Chimaev via submission and later to Reinier de Ridder by split decision.

Outside MMA, Whittaker has excelled in freestyle wrestling, winning the 2015 Australia Cup and the 2017 Australian National Championship, qualifying for the 2018 Commonwealth Games before withdrawing to prioritize his UFC title defense. He has been recognized with numerous awards, including *Sherdog* and *World MMA Awards* Fighter of the Year in 2017, and *GQ Australia* Sportsman of the Year in 2018.

Whittaker is married with three sons and a daughter, and he also cares for his younger half-siblings. Born in New Zealand but raised in Australia, he embraces his Māori and Samoan heritage, often referencing it in his public persona.

With 14 UFC wins, including eight consecutive victories at one point, Whittaker is tied for the third most wins in UFC Middleweight history. His career has been defined by resilience, adaptability, and a dedication to both combat sports and personal growth.

title: Bob Marley
text:
Robert Nesta Marley, born on 6 February 1945 in Nine Mile, Saint Ann Parish, Jamaica, was a groundbreaking singer, songwriter, and guitarist who became one of the most influential figures in reggae music. His unique blend of reggae, ska, and rocksteady, along with his spiritual and socially conscious lyrics, made him a global icon. Marley’s music and Rastafarian beliefs elevated Jamaican culture worldwide, and he advocated for democratic reforms, cannabis legalization, and Pan-Africanism, often facing controversy for his outspoken stance.

Marley’s musical journey began in 1963 when he formed a group called the Teenagers with Peter Tosh and Bunny Wailer, which later became the Wailers. Their debut album, *The Wailing Wailers* (1965), featured the hit single "One Love," a reworked version of "People Get Ready." The Wailers released 11 more albums, eventually signing with Island Records and renaming themselves Bob Marley and the Wailers. Their sound evolved from ska to a more rhythmic, roots-based style, influenced by Marley’s conversion to Rastafari.

After signing with Island Records, the Wailers gained international fame with albums like *Catch a Fire* (1973) and *Burnin'* (1973). The latter included "I Shot the Sheriff," which Eric Clapton’s cover turned into a major hit, introducing Marley to a global audience. Their 1975 live album *Live!* featured the breakthrough hit "No Woman, No Cry," and *Rastaman Vibration* (1976) further cemented Marley’s success in the U.S.

Marley’s life took a dramatic turn on 3 December 1976, when he, his wife Rita, and manager Don Taylor were shot in an assassination attempt at his Jamaican home. Believed to be politically motivated, the attack occurred just before a peace concert. Despite his injuries, Marley performed as scheduled. Afterward, he moved to London, where he recorded *Exodus* (1977), a critically acclaimed album blending reggae, blues, and rock. Tragically, in 1977, Marley was diagnosed with acral lentiginous melanoma, a rare form of skin cancer. He continued performing but ultimately succumbed to the disease on 11 May 1981, shortly after his baptism into the Ethiopian Orthodox Church.

Marley’s death sparked worldwide mourning, and he was honored with a state funeral in Jamaica. His posthumous greatest hits album, *Legend* (1984), became the best-selling reggae album of all time, with estimated global sales exceeding 75 million records. He was posthumously awarded Jamaica’s Order of Merit, inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1994, and ranked among the greatest artists of all time by *Rolling Stone*. His enduring legacy as a musical pioneer, cultural ambassador, and symbol of resistance continues to inspire generations.

title: Sergei Bodrov
text:
Sergei Vladimirovich Bodrov, born on 28 June 1948 in Khabarovsk, Russian SFSR, Soviet Union, is a prominent Russian film director, screenwriter, and producer. His career has spanned several decades, marked by his ability to navigate both Soviet-era restrictions and post-Soviet creative freedom. Bodrov moved to the United States after the fall of the Soviet Union, where he currently resides between an apartment in Los Angeles and a ranch in Arizona. He is married to American film consultant Carolyn Cavallaro.

Bodrov’s early life was shaped by his family’s diverse ethnic background—his paternal grandmother was Buryat, his mother was Tatar, and his paternal grandfather was Russian. Raised by his grandparents, he initially pursued a career in space engineering, studying shuttle design, but was expelled in his third year due to a gambling addiction. After robbing his grandmother, he vowed to stop gambling and began working as an electrician at Mosfilm, the Soviet government film studio. There, he assisted in wiring films for Andrei Tarkovsky before transitioning into screenwriting for comedies. His directorial debut came in 1985 with *Sweet Juice of the Grass*, produced by Kazakhfilm Studios, which screened in competition at the 38th Locarno Film Festival.

During the Glasnost era, Bodrov became one of the first directors to gain more creative freedom, tackling previously banned topics. His second film, *The Non-Professionals* (1987), was initially banned in the USSR for its references to the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan. It was only shown after the Fifth Congress of the Filmmakers Association of the USSR in 1986, which, under Perestroika, began decentralizing filmmaking and allowing censored films to be released. The film, which follows young touring musicians in Kazakhstan, was rediscovered in government film censor archives in Kazakhstan and is noted for its exploration of generational disillusionment, drawing comparisons to 1960s New Wave cinema.

Bodrov’s 1989 film *Freedom Is Paradise* (also known as *S.E.R.—Svoboda eta rai*) further solidified his reputation. Set in Kazakhstan, it follows a 13-year-old boy’s journey to reach his father in a labor camp, blending actors and non-actors, including Volodia Kozerev, a real-life incarcerated youth whom Bodrov helped parole after filming. The film is notable for its humanist approach and the director’s skill in casting non-professionals.

His most internationally recognized work, *Prisoner of the Mountains* (1996), is an anti-war film set during the Russian-Chechen conflict. The story of two captured Russian soldiers emphasizes humanist themes over political messaging. Filmed near an active war zone in Dagestan, the production faced real dangers, including a standoff where a local guard threatened Bodrov at gunpoint over pay disputes. The film marked the acting debut of Bodrov’s son, Sergei Bodrov Jr., who tragically died in an avalanche in 2002 while filming *The Messenger*.

Bodrov’s later works include *Mongol* (2007), inspired by his Buryat heritage, and *Nomad* (2005), a sequel to *Mongol* exploring Genghis Khan’s early life. Both films earned him critical acclaim, including multiple Nika Awards and Academy Award nominations for Best Foreign Language Film. His filmography also includes *The Quickie* (2001), *Bear’s Kiss* (2002), and *A Yakuza’s Daughter Never Cries* (2010). As of 2008, he had directed 14 feature films, writing or co-writing all but two.

Throughout his career, Bodrov has received numerous accolades, including two Nika Awards for Best Picture and Best Director for *Prisoner of the Mountains* and *Mongol*, as well as nominations for the Academy Award and Golden Globe. In 2008, he was honored with the International Achievement Award in Filmmaking at ShoWest (now CinemaCon) for his contributions to cinema. His work continues to be celebrated for its humanistic storytelling and cultural depth.

title: Michael H. Schneider Sr.
text:
Michael H. Schneider Sr. was born in 1943 in San Antonio, Texas. He pursued his education at several institutions, beginning with an Associate of Arts degree from Lon Morris College in 1963. He then earned a Bachelor of Science degree from Stephen F. Austin State University in 1965, followed by a Juris Doctor from the University of Houston Law Center in 1970. Later in his career, he obtained a Master of Laws from the University of Virginia Law School in 2001.

Schneider’s legal career began in 1971 when he joined the Harris County, Texas District Attorney's Office as an assistant district attorney, a position he held until 1975. After leaving the District Attorney's Office, he briefly entered private practice in Texas from 1975 to 1976. He then worked as a general attorney for Dresser Industries from 1976 to 1980, during which time he also served as a part-time municipal judge for the City of West University Place, Texas, from 1978 to 1990. From 1980 to 1986, he served as a general attorney for Bawden Drilling, Inc., and from 1986 to 1989, he worked as a general solicitor for the Union Pacific Railroad Company. He returned to private practice from 1989 to 1990 before transitioning into a full-time judicial role.

Schneider’s judicial career began in 1990 when he became the presiding judge of the 157th District Court in Harris County, a position he held until 1996. In 1996, he was appointed as the chief justice of the First Court of Appeals of Texas in Houston, serving in that role until 2002. During this time, he also earned his Master of Laws degree. From 2002 to 2004, he served as a justice on the Supreme Court of Texas.

In 2004, Schneider was nominated by President George W. Bush to a seat on the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Texas, which had been vacated by Judge John H. Hannah Jr. The U.S. Senate confirmed his nomination on September 7, 2004, and he received his commission on September 10, 2004. He served on the federal bench until January 7, 2016, when he assumed senior status. Schneider retired from the bench on October 1, 2016.

Throughout his career, Schneider held various positions in both the public and private sectors, demonstrating a diverse legal background that included roles in prosecution, corporate law, and judicial service. His tenure on the federal bench marked the culmination of a long and distinguished career in the legal profession.

title: Jake Tilson
text:
Jake Tilson, born in 1958 in London, is a multifaceted artist, graphic designer, writer, and publisher. His work spans various mediums, including visual art, publishing, web design, and journalism. Tilson comes from a creative family background; his father, Joe Tilson, was an artist, and his grandfather, Alastair Morton, was a businessman who commissioned notable artists like Ben Nicholson and Barbara Hepworth. Tilson studied painting at Chelsea School of Art from 1976 to 1979, followed by the Royal College of Art from 1980 to 1983, where he won the Royal College of Art Major Travelling Scholarship. This allowed him to spend a year in Paris, where he held his first solo exhibition at Galerie J et J Donguy.

Tilson founded the independent press Woolley Dale Press in 1979, which enabled him to publish limited-edition bookworks and the arts/literary magazine *Cipher* (1979–1981), supported by a grant from the Greater London Arts Association. After completing his studies, he continued publishing, including the trilingual arts magazine *Atlas* (1985–1993), which was sold in 15 countries. In 1993, he renamed his press Atlas, under which he published audio works and books such as *3 Found Fonts* (2003). His artistic practice during the 1990s primarily involved collage-based wall pieces and sculptural dioramas, and he exhibited widely, represented by the Nigel Greenwood Gallery in London. Tilson was also an Erna Plachte artist-in-residence at Oxford University’s Ruskin School of Drawing and Fine Art (1994–1995), where he developed *TheCooker*, an early art website launched in 1994. He was an early adopter of the World Wide Web as an artistic medium, designing websites for institutions like the Royal Institute of International Affairs (1995) and the Royal College of Art (1996).

As a graphic designer, Tilson has worked with notable clients, including Paul Smith, Haworth Tompkins, the Royal National Theatre, and Warehouse plc. His most recent exhibition was at the Venice Architecture Biennale 2012, commissioned by Haworth Tompkins Architects for the *Common Ground* exhibition. Tilson is also a trustee of the Oxford Symposium on Food & Cookery, reflecting his interest in culinary themes, which is evident in his book *A Tale of 12 Kitchens* (2006).

Tilson’s contributions to art and design have been featured in several publications, including *No More Rules: Graphic Design and Postmodernism* (2013) and *The Fundamentals of Graphic Design* (2008). His works are held in public collections such as the Tate Gallery, Chase Manhattan Bank, and the BBC World Service. Additionally, he has produced a range of audioworks, including *City Picture Fiction* (1996) and *Foundsounds* (1993). His diverse career highlights his role as a pioneer in blending traditional and digital artistic practices.

title: Marcel Hernández
text:
Marcel Hernández Campanioni, born on 11 July 1989, is a Cuban professional footballer who plays as a centre-forward. He currently represents the Costa Rican club Herediano and the Cuba national team. Hernández has had a varied club career, beginning with a stint in the Dominican Republic. On 10 January 2017, he signed with Barcelona Atlético, which had recently won the Liga Dominicana de Fútbol. Before this, he had been linked with Cibao, another team in the same league, and had attempted to join Trepça'89 in Kosovo's Football Superleague. However, bureaucratic issues prevented his transfer to Trepça'89, despite his registration with the Football Federation of Kosovo. It was expected that he would eventually join the team during the summer transfer window, but this did not materialize.

Hernández has also represented Cuba at both the youth and senior international levels. His under-23 debut came on 25 June 2011, in a 2012 CONCACAF Men's Pre-Olympic Tournament qualification match against Aruba. He scored two goals in Cuba’s 7–0 victory, establishing himself in the national team setup. At the senior level, he made his debut on 10 November 2010, in a 2010 Caribbean Cup qualification match against Dominica, where he also scored, helping Cuba win 4–2. Over his international career, he participated in four FIFA World Cup qualification matches. However, on 6 November 2013, he announced his retirement from international football after being excluded from Cuba’s squad for the 2013 CONCACAF Gold Cup.

Despite his early retirement from international duty, Hernández has continued to achieve success at the club level. He played for Alajuelense, where he won the CONCACAF League in 2020. Additionally, he was part of the Cuba national team that won the Caribbean Cup in 2012. Individually, he was recognized as the top scorer in the Liga FPD during the Apertura 2020 season. His career has been marked by both highs and challenges, including unsuccessful transfers and early retirement from international football, but he has remained a notable figure in Central American and Caribbean football.

title: Zeca Pagodinho
text:
Zeca Pagodinho, whose real name is Jessé Gomes da Silva Filho, is a prominent Brazilian singer and songwriter known for his contributions to samba and pagode music. Born on February 4, 1959, in the Irajá neighborhood of Rio de Janeiro, he was immersed in the traditional samba culture from a young age. His early exposure to samba came through his involvement with the GRES Portela samba school, where he began writing his own verses as a child. In the 1970s, he became a regular at the Cacique de Ramos Carnival Block, a gathering that played a significant role in shaping the pagode genre.

Zeca Pagodinho's career took off when samba singer Beth Carvalho noticed his talent at one of these events and invited him to record the song "Camarão Que Dorme a Onda Leva" in 1983. This opportunity marked the beginning of his solo recording career, which has since produced 15 studio albums and three live DVDs. His music, characterized by its playful and sometimes mischievous lyrics, captures the essence of the relaxed, carefree lifestyle of the typical Rio de Janeiro resident, or "carioca." His work has been immensely popular in Brazil, making him one of the country's top-selling artists.

He lives in the upscale neighborhood of Barra da Tijuca with his wife, Mônica Silva, and their four children: Eduardo, Elisa, Louis, and Maria Eduarda. His family lineage includes notable figures, such as his grandfather Jessé Gomes da Silva and grandmother Milena da Silva, as well as his sister, Ircéia Pagodinho. His granddaughter is Catarina, and his grandson is Noah. His daughter-in-law is Thalita.

One of his most recognized songs, "Deixa a Vida Me Levar," was featured in the 2004 edition of the FIFA video game series. In 2015, his album *Ser Humano* was nominated for a Latin Grammy Award in the Best Samba/Pagode Album category, further cementing his status as a leading figure in Brazilian music.

Zeca Pagodinho's discography is extensive, spanning multiple albums released between 1986 and 2019. Some of his notable works include *Boêmio Feliz* (1989), *Jeito Moleque* (1988), *Alô, Mundo!* (1993), *À Vera* (2005), *Vida da Minha Vida* (2010), and *Mais Feliz* (2019). He has also released several live albums and MTV Unplugged sessions, such as *Acústico MTV – Zeca Pagodinho* (2003) and *Multishow Ao Vivo: 30 Anos - Vida Que Segue* (2013).

Throughout his career, Zeca Pagodinho has received numerous accolades, including multiple wins for Best Singer at the Troféu Imprensa awards in 2003, 2004, and 2005. In 2009, he won the Video Music Brasil (VMB) award for Best Samba and received three honors at the Prêmio da Música Brasileira, including Best Singer, Best Album, and Best Song. He also won the Best Singer award at the Prêmio BRA GA de música in 2008. His enduring popularity and influence in Brazilian music continue to make him a beloved and respected artist.

title: Maggie Cogan
text:
Maggie Cogan, a native of New Hyde Park in Nassau County, New York, was a trailblazing figure in New York City, becoming the first female carriage driver in Central Park while working for the Plaza Hotel. Her career began at age 19, and she gained some public attention in the late 1960s, appearing in a 1967 Universal newsreel and on the syndicated version of *What’s My Line?* in 1968, where contestants tried to guess her unusual occupation. She was also quoted in the *New York Times* in 1968 opposing the city’s proposal to equip horse-drawn carriages with meters, calling the idea "ridiculous." Cogan attended several colleges but never completed a degree, and while in high school, she was involved in cheerleading and dance clubs.

Her personal life, however, was marked by instability. She went through two failed marriages, the second of which resulted in two sons, whom she gave up for adoption when her life began to fall apart. She briefly left New York, moving to Texas for four years, but upon returning, she was unable to regain custody of her children. In the 1970s, her mental health deteriorated. She became infatuated with actor Robert Ryan and sent him strange gifts, including voodoo dolls with love notes. Around the same time, she developed an obsession with the serial killer David Berkowitz. She was also mugged in 1977, suffering a facial slash, and later disclosed in the documentary *Jupiter’s Wife* that she had been raped, though she provided no further details. Her condition worsened, and by the end of 1977, she was committed to a mental hospital by her parents after barricading herself in her bedroom for weeks.

After leaving the hospital, Cogan became homeless, living in Central Park for about 15 years. To cope, she invented elaborate stories about herself, claiming to be Robert Ryan’s daughter and possessing extrasensory perception. Despite her struggles, she maintained a charming and witty personality, forming friendships with people who helped her with food and clothing. She also adopted several dogs, whom she cared for deeply.

In 1989, filmmaker Michel Negroponte encountered Cogan while working on a documentary about his childhood in Central Park. Intrigued by her story, he shifted his focus and made *Jupiter’s Wife*, a film chronicling her life from 1989 to 1991. The documentary followed her as she moved through the park with her dogs, interacted with friends, and even attended a gymnastics class. The film concluded with the demolition of a small shack where she had been living, but by then, she had secured public assistance due to her mental health condition and moved into an apartment. *Jupiter’s Wife* won a special jury prize at the Sundance Film Festival.

However, Cogan’s stability was short-lived. In 1995, she was evicted from her Long Island City apartment and briefly stayed with Sara Whalen, the founder of Pets Alive shelter in Wallkill, New York. The arrangement lasted only five weeks before Cogan returned to Central Park, continuing her transient lifestyle. Her story is one of resilience and tragedy, marked by fleeting moments of recognition but ultimately overshadowed by mental illness and homelessness.

title: Irina Shayk
text:
Irina Shayk, born Irina Valeryevna Shaykhlislamova on 6 January 1986 in Yemanzhelinsk, Soviet Union (now Russia), is a prominent Russian fashion model. She gained international fame when she became the first Russian model to appear on the cover of the 2011 *Sports Illustrated* Swimsuit Issue. In 2022, she was recognized as one of the "New Supers" by Models.com, cementing her status in the modeling world.

Shayk was born to a Volga Tatar father, Valery Shaykhlislamov, a coal miner, and an ethnic Russian mother, Olga, a kindergarten music teacher. She has one sister, Tatiana Petenkova, and is an aunt to her niece, also named Irina. Shayk inherited her striking features from her father, whose dark complexion often led people to mistake her for being of South American descent, while her light eyes came from her mother. Her father passed away from pneumonia complications when she was 14, leaving the family in financial difficulty and forcing her mother to work two jobs. Shayk began playing the piano at age six and later attended a music school for seven years, where she played the piano and sang in the choir. After high school, she initially studied marketing before enrolling in a beauty school with her sister. There, she was discovered by a modeling scout and encouraged to enter the "Miss Chelyabinsk 2004" contest, which she won.

Shayk's modeling career began in 2007 when she replaced Ana Beatriz Barros as the face of Intimissimi and appeared in *Sports Illustrated* Swimsuit Issue. By 2010, she became an official ambassador for Intimissimi and worked with brands like Beach Bunny Swimwear, Guess, Victoria’s Secret, Lacoste, and Cesare Paciotti. She signed with IMG Models in 2009, further boosting her career. Her breakthrough came in 2011 when she landed the cover of *Sports Illustrated* Swimsuit Issue, becoming the first Russian model to do so. That year, she also appeared on multiple magazine covers, including *Elle Spain*, *GQ Mexico*, and *Cosmopolitan Spain*, and was named "Best International Model of 2010" by *Glamour Spain*. Controversy arose when *GQ Spain* published nude images of her, which she claimed were digitally altered, though the magazine maintained she had posed nude.

From 2011 to 2015, Shayk transitioned from swimwear to high fashion, appearing in *Harper’s Bazaar Spain*, *Vanity Fair Italy*, and *Vogue Spain*. She worked with luxury brands like Givenchy and walked in major fashion shows, including New York and Paris Fashion Weeks. In 2014, she carried the Russian flag at the Winter Olympics opening ceremony. In 2016, while pregnant, she walked in the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show. She also became a L'Oréal Paris spokesperson in 2015.

In addition to modeling, Shayk ventured into acting, debuting as Megara in the 2014 film *Hercules* alongside Dwayne Johnson. Her personal life has been widely publicized. She dated Portuguese footballer Cristiano Ronaldo from 2009 to 2015, and they were engaged in 2011. After their split, she began a relationship with American actor Bradley Cooper in 2015. They had a daughter, Lea de Seine Shayk Cooper, in 2017, but separated in 2019.

Shayk’s career has spanned over a decade, with her versatility allowing her to excel in both commercial and high-fashion modeling. Her recognition as one of the "New Supers" in 2022 highlights her enduring influence in the industry.

title: Ricky Martin
text:
Ricky Martin, born Enrique José Martín Morales on December 24, 1971, in San Juan, Puerto Rico, is a celebrated singer, songwriter, and actor known for his versatility across Latin pop, dance, reggaeton, salsa, and other genres. His musical journey began at age 12 when he joined the Puerto Rican boy band Menudo, a group known for replacing members as they aged out. Though initially rejected for being too short, Martin’s persistence earned him a spot, and he became a fan favorite. During his five years with Menudo, the band released 11 albums, including *Evolución* (1984) and *Menudo* (1985), which featured the group’s only U.S. *Billboard* Hot 100 entry, "Hold Me." Martin left the group in 1989 to pursue acting and solo music.

After briefly attending New York University, Martin moved to Mexico City to star in the telenovela *Alcanzar una estrella II* (1991) and its film adaptation, earning an El Heraldo Award. His first solo album, *Ricky Martin* (1991), debuted at No. 5 on the *Billboard* Latin Pop Albums chart, followed by *Me Amaras* (1993), which sold over a million copies. Despite early setbacks, including a car accident and a plane crash, Martin gained recognition in Latin America. His breakthrough came with *A Medio Vivir* (1995), featuring the global hit "María," which topped charts in 20 countries and sold over five million copies. The album’s success solidified his international fame, leading to a two-year A Medio Vivir Tour and a role in *Les Misérables* on Broadway.

His next album, *Vuelve* (1998), earned him his first Grammy Award and included the hit "La Copa de la Vida," which he performed at the 41st Grammy Awards. Transitioning to English, *Ricky Martin* (1999) became his first U.S. *Billboard* 200 No. 1, with the lead single "Livin’ la Vida Loca" topping the *Billboard* Hot 100 and UK Singles Chart. This period marked the peak of the "Latin explosion," with Martin credited for bringing Latin pop to mainstream success. Subsequent albums like *Almas del Silencio* (2003) and *MTV Unplugged* (2006) continued his streak of hits, including "She Bangs" and "Nobody Wants to Be Lonely."

As an actor, Martin starred in *General Hospital* (1994–1996) and earned an Emmy nomination for *The Assassination of Gianni Versace: American Crime Story* (2018). With over 70 million records sold, he holds 11 *Billboard* Hot Latin Songs No. 1s and numerous awards, including two Grammys, five Latin Grammys, and a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. Beyond music, Martin is a philanthropist, founding The Ricky Martin Foundation in 2004 to combat human trafficking and advocate for LGBT rights. His career reflects a blend of artistic innovation, cultural impact, and activism.

title: Dana Ashbrook
text:
Dana Vernon Ashbrook, born on May 24, 1967, in San Diego, California, is an American actor best known for his role as Bobby Briggs in the cult television series *Twin Peaks* (1990–1991) and its 1992 prequel film, *Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me*. His parents were D'Ann Paton, a teacher, and Vernon L. "Buddy" Ashbrook, who directed the drama department at Palomar College. Ashbrook has a brother, writer Taylor Ashbrook, and a sister, actress Daphne Ashbrook.

Ashbrook began his acting career in 1978 with an uncredited role in the comedy-horror film *Attack of the Killer Tomatoes!*. After a decade-long hiatus, he returned to acting in the late 1980s, appearing in guest roles on television shows such as *Cagney & Lacey*, *Knots Landing*, and *21 Jump Street*, as well as the *ABC Afterschool Special*. In 1988, he starred in the horror sequel *Return of the Living Dead Part II* and the cult horror film *Waxwork*, alongside Deborah Foreman. He was also set to star in the independent film *A Place to Hide*, which was later retitled *Night of the Warrior* (1990) but ultimately filmed without him due to delays.

In 1989, Ashbrook played Joey in the comedy *She's Out of Control*. The following year, he gained significant recognition for his role as Bobby Briggs, the rebellious son of the sheriff, in David Lynch’s surreal mystery series *Twin Peaks*. During this time, he also appeared in several other films, including *Sundown: The Vampire in Retreat* (1990), *Ghost Dad* (1990), *Girlfriend from Hell* (1990), and *The Willies* (1990). He also had a guest role in the television series *The Hidden Room*.

In 1992, Ashbrook reprised his *Twin Peaks* character in the film *Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me* and took on the role of Clyde Barrow in the television film *Bonnie & Clyde: The True Story*, alongside Tracey Needham. Over the next few years, he appeared in a variety of projects, including the short film *The Coriolis Effect* (1994), which also featured Jennifer Rubin and Quentin Tarantino, and the science fiction pilot *W.E.I.R.D. World* (1995). He starred in the drama *Comfortably Numb* (1995) and had guest roles in *The Outer Limits* (1996) and the short-lived series *Crisis Center* (1997). In 1998, he appeared in the film *Interstate 5* and the series *Welcome to Paradox*.

Throughout the 2000s, Ashbrook continued to work in television, appearing in episodes of *The Pretender* (2000), *Charmed* (2001), and *Law & Order: Special Victims Unit* (2007). From 2002 to 2003, he played the recurring role of Rich Rinaldi in *Dawson’s Creek*. In 2009, he joined the cast of *Crash* as Jimmy. In 2010, he reunited with some of the *Twin Peaks* cast in the *Psych* episode "Dual Spires," a comedic homage to the series. Later, he starred in the thriller *The Aggression Scale* (2012) and the horror film *Late Phases* (2014).

In 2017, Ashbrook returned to his most famous role, Bobby Briggs, in the revival series *Twin Peaks: The Return*, directed by David Lynch. His career has spanned over four decades, with a mix of television and film appearances, though his most enduring legacy remains his work in the *Twin Peaks* universe.

title: Cha Eun-woo
text:
Cha Eun-woo, born Lee Dong-min on March 30, 1997, in Gunpo, South Korea, is a celebrated singer and actor known for his work as a member of the boy band Astro and for his successful solo career. He graduated from Hanlim Multi Art School and later studied performing arts at Sungkyunkwan University. Cha's career began with a minor role in the 2014 film *My Brilliant Life*, which led to his selection as a model for the cosmetics brand Shara Shara. He officially debuted as part of Astro in 2016 with their EP *Spring Up*.

Throughout his career, Cha has gained recognition for his acting roles in popular dramas such as *Gangnam Beauty* (2018), where he played his first leading television role, earning him a spot in *GQ Korea*'s "Men of the Year." He further solidified his acting prowess in *Rookie Historian Goo Hae-ryung* (2019), winning the Excellence Award for an Actor and a Best Couple Award at the MBC Drama Awards. His role in *True Beauty* (2020–2021) alongside Moon Ga-young also garnered significant attention. In 2022, he starred in the drama *Island* and the film *Decibel*, showcasing his versatility in both television and cinema.

In 2023, Cha expanded his solo career with the release of the remake of "Jealousy" for the drama *A Good Day to Be a Dog* and received the Global Icon Award at the MTV Video Music Awards Japan. He debuted as a solo artist in 2024 with his EP *Entity*, featuring the lead single "Stay," and embarked on his first solo fan concert tour, *Just One 10 Minutes "Mystery Elevator,"* which included stops in multiple countries. His second solo concert, "THE ROYAL," is scheduled for July 2025 before his enlistment.

Cha has also been involved in numerous endorsements and brand collaborations, representing companies such as Tommy Hilfiger, Burberry, Dior, Calvin Klein, and The North Face. He has been a prominent face in the fashion and beauty industries, frequently appearing in global campaigns. In addition to his professional success, Cha is known for his philanthropic efforts, including donations to educational funds, disaster relief, and COVID-19 support. He has consistently contributed to causes such as the Junior Love Academic Support Fund and the ALS nursing hospital through initiatives like the Ice Bucket Challenge.

Cha's influence extends beyond South Korea, as he has become a global ambassador for brands like Skechers, Chaumet, and Saint Laurent. His dedication to philanthropy, combined with his artistic achievements, has cemented his status as a multifaceted entertainer with a strong international presence. As of 2025, he is set to lead a tribute song for his late Astro bandmate Moonbin and will star in the film *First Ride*, marking his debut as a leading actor in cinema.

title: Abdul Halik Hudu
text:
Abdul Halik Hudu, widely known by his nickname "Rooney," is a Ghanaian professional footballer born on 19 March 2000. He plays as a midfielder and most recently represented Al-Wehdat in the Jordanian Pro League. Hudu began his professional career with Inter Allies in the Ghana Premier League, having previously come through their feeder club, Accra Youth FC. In his debut season in 2016, he made 19 appearances and quickly became a key player, earning recognition as the "Most Promising Player of the Year" in the Ghanaian Premier League. He also received the "Fans' Player of the Season" award at Inter Allies. In early 2017, Hudu went on a two-month trial with Swedish club Hammarby IF, appearing in friendly matches before returning to Inter Allies. That year, he won the "Man of the Match" award in three league games and accumulated 37 competitive appearances across two seasons, scoring twice.

In January 2018, Hudu returned to Hammarby IF for a second trial and signed a permanent deal on 26 March, a week after his 18th birthday. The contract was a three-and-a-half-year agreement. He made his competitive debut for Hammarby on 23 August 2018, scoring in a 3–0 Svenska Cupen victory over Carlstad United. The following year, in 2019, he was loaned to IK Frej in Sweden's second division, Superettan, where he played 26 games and scored twice as the club was relegated. On 28 July 2020, Hudu was loaned to GIF Sundsvall for the rest of the season, and his contract with Hammarby was extended by another year. He won the 2020–21 Svenska Cupen with Hammarby, defeating BK Häcken 5–4 on penalties after a 0–0 draw in the final.

On 16 July 2021, Hudu moved to Danish club Lyngby, signing a two-year contract with the second-tier 1st Division team. He made his debut on 30 July as a late substitute in a 2–1 win over Jammerbugt. In March 2022, he transferred to AFC Eskilstuna in Sweden, signing a two-year deal. On 14 December 2023, he returned to GIF Sundsvall, this time on a permanent three-year contract. In January 2025, Hudu joined Al-Wehdat SC in the Jordanian Pro League.

Internationally, Hudu has represented Ghana at the under-17 level and captained the national team in an 8–0 victory over Namibia in March 2016. In 2018, he was called up to the Ghana under-20 team for an Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Algeria. His individual accolades include the "Most Promising Player of the Year" in the Ghanaian Premier League (2016) and the Svenska Cupen (2020–21) with Hammarby. As of 27 September 2021, his career statistics were recorded across these clubs, though further details are not provided in the article.

title: Ryan Brasier
text:
Ryan David Brasier, born on August 26, 1987, is an American professional baseball pitcher currently playing for the Chicago Cubs in Major League Baseball (MLB). Standing at 6 feet 0 inches and weighing 225 pounds, he is a right-handed pitcher and batter. Brasier has played for several MLB teams, including the Los Angeles Angels, Boston Red Sox, and Los Angeles Dodgers, as well as the Hiroshima Toyo Carp in Japan's Nippon Professional Baseball (NPB). He is a two-time World Series champion, winning with the Red Sox in 2018 and the Dodgers in 2024.

Brasier attended S. H. Rider High School in Wichita Falls, Texas, where he played as a catcher on the baseball team. After high school, he enrolled at Weatherford College in 2006 to play college baseball. The Los Angeles Angels selected him in the sixth round of the 2007 MLB draft. He spent his early career in the Angels' minor league system, advancing through various levels before reaching Triple-A with the Salt Lake Bees in 2012. That year, he made 55 relief appearances, recording 13 saves, a 7–3 record, 54 strikeouts, and a solid 2.77 ERA in 59+2⁄3 innings. The Angels promoted him to the majors in 2013, where he made his MLB debut on May 2, pitching an inning against the Baltimore Orioles. He allowed two runs in his first appearance but finished the season with a 2.00 ERA in seven games. After undergoing Tommy John surgery in 2014, he missed the entire season and was later removed from the Angels' 40-man roster in October 2014.

In July 2015, Brasier signed a minor league deal with the Oakland Athletics, spending the 2015 season rehabbing and making only six minor league appearances. In 2016, he pitched for the Triple-A Nashville Sounds, posting a 3.56 ERA in 46 relief appearances. In December 2016, he signed with the Hiroshima Toyo Carp in Japan, where he improved his pitching mechanics. Over 26 relief appearances, he recorded a 3.00 ERA in 30 innings, striking out 19 batters.

Brasier returned to the MLB in 2018 after signing a minor league contract with the Boston Red Sox. He began the season with Boston's Triple-A affiliate, the Pawtucket Red Sox, earning a spot in the Triple-A All-Star Game. The Red Sox promoted him to the majors in July 2018, where he quickly became a reliable reliever. He finished the season with a 1.60 ERA in 34 appearances and was part of Boston's World Series-winning team. In 2019, he recorded his first MLB save and appeared in 62 games, though his ERA rose to 4.85. The 2020 season was shortened due to COVID-19, and Brasier made 25 appearances, posting a 3.96 ERA. In 2021, he suffered a calf injury and later a head injury after being hit by a line drive during rehab. He returned in September, making 13 regular-season appearances and seven postseason appearances as the Red Sox reached the American League Championship Series. After a strong 2021, he signed a one-year, $1.4 million contract for 2022 but struggled, posting a 5.78 ERA in 68 appearances. In 2023, he began the year with a 7.29 ERA in 20 games before being designated for assignment and later released.

Brasier signed a minor league deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers in June 2023 and was quickly promoted to the majors. He excelled as a reliever, finishing the season with a 0.70 ERA in 39 appearances and contributing in the 2023 NLDS. The Dodgers re-signed him to a two-year, $9 million contract in 2024, but he dealt with injuries, including a calf strain, and ultimately posted a 3.54 ERA in 29 games. He helped the Dodgers win the 2024 World Series, appearing in multiple postseason games.

On January 30, 2025, the Dodgers designated Brasier for assignment, and just four days later, he was traded to the Chicago Cubs in exchange for a player to be named later or cash. Throughout his career, Brasier has been a versatile reliever, known for his ability to adapt and contribute to championship teams.

title: Worranit Thawornwong
text:
Worranit Thawornwong, commonly known by her nickname Mook, is a Thai actress and singer born on October 9, 1996, in Bangkok. She is the second child in her family, and her brother, Jirakit Thawornwong, is also an actor. Worranit completed her high school education at Satriwitthaya 2 School and later graduated from the Faculty of Humanities at Kasetsart University.

Worranit Thawornwong began her acting career in 2014 when she appeared in the drama *Rukjing Pinker* on Channel Bang, playing the character Bew. The following year, she starred in *Room Alone 401–410* as Snow. Her breakthrough came in 2015 with the popular Thai television series *Ugly Duckling Series: Perfect Match*, where she portrayed the character Junior and was paired with Puttichai Kasetsin. This role significantly boosted her popularity, and she also contributed to the drama by singing its theme song.

In 2016, she continued to gain recognition through her role in *Kiss The Series*, where she was paired with Sattaphong Phiangphor. That same year, she appeared in *U-Prince* alongside March Chutavuth Pattarakampol in the segment titled *Ambitious Boss*. The following year, 2017, she starred in *My Dear Loser* with Thanat Lowkhunsombat in the segment *Monster Romance*.

Her career continued to flourish in 2018 when she appeared in two prominent series: *Mint To Be* with Perawat Sangpotirat and *Love At First Hate* with Yuke Songpaisan. In 2019, she worked on *Mia Noi* alongside Krissada Pornweroj and *Plara Song Krueng* with Oil Thana Suttikamol. The following year, 2020, she starred in *Girl Next Room* with Pathompong Reonchaidee in the segment *Motorbike Baby* and *Ban Sao Sod* with Jirayu La-ongmanee.

In addition to acting, Worranit has ventured into singing, contributing to several drama soundtracks. Notable songs include *Mah Tun Welah Por Dee* and *Kon Jao Choo* (*Bee Dup Bee Doo*), which she performed for *Ugly Duckling: Perfect Match*, and *Poot Wah Ruk Nai Jai* for *Roon Pee Secret Love*. She also participated in *The Mask Singer Thailand*, showcasing her vocal talents.

One of her most recent notable roles was in the 2021 television series *Oh My Boss*, where she played the character Noomnim. In 2022, she announced that she would not renew her contract with GMMTV, marking a significant shift in her career.

Worranit Thawornwong has built a diverse and successful career in both acting and music, earning a strong fan base in Thailand and beyond. Her work spans multiple dramas, and her contributions to soundtracks have further solidified her presence in the entertainment industry.

title: Kathinka Pasveer
text:
Kathinka Pasveer, born on 11 June 1959 in Zaandam, The Netherlands, is a renowned Dutch flautist who has made significant contributions to contemporary classical music, particularly through her collaboration with the composer Karlheinz Stockhausen. The daughter of conductor Jan Pasveer, she studied at the Royal Conservatory of The Hague under Frans Vester, earning her performer's diploma in 1983 with the prestigious Nicolai Prize. During her final year of studies, she served as the principal flutist of the Gewestelijk Orkest Zuid-Holland.

Pasveer's career took a transformative turn when she met Stockhausen in 1982. He invited her to collaborate on *Zeitmaße*, *Amour*, and *In Freundschaft*, leading to the composition of *Kathinkas Gesang* (the second scene of *Samstag aus Licht*), which she premiered in 1983. This marked the beginning of a 25-year partnership, during which Stockhausen composed numerous works for her, many of which she premiered and which were dedicated to her. These works included parts in the operas *Montag aus Licht* (1988), *Dienstag aus Licht* (1993), and *Freitag aus Licht* (1996), as well as solo pieces like *Orchester-Finalisten* (1996), *Michaelion* (1998), and *Licht-Bilder* (2004). After the *Licht* cycle, Stockhausen wrote *Harmonien* (2006) and *Paradies* (2007) for her, both part of the *Klang* cycle.

Beyond performing, Pasveer also took on interpretive and technical roles in Stockhausen's works. She learned the solo dancer-mime part for *Inori*, which she performed in 1989 and continues to practice as a form of meditation. She also performs the *Vortrag über HU*, a lengthy lecture on *Inori*, from memory in both German and English. Additionally, she has contributed as a soprano singer in several of Stockhausen's works, including *Die sieben Lieder der Tage*, *Zwei Paare*, and *Urantia*.

Pasveer has been instrumental in preserving and promoting Stockhausen's legacy. Since 1998, she has taught the interpretation of his works at the annual Stockhausen Courses for New Music in Kürten. She also assisted Stockhausen in recording productions, learning his sound projection techniques, and later became a sound projectionist for live performances. Since his death in 2007, she has overseen the production and mixing of recordings for the *Stockhausen Complete Edition* and, alongside Antonio Pérez-Abellán, produced the sound loops for *Cosmic Pulses* (2006).

As a flautist, Pasveer has recorded extensively, particularly for the *Stockhausen Complete Edition*, which includes solo works, operas, and collaborations. Notable recordings feature her performances in *Kathinkas Gesang*, *In Freundschaft*, *Tierkreis*, and *Paradies*. She has also released recordings as a soprano, contributing to works like *Die sieben Lieder der Tage* and *Urantia*.

Pasveer's influence extends to film, with several recordings of her performances in Stockhausen's works, including *Kathinkas Gesang* (1985), *Inori* (1998), and *Michaelion* (2003). Her work has been documented in various articles, interviews, and reviews, highlighting her role as Stockhausen’s muse and a key figure in contemporary flute repertoire.

Together with Suzanne Stephens, Pasveer directs the Stockhausen Foundation for Music, ensuring the preservation and dissemination of Stockhausen’s musical and artistic vision. Her niece, harpist Marianne Smit, is also connected to the musical world, reflecting the family’s deep involvement in music. Pasveer’s contributions as a performer, educator, and custodian of Stockhausen’s legacy have cemented her status as a pivotal figure in 20th- and 21st-century music.

title: Carl Braun (obstetrician)
text:
Carl Braun, born on 22 March 1822 in Zistersdorf, Austria, was a prominent obstetrician whose career significantly influenced the development of obstetrics and gynecology in the 19th century. He was the son of a medical doctor, Carl August Braun, and pursued his own medical education in Vienna, beginning his studies in 1841. By 1847, he had secured a position as an assistant doctor (Sekundararzt) at the Vienna General Hospital. Two years later, in 1849, he succeeded Ignaz Semmelweis as an assistant to professor Johann Klein at the hospital's first maternity clinic, a role he held until 1853.

In 1853, Braun became a Privatdozent and was appointed as an ordinary professor of obstetrics in Trient, also serving as vice-director of the Tiroler Landes-Gebär- und Findelanstalt. His tenure there was brief, as he was called back to Vienna in November 1856 to succeed Johann Klein as professor of obstetrics. During his time in Vienna, Braun played a pivotal role in the establishment of gynecology as an independent medical field. In 1858, on his recommendation, the hospital's first gynecology clinic was created under his direction, solidifying his reputation as a pioneer in the specialization of obstetrics and gynecology.

Braun's academic and administrative achievements were substantial. Between 1867 and 1871, he served as dean of the medical faculty at the University of Vienna, and in the academic year 1868/69, he was appointed rector of the university. His contributions to the medical profession were formally recognized in 1872 when he was knighted, adopting the title *Ritter von Fernwald*. In 1877, he was further honored with the title *Hofrat*, a distinction reserved for highly eminent professors.

One of Braun's notable medical eponyms is the "Braun-Fernwald sign," a condition observed during pregnancy. This sign involves an asymmetrical enlargement and softening of the uterine fundus at the site of implantation, typically detected at 4–5 weeks of gestation. This observation contributed to the diagnostic understanding of early pregnancy.

Braun's views on puerperal fever, a major cause of maternal mortality at the time, were influenced by the prevailing medical opinions of his era. Unlike Ignaz Semmelweis, who argued that "cadaverous poisoning" (infection from autopsies) was the sole cause, Braun identified 30 separate causes of childbed fever. Despite this disagreement, Braun maintained relatively low mortality rates in the First Division of the Vienna General Hospital, comparable to those achieved by Semmelweis. Historical records from 1849 to 1853 suggest that Braun continued to enforce strict hand hygiene practices, which likely contributed to the sustained reduction in mortality rates.

Throughout his career, Braun authored several influential works. In 1855, he co-wrote *Klinik der Geburtshilfe und Gynäkologie* (Maternity and Gynecology Clinic) with Chiari and Spaeth. In 1857, he published *Lehrbuch der Geburtshilfe* (Textbook of Obstetrics), which covered obstetrics, puerperal processes, and surgical techniques. A second edition of his *Lehrbuch der gesammten Gynäkologie* (Textbook of Gynecology) was released in 1881. Additionally, he documented his surgical experiences in *Über 12 Fälle von Kaiserschnitt und Hysterectomie bei engem Becken* (On 12 Cases of Caesarean Section and Hysterectomy with Narrow Pelvis), highlighting his contributions to obstetric surgery.

Braun remained active in his field until his death on 28 March 1891. His legacy endures through his medical discoveries, administrative leadership, and the enduring impact of his educational works on the development of obstetrics and gynecology.

title: Shawn Ashmore
text:
Shawn Robert Ashmore, born on October 7, 1979, in Richmond, British Columbia, is a Canadian actor known for his work in film, television, and video games. He began his acting career at a young age, starting with television commercials alongside his identical twin brother, Aaron. His family moved frequently in his early years, settling in Brampton, Ontario, where he attended Turner Fenton Secondary School. Ashmore’s first acting role came when he was nine years old, appearing on the CTV series *Katts and Dog* (1990). He and his brother also appeared in the film *Married to It* (1991). At age 14, he earned a Gemini Award nomination for his role in the TV film *Guitarman* (1994), marking an early recognition of his talent.

Ashmore gained prominence in the late 1990s and early 2000s with roles in Nickelodeon’s *Animorphs* (1998–1999) and Disney Channel’s *In a Heartbeat* (2000–2001) and *Cadet Kelly* (2002). His breakthrough came with the *X-Men* film series (2000–2014), where he portrayed Bobby Drake / Iceman. The role earned him an MTV Movie Award for Breakthrough Male Performance in 2004. Beyond *X-Men*, Ashmore took on diverse roles, including Canadian hero Terry Fox in the biopic *Terry* (2005), for which he received a Gemini Award nomination. He also starred in horror films like *The Ruins* (2008) and *Frozen* (2010), showcasing his versatility.

On television, Ashmore played FBI agent Mike Weston in *The Following* (2013–2015) and has been a series regular as attorney Wesley Evers on *The Rookie* since 2018. He has also ventured into interactive media, providing voice and motion capture for video games such as *Quantum Break* (2016) and *The Dark Pictures Anthology: Man of Medan* (2019). In 2023, he reprised his video game work in *Alan Wake II* and *Sons of the Forest*.

Ashmore’s career has been marked by critical acclaim and awards. He won a Leo Award for *Legend of Earthsea* (2004) and has received multiple Gemini and Saturn Award nominations. His twin brother, Aaron, is also an actor, and the two occasionally collaborate, appearing together in *Fringe* (2010) after a 15-year hiatus from working together.

In his personal life, Ashmore married Dana Renee Wasdin in 2012, whom he met on the set of *Frozen*. They have a son, Oliver, born in 2017. Ashmore and his brother share matching "GMA" tattoos, honoring their step-grandfather, Gangu Jagtiani. He has also supported breast cancer awareness campaigns.

Ashmore’s upcoming projects include the supernatural-horror film *It Feeds* (2025) and the psychological thriller *The Huntsman*, set for release in 2025. His career has spanned nearly three decades, showcasing his ability to adapt across genres and mediums, from blockbuster films to independent projects and interactive entertainment.

title: Sila María Calderón
text:
Sila María Calderón Serra, born on September 23, 1942, in San Juan, Puerto Rico, is a prominent Puerto Rican politician, businesswoman, and philanthropist. She made history by becoming the first woman to be elected and serve as governor of Puerto Rico, holding the position from 2001 to 2005. Her political career was preceded by significant roles in both the public and private sectors, demonstrating her versatility and leadership.

Calderón’s early life was marked by a strong educational foundation. She attended the Colegio Sagrado Corazón de Las Madres in Santurce and later graduated with honors from Manhattanville College in New York with a Bachelor of Arts in Government in 1964. She furthered her education at the Graduate School of Public Administration at the University of Puerto Rico. Her maternal grandfather’s Spanish heritage later granted her Spanish citizenship in 2012.

Her professional career began in 1973 as an Executive Aide to the Labor Secretary, followed by a role as Special Aide for Economic Development under Governor Rafael Hernández Colón. After his defeat in the 1976 elections, she transitioned to the private sector, working at Citibank in San Juan, where she developed new consumer products that boosted the bank’s earnings. In 1978, she became president of Commonwealth Investment Company, a family-run real estate firm.

Calderón returned to public service in the 1980s, serving as Chief of Staff to Governor Hernández Colón from 1984 to 1988 and later as Puerto Rico’s 12th Secretary of State. During this time, she also held positions on various economic and governmental advisory boards. After resigning in 1989, she focused on her business ventures, serving on the boards of major corporations like BanPonce and Banco Popular, as well as engaging in philanthropic work.

In 1997, Calderón was elected Mayor of San Juan, becoming the first woman to be elected to the position. During her tenure, she implemented extensive urban redevelopment projects in areas like Old San Juan, Condado, and Río Piedras, alongside initiatives to empower disadvantaged communities through the Special Communities Program.

Her political ascent continued when she announced her candidacy for governor in 1999. Winning the primary, she led the Popular Democratic Party (PPD) to victory in the 2000 election, defeating opponents Carlos Pesquera and Rubén Berríos. As governor, she prioritized economic and social development, particularly for marginalized communities. She established the Puerto Rico Office for Socioeconomic and Community Development through Law 1 of 2001, allocating $1 billion for projects, though the program faced criticism for underdelivered outcomes.

Calderón’s governorship was also marked by a notable incident in 2004 when a man armed with a knife took a hostage in La Fortaleza, the governor’s mansion. She personally negotiated with the assailant, leading to his surrender. That same year, she announced she would not seek re-election, stepping down in 2005.

Post-governorship, Calderón became a partner in Inter-American Global Links, Inc., a consulting firm, and established a philanthropic foundation focused on poverty, women’s issues, and urban revitalization. She has received numerous honors, including the Order of Isabella the Catholic from Spain, the Golden Plate Award, and honorary degrees from institutions like Manhattanville College and Boston University. She also strengthened Puerto Rico’s ties with Latin American countries, earning high civilian honors from the Dominican Republic, Panama, and Costa Rica.

In her personal life, Calderón was married three times. Her first marriage, to engineer Francisco Xavier González Goenaga, ended in 1975. They had three children: Sila María, Francisco Xavier, and María Elena, all of whom pursued successful careers. Her second marriage, to entrepreneur Adolfo Krans, lasted from 1978 to 2001. She married her third husband, Ramón Cantero Frau, during her governorship in 2003, but they divorced in 2005.

Calderón’s legacy is defined by her groundbreaking political achievements, her commitment to public service, and her dedication to improving Puerto Rico’s social and economic landscape.

title: Shane Fontayne
text:
Shane Fontayne, born Michael Barakan on April 29, 1954, is an English rock guitarist with a career spanning several decades. He first gained prominence in the 1970s as part of the psychedelic band Byzantium, having previously been in their precursor group, Ora. Over the years, Fontayne has collaborated with a wide array of notable artists, showcasing his versatility and skill. In the 1980s, he worked with Steve Forbert on the 1980 album *Little Stevie Orbit*, Lone Justice on their 1986 album *Shelter*, and Maria McKee on her 1989 self-titled album. His career reached a significant milestone in the 1990s when he joined Bruce Springsteen’s "Other Band" for the 1992–1993 tour, filling the role of guitarist after Springsteen had disbanded the E Street Band in 1989.

Beyond his work with Springsteen, Fontayne has been a sought-after session and touring musician. In 1995, he served as the lead guitarist for French rock legend Johnny Hallyday during the "Lorada tour" and a 1996 concert in Las Vegas. He has also worked with prominent artists such as Ian Hunter, Van Zant, John Waite, Chris Botti, Joe Cocker, Randy VanWarmer, and Graham Nash. Notably, he has been Marc Cohn’s touring guitarist since 1998, a partnership that has endured for many years. In recent years, he collaborated with Crosby, Stills & Nash and Graham Nash on tour, and produced Nash’s 2016 solo album *This Path Tonight*.

Fontayne’s contributions extend beyond studio and live performances. On December 2, 2012, he played lead electric guitar for Ann and Nancy Wilson’s rendition of "Stairway to Heaven" at the Kennedy Center Honors, honoring the remaining members of Led Zeppelin. The performance also featured Jason Bonham on drums, paying tribute to his late father, John Bonham.

In addition to his musical career, Fontayne has a notable personal life. He was married to actress Mackenzie Phillips from 1986 to 2000, and the couple has a son, Shane, born in 1987. His brother, Peter, is a music critic based in Japan.

Fontayne has also released his own music, including the 1991 album *Merchants of Venus*, the 2003 album *What Nature Intended*, and the 2006 album *Voodoo at the Mint*. These releases highlight his abilities as both a performer and a songwriter. His work has been documented on platforms like AllMusic, Discogs, and the NAMM Oral History Library, where he participated in an interview in 2017.

Throughout his career, Shane Fontayne has demonstrated a remarkable ability to adapt to different musical styles and collaborate with some of the most influential artists in rock and pop. His contributions as a guitarist, producer, and performer have solidified his reputation as a respected figure in the music industry.

title: Lodewicus du Plessis
text:
Lodewicus Johannes du Plessis (1897–1968) was a South African academic, political philosopher, and Calvinist who made significant contributions to education, theology, and Afrikaner politics. Born on 10 February 1897 in Burgersdorp, Cape Colony, he was the son of Jacobus Albertus du Plessis and Laurika Postma. He married Engela Susanna van der Merwe on 12 January 1926 and spent much of his later life in Potchefstroom, where he died on 19 February 1968.

Du Plessis received his early education at Potchefstroom Gimnasium, matriculating in 1912. He pursued higher education at the University of Pretoria, where he earned a BA, an Honours degree in Classical languages, and an MA in the same field. Later, he expanded his academic pursuits by obtaining a master's degree in Economics and an LL.B. in law. His diverse academic background laid the foundation for his multifaceted career.

His professional journey began in 1918 when he was appointed as a senior lecturer in Classical languages at the Theological Seminar of the Reformed Church (Gereformeerde Kerke in Suid-Afrika) in Potchefstroom. After completing his additional qualifications in economics and law, he was offered a professorship at the Potchefstroom University for Christian Higher Education (now North-West University), where he taught economics, political science, and ethics, eventually focusing on law. Beyond academia, he played a key role in the translation of the Bible into Afrikaans, serving as the secretary of the commission responsible for this project. He was also an advisor to Totius, a prominent Afrikaner theologian and poet.

Du Plessis was an alternative Calvinist, meaning he believed that while Calvinism was significant, it was not the sole answer to philosophical and theological questions. He was open to integrating elements of Calvinism with other belief systems, including Marxism, reflecting his intellectual flexibility and willingness to engage with diverse ideologies.

In politics, du Plessis was an active participant in Afrikaner nationalism, though he never held public office. He served as chairman of the Afrikaner Broederbond, a secretive Afrikaner political organization, from 1930 to 1932. Despite his influential role, he was known for his independent thinking and was unafraid to challenge leading figures such as J.B.M. Hertzog, D.F. Malan, and J.G. Strijdom. His most significant political conflict arose with H.F. Verwoerd, the architect of apartheid, over Verwoerd’s rigid racial policies and narrow definition of Afrikaner identity. This disagreement led to his expulsion from the National Party and his subsequent departure from the Afrikaner Broederbond. Du Plessis opposed Verwoerd’s policies, which he viewed as excessive and exclusionary, marking a turning point in his political career.

Throughout his life, du Plessis remained a figure of intellectual rigor and moral conviction, contributing to both academia and Afrikaner politics while maintaining a critical stance on the direction of South African governance. His work in education, theology, and political thought left a lasting impact, though his dissenting views on apartheid-era policies set him apart from many of his contemporaries.

title: Francisco Urroz (footballer)
text:
Francisco Urroz Martínez was a Chilean footballer born on 14 December 1920 in Higuerote, Venezuela. He began his football career at a young age, joining Unión Deportiva Española in 1931 alongside his brothers Guillermo and Gilberto. Their entry into the club was facilitated by their uncle, Simón Martínez, who was a prominent football leader. By 1940, Urroz had become a key member of the first team, eventually rising to the position of team captain. In 1943, he led his team to their first-ever league title, the Primera División de Chile, marking a significant milestone in the club's history.

After his successful tenure at Unión Deportiva Española, Urroz moved to Colo-Colo, where he continued to excel. In 1947, he helped Colo-Colo secure another Primera División de Chile title, further cementing his reputation as a talented defender. His club career was distinguished by his leadership and contributions to two of Chile's most prominent football teams.

On the international stage, Urroz represented the Chile national team, earning 11 caps. One of his most notable international appearances was in the 1950 FIFA World Cup, where he contributed to Chile's campaign. His defensive skills and experience played a crucial role in the team's performances during this period.

Off the field, Urroz's life was marked by personal achievements and family connections. His father, Francisco Urroz Sr., was a fruits and vegetables seller, but passed away when Francisco Jr. was only 13 years old. Despite this early setback, Urroz continued to pursue his passion for football. His family legacy extended beyond football as well. He was the father of Silvana Urroz, a tennis player, and the grandfather of Manuela Urroz, a field hockey player who also played youth football for Unión Española, and Francisco Urroz, a rugby union player and doctor.

Urroz passed away on 22 January 1992 in Concón, Chile, at the age of 71. His contributions to Chilean football were recognized through his achievements with Unión Deportiva Española and Colo-Colo, as well as his participation in the 1950 World Cup. His career spanned over a decade, during which he demonstrated leadership, skill, and dedication to the sport. The legacy he left behind, both in football and through his family, continues to be remembered in Chile.

title: Pratibha Patil
text:
Pratibha Devisingh Patil, born on 19 December 1934 in the village of Nadgaon in Maharashtra, is a prominent Indian politician and lawyer who made history as India’s first female president, serving from 2007 to 2012. She belongs to a Marathi family and was the daughter of Narayan Rao Patil. Patil received her education from local institutions, earning a master's degree in Political Science and Economics from Mooljee Jetha College and a law degree from Government Law College, Bombay. After completing her studies, she practiced law at the Jalgaon District Court while actively engaging in social causes, particularly those related to women's welfare. She married Devisingh Ramsingh Shekhawat in 1965, and the couple had two children, a daughter named Jyoti Rathore and a son, Raosaheb Shekhawat, who is also a politician.

Patil began her political career in 1962 at the age of 27 when she was elected to the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly from the Jalgaon constituency. She went on to win four consecutive elections in the Muktainagar constituency between 1967 and 1985. From 1985 to 1990, she served as a Member of Parliament in the Rajya Sabha and later represented the Amravati constituency in the Lok Sabha from 1991 to 1996. During her political career, she held various cabinet positions in the Maharashtra government and also served as the president of the Maharashtra Pradesh Congress Committee. Additionally, she held roles in cooperative organizations, including as Director of the National Federation of Urban Co-operative Banks and Credit Societies and as a Member of the Governing Council of the National Co-operative Union of India. In 2004, she was appointed Governor of Rajasthan, the first woman to hold that position.

In 2007, Patil was selected as the United Progressive Alliance’s (UPA) candidate for the presidency, a decision influenced by her long-standing loyalty to the Indian National Congress (INC) and the Nehru-Gandhi family. Her nomination was met with controversy, particularly due to allegations that she shielded her brother, G. N. Patil, in a 2005 murder case involving a political rival. Despite these accusations, she won the presidential election on 19 July 2007, defeating Bhairon Singh Shekhawat, the incumbent vice president and a BJP-supported candidate. Her victory marked a significant moment in Indian politics, as she became the first woman to hold the office of President of India.

Patil’s presidency was marked by controversies, including her decision to commute the death sentences of 35 petitioners to life imprisonment, a record number for a president. She also faced criticism for her extensive foreign travels, which were more frequent and costly than those of her predecessors. By May 2012, she had completed 12 foreign trips to 22 countries, accompanied by family members, at a cost of Rs 205 crore. After her term ended in 2012, she faced further controversy over the construction of a retirement mansion on military land in Pune using public funds, a move unprecedented for a retiring president. She also attempted to claim both an official government car and a fuel allowance for a private vehicle, violating established rules.

Before becoming president, Patil was involved in various business and social initiatives. She founded Vidya Bharati Shikshan Prasarak Mandal, an educational institution with schools and colleges in several cities, and the Shram Sadhana Trust, which operates hostels for working women. She also co-founded a cooperative sugar factory in Muktainagar. However, her involvement in the Pratibha Mahila Sahakari Bank, which was liquidated in 2003 due to financial mismanagement, raised ethical concerns. The bank had granted illegal loans to her relatives, including one to her sugar mill that was never repaid. Despite the Indian National Congress claiming she had no involvement since 1994, official documents showed her continued engagement as late as 2002.

Throughout her career, Patil held numerous official positions, including roles in the Maharashtra government, the Rajya Sabha, and the Lok Sabha. Her presidency remains a subject of debate, with some praising her historic achievement while others critique her tenure for its controversies and lackluster performance. In 2018, she received the Order of the Aztec Eagle, a high honor from Mexico, recognizing her contributions. Despite the mixed legacy of her presidency, Patil’s role as India’s first female president remains a significant milestone in the country’s political history.

title: Ana Cláudia Bolzan
text:
Ana Cláudia Bolzan e Silva is a Brazilian handball player born on 15 July 1996. She currently plays for the professional team Sport Lisboa e Benfica and represents the Brazilian national team. Bolzan has achieved notable success in her career, including winning the Pan American Women's Club Handball Championship in 2017, a significant regional title. Additionally, in 2022, she secured victory in the South and Central American Women's Club Handball Championship, further solidifying her reputation as a top-tier player in the sport.

Bolzan's individual skills have also been recognized, as she was selected to the All-Star Team as a left wing player during the 2022 South and Central American Women's Club Handball Championship. This distinction highlights her exceptional performance and contributions to her team's success in that competition. Her ability to excel in both team and individual contexts demonstrates her versatility and impact on the game.

Beyond her club achievements, Bolzan is a key member of the Brazilian national handball team, competing at the highest international level. Her experience and talent make her an important asset to the team, particularly in major tournaments and championships. Her presence in the sport has been marked by consistent high performance, earning her respect among peers and fans alike.

Bolzan's career includes participation in prestigious events such as the Paris 2024 Summer Olympics, where she will represent Brazil. This upcoming competition underscores her continued relevance and the high expectations placed on her as a national athlete. Her online presence, including an Instagram account, suggests an active engagement with fans and the handball community, further reinforcing her role as a prominent figure in the sport.

Her success in both club and national team settings reflects a well-rounded career, balancing individual accolades with team victories. Bolzan's journey in handball exemplifies dedication, skill, and the ability to perform under pressure, making her a standout athlete in the sport. Her involvement in major championships and recognition as an All-Star player underscore her influence and the significant contributions she has made to Brazilian handball. As she continues to compete at the highest levels, including upcoming Olympic appearances, Bolzan remains a key figure in the sport, inspiring future generations of handball players.

title: Cleopatra
text:
Cleopatra VII, the last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt, reigned from 51 to 30 BC. Born in Alexandria around 69 BC, she was the daughter of Ptolemy XII Auletes and a member of the Hellenistic Greek dynasty founded by Ptolemy I, a general of Alexander the Great. Unlike her predecessors, Cleopatra learned the Egyptian language in addition to Koine Greek, Latin, and several other languages, reflecting her ambition to reclaim territories lost by the Ptolemaic Kingdom.

Cleopatra co-ruled with her younger brother Ptolemy XIII, but their relationship deteriorated, leading to a civil war. In 48 BC, the Roman general Pompey, defeated by Julius Caesar in the Battle of Pharsalus, fled to Egypt. Ptolemy XIII, seeking Roman favor, had Pompey assassinated, but Caesar arrived soon after and occupied Alexandria. Caesar mediated between the siblings, but Ptolemy XIII’s forces besieged the palace, prompting Caesar to intervene militarily. Ptolemy XIII died in the ensuing Battle of the Nile, and Caesar declared Cleopatra and her new co-ruler, Ptolemy XIV, as joint rulers. Cleopatra and Caesar became lovers, and she gave birth to their son, Caesarion. She later traveled to Rome, where she lived at Caesar’s villa. After Caesar’s assassination in 44 BC and the mysterious death of Ptolemy XIV, Cleopatra named Caesarion her co-ruler.

During the Roman civil wars, Cleopatra allied with Mark Antony, one of Caesar’s successors, after their meeting in 41 BC. Their relationship produced three children, and Antony granted territories to their children in the Donations of Alexandria (34 BC). However, Octavian (later Augustus), Caesar’s heir, used this as an excuse to declare war on Cleopatra, portraying her as a threat to Rome. After Antony’s defeat at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC, Octavian invaded Egypt. With her defeat imminent, Cleopatra and Antony committed suicide in 30 BC. According to tradition, she chose poisoning over capture. Egypt was then annexed as a Roman province, ending the Hellenistic period.

Cleopatra’s legacy was shaped by Roman propaganda, which depicted her as a seductive and treacherous foreign queen. However, she was also admired for her intelligence, linguistic skills, and political acumen. Ancient and Renaissance art, literature, and modern media have immortalized her as a symbol of power and intrigue.

title: Ameyaw Debrah
text:
Ameyaw Kissi Debrah, professionally known as Ameyaw Debrah, is a prominent Ghanaian celebrity blogger, freelance journalist, and reporter. He is best known for founding AmeyawDebrah.com, an entertainment website that covers news about Ghanaian celebrities. Debrah graduated from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) with a bachelor’s degree in publishing, where he earned the Best Publishing Student award in 2005. His early education took place at Adisadel College in Cape Coast, where he served as the editor of the school’s magazine in 1999. After completing his degree, he fulfilled his National Service Secretariat (NSS) program at Ovation International Magazine in Accra, where he wrote about the Ghanaian entertainment industry for an international audience.

Debrah’s career began with a stint at Ovation International, followed by freelance contributions to various media outlets. In 2007, he became a columnist for the Star newspaper and contributed to pan-African websites such as Jamati.com, Orijin-ent.com, and ModernGhana.com. Later that year, he joined Voices of Africa, a Dutch media project, where he provided Africanews.com with videos, photos, and news from Ghana. In 2008, he became the entertainment editor at GhanaWeb.com and launched his own blog, AmeyawDebrah.com, the same year. He left GhanaWeb in 2012 to focus full-time on his blog, which has since gained a global readership. The website expanded in 2010 with the launch of an iPhone app developed by MobBase, and in 2012, Debrah introduced a talent hunt competition to discover new Ghanaian musical talents. He also initiated the My Ghana Campaign, a platform encouraging readers to share one-minute videos discussing Ghanaian issues.

In 2014, Debrah joined Ringier Ghana to launch and manage Pulse Ghana, leaving in 2015 to work with Genesis Technology. From September 2015 to September 2017, he served as the editor-in-chief of Yen.com.gh. Additionally, he has managed the careers of Ghanaian artists, including music producer Coptic, whom he helped introduce to the African market through *The Black Star Line Mixtape, Vol 1* (2011). He also managed rapper Pappy Kojo in 2014. Beyond music, Debrah has contributed to entertainment segments on Africa Magic, EbonyLife TV, and Glitz Africa Magazine, and served as an ambassador for Malta Guinness’ Africa Rising Campaign.

In 2018, Debrah expanded his digital media presence by launching Ameyaw TV, a web portal featuring shows like *Daily Buzz*, *News in One*, and *Trend Mill*, with plans for more content in 2019.
