She followed this up with back-to-back unanimous decision wins over Jennifer Maia and Norma Rueda Center, solidifying her reputation as a rising talent.

In 2017, Bennett was selected to compete on *The Ultimate Fighter 26*, a competition to determine the UFC’s first women’s 125-pound champion. She was picked seventh by coach Eddie Alvarez and advanced to the quarterfinals by defeating Karine Gevorgyan via first-round TKO. However, she lost her quarterfinal match to Sijara Eubanks by first-round knockout. Later that year, she faced Melinda Fábián at *The Ultimate Fighter 26 Finale*, where the fight ended in a majority draw. Following this result, she was released from the UFC.

Bennett returned to Invicta FC in 2018, winning a split decision against Karina Rodríguez. She then participated in a flyweight tournament, defeating Miranda Maverick by unanimous decision but losing in the final to Rodríguez in a rematch. In 2020, she began competing in Bellator, making her debut against Liz Carmouche, whom she lost to by rear-naked choke submission in the third round.

Throughout her Bellator career, Bennett had a string of notable performances. She defeated Alejandra Lara in a catchweight bout after missing weight, winning by unanimous decision. She then faced and defeated Justine Kish twice in 2022, both times by unanimous decision. In 2023, she challenged Carmouche again for the Bellator Women’s Flyweight World Championship but lost by submission in the fourth round after missing weight once more.

Beyond MMA, Bennett also ventured into professional grappling, competing at Fury Pro Grappling 7 in 2023, where she lost to Marissa Pacelli by unanimous decision. As of the information available, Bennett’s MMA record stands at 11 wins and 7 losses, with 2 no contests in exhibition fights. Her career has been marked by resilience and competitive performances across multiple promotions.

title: Lou Briel
text:
Lou Briel, born in October 19 in Santurce, Puerto Rico, is a multifaceted artist known for his work as a singer, composer, comedian, record producer, pianist, and television host. His career began at a young age as a member of the pop music group Anexo 3, which recorded four albums and gained popularity with songs like "Oh, Cuanto te Amo," "Contigo," and "Por eso estoy Preso." The group won second place in the local OTI Festival for two consecutive years with the songs "Tengo Vida" and "Más Allá de mis Canciones," both co-written by Briel and his partner Julio Ortiz-Teissonniere. Anexo 3 also produced and hosted a television variety show, *Contigo... Anexo 3*, on Rikavisión, and appeared in a popular Datsun commercial, where Briel sang a jingle about the car.

After Anexo 3 disbanded, Briel launched a solo career, achieving success in 1984 with the inspirational song "Yo puedo," written for Puerto Rican singer Yolandita Monge. He toured extensively across Latin America, including Mexico, Colombia, Peru, and the Dominican Republic, and performed in the United States. The song "Yo puedo" also placed highly in Colombia's Festi-Buga festival. Briel has represented Puerto Rico four times at the International OTI Festival as a composer: in 1983 with "Navegaré" (sung by Edgardo Huertas), in 1984 with "Todo llega" (performed by himself), in 1985 with "Represento" (sung by Juan Manuel Lebrón), and in 1990 with "La Mujer que Sueño Ser" (performed by his niece Ivonne Briel, known as "Arana"). His compositions have been recorded by renowned artists such as Yolandita Monge, Gilberto Santa Rosa, José Feliciano, and Tony Vega, among others.

Beyond his musical work, Briel has composed songs for television programs and telenovelas, including the theme for *De Fiesta con Nydia* and *Estudio Alegre* on Telemundo, as well as *Ave de Paso* (performed by Yolandita Monge) for Tele-Once. His acting career includes hosting and starring in the musical-comedy show *En Broma y en Serio* alongside Dagmar, producing the children's series *Teatrimundo* (where he played the character "Lubrielito"), and appearing in the sitcom *Cara o Cruz* with Edgardo Huertas. From 1995 to 2001, he hosted *Voces en Función*, a variety show featuring guest stars and emerging talent, broadcast by WIPR-TV.

Briel has also performed in theater, starring in zarzuelas and operettas such as *La Viuda Alegre* and *El Conde de Luxemburgo*, as well as children's musicals like *Jack y la Mata de Guisantes* and *Los Pitufos*. In recent years, he reprised his "Lubrielito" role in the family film *Yo Creo en Santa Claus* (2004) and directed the inspirational video *Dios Alumbra a Puerto Rico* (2005), featuring Latin pop and gospel artists advocating against child abuse. He has continued performing in live shows, including *Solo para Hombres.. y para Mujeres tambien* and the Puerto Rican Folkloric Revue, while also participating in the *La Receta de la Abuela* tour.

Briel's discography includes albums like *Solo Por Fin* (1981), *Yo Puedo* (1984), and *En Otra Frecuencia* (1991), among others. His work has solidified his reputation as a versatile and influential figure in Puerto Rican entertainment, spanning music, television, theater, and film.

title: Jennifer Paz
text:
Jennifer Paz-Fedorov is a Filipino actress best recognized for her recurring role as Lapis Lazuli in the animated series *Steven Universe* and its sequel, *Steven Universe Future*. Born and raised in the Philippines, she moved to Seattle, Washington, with her family at the age of five, where her uncle resided. She is the youngest of four children. After completing her freshman year at the University of Washington, Paz began her professional acting career at the age of 21, originating the alternate lead role of Kim in the first U.S. National Tour of *Miss Saigon*, a musical based on the Vietnam War. Her performance earned her critical acclaim and multiple award nominations, including a 2008 LA Stage Alliance Ovation Award for Best Lead Actress. She later reprised the role of Kim in various regional productions, demonstrating her dedication to the character.

Beyond *Miss Saigon*, Paz expanded her theatrical career by performing in *Les Misérables* on Broadway and taking on the role of Mei-Li in the pre-Broadway run of *Flower Drum Song* at the Los Angeles Mark Taper Forum. The production was extended for an additional five weeks due to its popularity. In 2013, she returned to the role of Kim in a production of *Miss Saigon* at the Casa Mañana theatre, further solidifying her reputation as a versatile stage actress. In addition to her live performances, Paz has contributed her voice to animation, notably as Lapis Lazuli and part of Malachite in *Steven Universe*, a role that gained her widespread recognition among fans of the series. Her vocal work also includes appearances in the *Steven Universe* soundtracks, where she performed songs such as "That Distant Shore" and "Happily Ever After" in *Steven Universe the Movie*.

Paz has also ventured into writing, earning the 2022/23 NAMT Writers Residency Grant and winning the Outstanding Screenplays TV Pilot Competition 2021 for her original comedy series, *Proud Marys*. Aside from her professional achievements, Paz’s personal life includes her marriage to actor Anthony Fedorov, whom she became engaged to on Christmas Day 2012. Their son, Julian Paz Fedorov, was born on April 1, 2013. Her discography includes contributions to Disney’s *The Lost Chords* albums, featuring tracks from *Cinderella* and *The Rescuers*, as well as original music from *Steven Universe* and *Steven Universe Future*.

Throughout her career, Paz has demonstrated versatility as an actress, singer, and writer, transitioning seamlessly between stage, voice acting, and screenwriting. Her work in *Miss Saigon* and *Steven Universe* has earned her both critical acclaim and a dedicated fanbase, while her recent writing accolades highlight her creative range beyond performance. Her personal life reflects her commitment to family, balancing professional success with her role as a mother and wife.
